questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
During a professional baseball game, a pitcher was continuously heckled by some spectators seated behind a wire mesh fence in the stands above the dugout. On several occasions, the pitcher turned and looked directly at the hecklers with a scowl on his face, but the heckling continued. The pitcher then wound up as though he was preparing to pitch in the direction of his catcher but threw a fastball toward the hecklers instead. The ball passed through the wire mesh fence and struck a woman who was one of the hecklers.
The woman brought an action against the pitcher and the team to recover damages for battery. The trial court entered judgment as a matter of law in favor of the defendants on the battery claim. The woman has appealed the judgment, contending that the trial court erred in entering judgment as a matter of law in favor of the defendants. The appellate court has held that the battery claim presents a jury issue.
How should the court rule on the judgment as a matter of law entered in favor of the team?

choices.A: Affirm, because an employer is not vicariously liable for a servant's battery.
choices.B: Affirm, if the pitcher's act was a knowing violation of team rules.
choices.C: Reverse and remand, because a jury could find the team vicariously liable for a battery committed by the pitcher in the course of his employment.
choices.D: Reverse and remand, if a jury could find negligence on the part of the team's management.

questions.explanation:
Respondeat superior
Employer vicariously liable when employee's conduct:
is inherent in employment positionorfurthers employer’s business

An employer is vicariously liable under the doctrine of respondeat superior for any tort committed by its employee acting within the scope of the employment relationship—ie, when:

  • the employee's conduct is inherent in the employment position (eg, a security guard batters a thieving customer) or
  • the employee acts to further the employer's business (eg, a waiter batters a customer who is complaining about food quality to protect the restaurant's integrity).

Here, a reasonable jury could find that the pitcher committed the battery within the course of his employment—eg, to further the team's success by quieting the hecklers. Therefore, the appellate court should reverse the judgment as a matter of law and remand the case for a jury to ultimately determine the team's vicarious liability (Choice C).

(Choice B) An employer (master) may be vicariously liable for a tort committed by its employee (servant) acting within the scope of the employment relationship, even if the employee knowingly violated employment guidelines or rules.

(Choice D) Vicarious liability holds the employer liable for torts committed by its employee within the scope of employment solely based on the relationship between the two parties—not based on the employer's negligent supervision or control of its employee. Therefore, it is irrelevant whether the team's management acted negligently.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of respondeat superior, an employer is vicariously liable for its employee's torts committed within the scope of the employment relationship. Torts are committed within the scope of employment when the employee's conduct is (1) inherent to the job or (2) in furtherance of the employer's business.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Agency §§ 2.04, 7.07 (Am. Law Inst. 2006) (doctrine of respondeat superior).
  • Fed. R. Civ. P. 50(a) (judgment as a matter of law).
  • Manning v. Grimsley, 643 F.2d 20 (1st Cir. 1981).
questions.zh-question:
在一场职业棒球比赛中，一名投手不断受到坐在休息区上方看台铁丝网围栏后面的一些观众的嘲讽。投手几次转身，怒视着那些嘲讽者，但嘲讽仍在继续。随后，该投手做出准备向捕手投球的姿势，但却将一个快速球扔向了嘲讽者。球穿过铁丝网围栏，击中了一名女性嘲讽者。

该女性以伤害罪为由对投手和球队提起诉讼，要求损害赔偿。审判法院就该伤害罪诉求，依法作出了有利于被告的判决。该女性对判决提起上诉，主张审判法院在依法作出有利于被告的判决方面存在错误。上诉法院已裁定，该伤害罪诉求应由陪审团裁决。

法院应如何裁决这项有利于球队的依法作出的判决？

zh-choices.A: 维持原判，因为雇主不对其雇员的伤害罪承担替代责任。
zh-choices.B: 维持原判，如果投手的行为是明知故犯地违反了球队规则。
zh-choices.C: 撤销原判并发回重审，因为陪审团可以认定球队对投手在其雇佣过程中所犯的伤害罪负有替代责任。
zh-choices.D: 撤销原判并发回重审，如果陪审团可以认定球队管理层存在过失。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Vicarious liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：替代责任（respondeat superior）下，雇主会不会为员工在工作范围内实施的殴打行为承担责任。

三秒认题路径：

员工出手 → 工作场景 → 为雇主做事 → 范围内侵权 → 雇主担责

核心法律规则

在替代责任（respondeat superior）里，雇主对员工的侵权负责，前提是员工是在雇佣范围（scope of employment）内行事。考试里最常见的两种落点是：行为本身是岗位里常见的动作，或者员工是在帮雇主做生意。

违反队规（violate rules）不等于跳出雇佣范围；只要他的动作仍然是在工作中、还在替团队处理现场问题，雇主还是可能被追责。律师-当事人特权这类词不在本题；本题只看“这一下是不是工作中的一下”。

核心判例： Manning v. Grimsley / Restatement (Third) of Agency：员工在工作中为雇主利益出手，雇主可因替代责任担责。

思维导图

看台挑衅者背景事实，不是责任主体
→
投手员工/实施者
→
球队要不要跟着担责
先问：这一下是不是在雇佣范围（scope of employment）里？
YES：动作发生在比赛中，球员是在处理现场干扰，可能是在帮球队继续比赛、维持秩序。
再问：是为了雇主业务，还是纯私人报复？
为业务：仍可能让球队承担替代责任（respondeat superior）。
卡死点：不是看他有没有先瞪人，也不是看他有没有违反队规。
结论：可由陪审团认定球队可能担责，不能直接给球队作出judgment as a matter of law。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他明知不该投，还违反了队规，所以球队应该直接免责。

但考试真正问的是：这一下是不是还发生在工作中、是不是在帮球队处理眼前的麻烦。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里投手是在比赛现场应对持续叫骂，陪审团可据此认定他是为球队业务出手，所以球队可能因within the course of his employment承担替代责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 绝对免责误判

✕ A: 把battery当成雇主一律免责，错把侵权类型当成免责规则。

❌ 法律适用 | 队规效力误判

✕ B: 看到team rules就想切断责任，但违反规则不自动脱离雇佣范围。

❌ 事实误判 | 过度强调过失

✕ D: 把negligence硬塞进来，替代责任看的是雇佣关系，不是管理层过失。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“员工是在替谁做事”，再判断是否仍在雇佣范围内，别被队规和情绪化背景带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：替代责任（respondeat superior）只看员工是不是在工作中、是不是在帮雇主做事；像这题这种现场出手，先别急着排除球队。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是程序题才常用；本题不用上诉例外，直接记“工作中 + 为雇主”就够了。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A 13-year-old girl was operating a high-speed motorboat. The boat was towing a 9-year-old boy in an inner tube tied to the rear of the motorboat by a rope. The rope became tangled around the boy's foot, causing him to suffer severe injuries.
In a suit brought on the boy's behalf against the girl, the boy has introduced uncontroverted evidence that the girl drove carelessly in such a way as to entangle the boy in the rope.
Is the boy likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the boy assumed the risk.
choices.B: No, because the girl was too young to be expected to appreciate and avoid the risk to which she exposed the boy.
choices.C: Yes, because children of the girl's age should have the capacity to operate motorboats.
choices.D: Yes, because the girl will be held to an adult standard of care.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Standards of care for negligence
Adult Must act in same manner as ordinary, reasonable adult in similar circumstances
  • Standard adjusted for physical disabilities, superior skill & knowledge, involuntary intoxication
  • Standard not adjusted for mental & emotional disabilities, voluntary intoxication
Professional Must demonstrate same knowledge, skill & care as another professional in similar community
  • National (not community) standard applied to medical specialists*
Child Must act in same manner as reasonable child of same age, intelligence & experience
  • Adult standard applied to children engaged in dangerous adult activity
  • Children under five years old incapable of negligence
*A modern trend applies a national standard of care to all physicians.

Children are generally expected to conform to a child's standard of care, which requires them to act like a reasonable child of the same age, intelligence, and experience. But a child who engages in a dangerous activity that is normally undertaken by adults (eg, driving a car) will be held to an adult standard of care. The child's conduct will then be measured against that of an ordinary, reasonable adult under the circumstances. And if the child breaches this duty of care and causes the plaintiff physical harm, the child is liable for negligence.

Here, the 13-year-old girl may have been too young to appreciate and avoid the risk to which she exposed the boy by towing him in an inner tube behind the motorboat. But she will be held to an adult standard of care because she was engaged in a dangerous adult activity (Choice B). And since the girl breached that duty of care by driving carelessly and caused the boy to suffer severe injuries, the boy will likely prevail in his suit against her.

(Choice A) In most jurisdictions, a plaintiff's voluntary assumption of the risk reduces—but does not bar—recovery. So even if the boy assumed the risk by choosing to ride in the inner tube, his recovery will not be barred.

(Choice C) Children of the girl's age should not be expected to have the capacity to operate motorboats. Instead, the boy's claim will likely succeed because the girl will be held to an adult standard of care.

📌 Educational Objective

Children who engage in a dangerous adult activity (eg, driving a motor vehicle) will be held to an adult standard of care, which requires them to conform their conduct to that of an ordinary, reasonable adult.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts § 10 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (standard of care for children).
questions.zh-question:
一名13岁的女孩正在驾驶一艘高速摩托艇。摩托艇用一根绳索拖着一个绑在船尾的充气浮胎，一名9岁男孩坐在浮胎上。绳索缠住了男孩的脚，导致他严重受伤。

在代表男孩对女孩提起的诉讼中，男孩一方提出了无可争议的证据，证明女孩的疏忽驾驶导致绳索缠住了男孩。

男孩是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为男孩自担风险。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为女孩年龄太小，不能指望她认识到并避免使男孩面临的风险。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为与女孩同龄的儿童应具备驾驶摩托艇的能力。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为女孩将被要求遵守成年人的注意义务标准。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - The Standard Of Care

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：未成年人（child）在从事危险的成人活动（dangerous adult activity）时，要不要按成人注意义务标准（adult standard of care）来判断过失。

三秒认题路径：

13岁开快艇 → 危险成人活动 → 成人标准 → 看是否疏忽 → 选 D

核心法律规则

一般情况下，未成年人（child）只要按同龄、同智力、同经验的合理孩子标准来衡量；考场意思：不是拿大人标准直接压上去。

但如果孩子在做通常由成年人从事的危险活动（dangerous activity normally undertaken by adults），就改用成人标准（adult standard of care）；考场意思：这时法院不再问“她是不是小孩”，而是问“一个合理成年人会不会这样做”。

这题里 13 岁女孩在驾驶高速摩托艇并拖曳内胎，正是这种危险成人活动，所以她要按成人注意义务判断，negligence 成立就会对受害男孩负责。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts § 10 - 未成年人从事危险成人活动时，按成人标准衡量其注意义务。

思维导图

先看被告是不是未成年人：13 岁女孩 → 原则上用孩子标准。
YES再看她做的是不是危险的成人活动（dangerous adult activity）。
本题卡死点：高速摩托艇拖人内胎，属于成人常做且高风险的活动。
YES → 改用成人注意义务标准（adult standard of care）。
再比事实：她“carelessly”驾驶，导致绳子缠住男孩脚并造成重伤。
结果 → 选 D：她会被按成人标准判断，所以男孩更可能赢
别被带跑“她才 13 岁”不是护身符；一旦进入危险成人活动，年龄退后，标准前移。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她还是个 13 岁孩子，所以应该按孩子的理解能力放她一马。

但考试真正问的是：她是不是在做危险的成人活动（dangerous adult activity）；一旦是，就直接切到成人标准（adult standard of care）。

司法考试看的是「标准怎么定」，不是「她年纪小不可怜」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干核心事实是 13 岁女孩在操作高速摩托艇并拖曳内胎，这属于危险成人活动，所以要按成人注意义务判断，她的 careless driving 足以支持男孩胜诉。

❌ 法律适用 | 风险抗辩误判

✕ A: 以为 assumed the risk 能直接挡掉赔偿，但这里最多减损，不是全灭。

❌ 概念混淆 | 年龄标准误判

✕ B: 只盯着“她太小”，忘了危险成人活动会把标准抬到成人层面。

✕ C: 把“会不会开摩托艇”偷换成“应不应该按孩子标准”，题干要的是注意义务标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定行为类型，再切标准：未成年人 + 危险成人活动 = 直接套成人注意义务。

考场速记

记忆口诀：孩子做成人危险活，按成人标准算过错。这类题先找“危险成人活动”，再决定是孩子标准还是成人标准。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A grandmother had her grandson and his friend, both eight years old, over to visit at her house. The grandson and his friend explored her home and discovered a hunting rifle in an unlocked gun cabinet. They removed it from the cabinet and were examining it when the rifle, while in the grandson's hands, somehow discharged. The bullet struck and injured his friend. The gun cabinet was normally locked, but the grandmother had opened it for dusting several days before the boys' visit and had then forgotten to relock it. She was not aware that it was unlocked when the boys arrived.
The friend brought a suit against the grandmother to recover for his injuries. The friend introduced evidence supporting all the facts listed above. At the end of the friend's case-in-chief, the grandmother moved for a directed verdict.
The jurisdiction has abolished traditional rules of landowner liability.
How should the court rule on the grandmother's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because a jury could find that the grandmother breached a duty of care she owed to the friend.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because keeping a firearm in one's home is an abnormally dangerous activity.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the grandmother did not recall that the gun cabinet was unlocked.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the grandmother is not legally responsible for the acts of her grandson.

questions.explanation:
Defendant's motion for directed verdict
(negligence claim)
Reasonable jury could find:
Δ owed π duty?
No
Grant motion
Yes
Δ breached duty?
No
Grant motion
Yes
Breach actually & proximately
caused π physical harm?
No
Grant motion
Yes
π's damages traceable to
physical harm?
No
Grant motion
Yes
Deny motion

Δ = defendant; π = plaintiff

A court should grant a defendant's motion for a directed verdict if the plaintiff fails to present legally sufficient evidence to support every element of his/her claim—i.e., no reasonable jury could find in the plaintiff's favor. In a negligence claim—the typical claim for unintentional physical harm—the plaintiff must prove all of the following:

  • The defendant owed the plaintiff a duty.
  • The defendant breached that duty.
  • The defendant's breach caused the plaintiff's harm.
  • The plaintiff is entitled to damages (i.e., suffered physical harm).

Traditionally, the duty owed to land entrants depends on their status on the land (eg, licensee). But under the modern approach—adopted in this jurisdiction and about half the others—land possessors owe all land entrants (except trespassers) a duty of reasonable care.

Here, the grandmother (land possessor) owed a duty of reasonable care to her grandson's friend because he was visiting her home (and entrant). A reasonable jury could find that she breached that duty by failing to lock the gun cabinet, which ultimately caused the friend to get shot and suffer damages. As a result, the court should deny her motion for a directed verdict and allow the case to proceed.

(Choice B) Keeping a firearm in one's home is not an abnormally dangerous activity that subjects the actor to strict liability (i.e., liability regardless of fault). That is because it is a common activity whose risk can be mitigated by reasonable care.

(Choice C) The fact that the grandmother did not recall that the gun cabinet was unlocked does not shield her from liability for negligence since she owed a duty to ensure that it was locked.

(Choice D) The grandmother is not legally responsible for her grandson's acts because they do not share a special relationship (eg, parent-child). But she is responsible for her own failure to lock the gun cabinet.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the modern approach to land-posessor liability, land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to all land entrants (except trespassers).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts §167, 51 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (general duty of land possessors).
questions.zh-question:
一位祖母让她的孙子和他八岁的朋友到她家做客。孙子和他的朋友在探索她的家时，在一个未上锁的枪柜里发现了一支猎枪。他们把它从枪柜里拿出来检查时，猎枪在孙子手中不知何故走火了。子弹击中并伤了他的朋友。枪柜通常是锁着的，但祖母在男孩们来访前几天为了除尘打开了它，然后忘记重新锁上。男孩们到达时，她并不知道枪柜是未上锁的。

朋友对祖母提起诉讼，要求赔偿其所受的伤害。朋友提出了支持上述所有事实的证据。在朋友一方完成主案陈述后，祖母申请了指示裁决。

该司法管辖区已经废除了传统的土地所有者责任规则。

法院应如何裁定祖母的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为陪审团可以认定祖母违反了她对朋友负有的注意义务。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为在家中存放枪支是一项异常危险的活动。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为祖母不记得枪柜未上锁。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为祖母对她孙子的行为不负法律责任。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告作为土地占有人，对来访儿童负有合理注意义务，且在原告举证完毕后，法院是否应因“理性陪审团仍可认定过失”而拒绝 directed verdict。

三秒认题路径：

动议判决 → 看证据够不够 → 先问 duty → 再看 breach → 终局前能否送陪审团

核心法律规则

定向裁决（directed verdict）的考场意思：如果原告证据再怎么往好处看，no reasonable jury 还是不能支持每个要件，法官才会直接判被告赢。

在过失（negligence）里，原告要证明 duty、breach、因果关系和损害；本题先卡在 duty 和 breach 是否足够送陪审团。

本辖区已废除传统土地占有人分类，所以对来访者适用的是合理注意义务（reasonable care）；题干里枪柜被忘记锁上，足以让陪审团认定 grandmother 可能违背了这份义务。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts § 51 - 土地占有人对除 trespasser 外的所有进入者负合理注意义务。

思维导图

1. 被告身份
grandmother 是房屋占有人，先进入义务审查。
2. 进入者身份
friend 是受邀来访者，不是 trespasser。
3. 适用规则
reasonable care 直接适用于所有非 trespasser。
4. 关键事实
枪柜本来该锁，却被忘记锁上；这就是可认定的 breach。
5. 结果
理性陪审团可以支持原告，所以要 Deny motion。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她只是忘了把柜子锁回去，主观上不是故意伤人，所以应该免责。

但考试真正问的是：法院现在看的是“有没有足够证据让陪审团审”，不是“被告心里有没有故意”。

另一个陷阱是把枪支风险想成 abnormally dangerous activity；在 MBE 里，普通家庭持有枪械通常还是 negligence 的分析，不会自动跳到严格责任。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 gun cabinet was unlocked 让陪审团可以认定她未尽合理注意义务；原告已把过失四要件的证据送到陪审团门口，所以不能直接判被告赢。

❌ 概念混淆 | 严责活动误判

✕ B: 把 abnormally dangerous 当成普通家用持枪。

❌ 事实误判 | 主观遗忘偷换

✕ C: 只抓她“忘记了”，却漏掉她本来就有锁柜义务。

❌ 法律适用 | 代责规则错套

✕ D: 题目追的是她自己的 failure to lock，不是孙子的行为。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看 directed verdict 的证据门槛，再把土地占有人的合理注意义务套回具体事实。

考场速记

记住这句：过失题先找 duty，再找 breach；只要原告证据足以让理性陪审团“可能判他赢”，就轮不到法院直接把案子拿走。

这题的口诀可以记成：“能给陪审团，就别直接判。”

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A private school held a bake sale to raise money. Three parents separately made chocolate chip cookies at their own homes, following their own recipes. The parents brought their cookies to school on the designated day, and a volunteer divided the cookies among small plates for sale. Each small plate contained at least one cookie from each of the three parents. Several people who purchased treats from the bake sale became ill and were diagnosed with food poisoning. After an investigation, the Health Department determined that the chocolate chip cookies caused the outbreak, and that someone who made the cookies did not follow appropriate food-safety measures.
A student who purchased a plate of the chocolate chip cookies became so ill that she required hospitalization. She sued the three parents who made the chocolate chip cookies for negligence, claiming that the parents are jointly and severally liable for her harm. The student was able to conclusively establish that the chocolate chip cookies were the cause of her illness, but not which specific parent made the contaminated cookies.
Is the student likely to succeed in her negligence suit?

choices.A: No, because the student cannot sue multiple defendants for the same harm.
choices.B: No, because there is no evidence that each of the parents was negligent.
choices.C: Yes, because the parents have the burden to prove that they did not cause the student's harm.
choices.D: Yes, because the parents were acting in concert to raise money through the bake sale.

questions.explanation:
Joint and several liability arises when two or more defendants were negligent and any one of them could have caused the plaintiff's indivisible harm. This allows the plaintiff to recover the full amount of damages from any of the negligent defendants, even if it is impossible to prove which one actually caused the harm. However, the plaintiff must first prove that each defendant was negligent.

Here, the parents were not acting in concert—ie, pursuant to a common plan or design—because they each made the cookies in their own homes, following their own recipes ((Choice D)). And there is no evidence that each parent was negligent because the Health Department merely determined that someone (not everyone) failed to follow appropriate food-safety measures. This means that the parents are not jointly and severally liable for the student's illness. Therefore, the student is unlikely to succeed in her negligence suit.

(Choice A) A plaintiff can sue multiple defendants for the same harm based on joint and several liability. However, the plaintiff must still prove that each defendant acted negligently.

(Choice C) In a joint and several liability action, the burden shifts to each defendant to prove that his/her negligence did not cause the plaintiff's harm only after the plaintiff proves that each defendant was negligent (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

If multiple defendants were negligent and any one of them could have caused the plaintiff's harm, joint and several liability allows the plaintiff to recover from any of them even if it is impossible to prove which defendant actually caused the harm. But the plaintiff must first show that each of the defendants was negligent.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 875 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (explaining that multiple tortfeasors who cause an indivisible harm can be held liable individually for the entire harm).
questions.zh-question:
题目：侵权法（Torts）— 过失（Negligence）

一所私立学校举办了一场 bake sale 以筹集资金。三位家长分别在各自家中按照各自的配方制作了 chocolate chip cookies。家长们在指定日期把饼干带到学校，一名志愿者将这些饼干分装到小盘子里出售。每个小盘子里都至少包含来自三位家长中每一位的一块饼干。几位购买了 bake sale 食品的人随后生病，并被诊断为食物中毒。经调查，Health Department 认定是这些 chocolate chip cookies 引发了此次疫情，而且制作这些饼干的人中有人没有遵守适当的 food-safety measures。

一名购买了一盘 chocolate chip cookies 的学生病得非常严重，甚至需要住院治疗。她以 negligence 为由起诉制作 chocolate chip cookies 的三位家长，并主张这些家长对她的损害承担 joint and several liability。该学生能够明确证明 chocolate chip cookies 是导致她生病的原因，但无法确定究竟是哪一位家长制作了受污染的饼干。

该学生在她的 negligence 诉讼中是否很可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为该学生不能就同一损害起诉多个被告。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为没有证据表明每一位家长都存在 negligence。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为家长们负有证明自己没有造成该学生损害的举证责任。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为家长们是为了通过 bake sale 筹款而 acting in concert。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Causation problems

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多被告的 连带责任（joint and several liability） 里，原告能不能先证明“每个被告都过失”，再去追究到底是谁做了有毒饼干。

三秒认题路径：

多被告 → 谁致害不明 → 先证各自过失 → 才谈连带 → 本题否

核心法律规则

连带责任（joint and several liability） 的考场意思：多个被告都先各自有 过失（negligence），而且任一被告都可能造成同一个不可分损害时，原告可以向其中任何一个追全额赔偿。

但前提很硬：原告必须先把“每个被告都过失”这一步证明出来。因果不明 只是在“谁具体致害”上放宽，不是把“谁有过失”也一并免掉。

这题里，能证明的是“有人没守食品安全”，不是“三个家长都没守”。所以连带责任的门槛没过，原告不能靠这个规则直接赢。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 875 —— 多个共同致成不可分损害的侵权人，可以对全损害各自负责，但仍要先证明每个被告都构成过失。

思维导图

三个家长 分别在自家烤饼干
→
同一托盘 每盘混有三人的饼干
→
学生食物中毒 损害已发生
→
关键关卡 先证每个被告都过失
→
结果 只知“有人有问题”，不够
是不是每个父母都被证明有过失？
NO： 卫生部门只说“有人 没守食品安全”，没有锁定“每个人”。
卡死点：连带责任不能跳过“每个被告都过失”这一步。
YES 才能继续： 再处理“谁实际做了有毒那批”这个因果难题。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然已经证明饼干导致了中毒，而且又分不清到底是谁做坏的，那就应该让三个父母一起赔。

但考试真正问的是：每个被告有没有先被证明过失，不是“损害看起来多严重”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题里真正缺的是“每个被告都过失”的证据，不是“损害很惨”的同情点。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只证明了饼干致病和“有人”没守食品安全，没有证明三个父母都过失，所以连带责任进不去。

❌ 概念混淆 | 多人可诉误判

✕ A: 误以为多人一起被告就自动成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 反转举证误判

✕ C: 把举证责任提前倒给被告，burden shifts 还没到那一步。

❌ 事实误判 | 共同计划偷换

✕ D: 三人各自做饼干，不是为了同一违法方案。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看“每个被告是否都过失”，再看因果不明能否触发连带责任。

考场速记

口诀：先证每人过失，再谈连带赔偿。Restatement § 875 解决的是“谁致害不明”，不是“谁有过失都不用证”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Apply joint and several liability prerequisites

reason.en: The student must satisfy the doctrinal prerequisites before any defendant can be held liable for the full harm.
reason.zh: 学生须先满足该责任的构成要件，才能要求任一被告承担全部损害。

reason.en: Recovery depends on proving each defendant breached a duty of care.
reason.zh: 能否获赔取决于能否证明各被告违反注意义务。

keywords.text: not which specific parent made the contaminated cookies

reason.en: Shows causation is indivisible but does not substitute for proving each parent's negligence.
reason.zh: 表明损害不可分，但不能替代证明各家长均有过失。

keywords.text: someone who made the cookies did not follow appropriate food-safety measures

label.zh: 仅一人未遵守食品安全

reason.en: Health Department finding supports only that one baker was negligent, not all three.
reason.zh: 卫生部门结论仅支持一名制作者有过失，而非三名家长均有过失。

keywords.text: Each small plate contained at least one cookie from each of the three parents

reason.en: Explains why any one of the three cookies could have caused the student's illness.
reason.zh: 说明三名家长制作的饼干均可能致学生生病。

keywords.text: conclusively establish that the chocolate chip cookies were the cause of her illness

reason.en: Causation is proven, but that alone does not establish joint and several liability.
reason.zh: 因果关系已成立，但仅此不足以成立连带且分别责任。

A.text: cannot sue multiple defendants for the same harm

reason.en: Misstates the law; plaintiffs may sue multiple defendants for the same indivisible harm.
reason.zh: 误述法律；原告可就同一不可分损害起诉多名被告。

B.text: no evidence that each of the parents was negligent

reason.en: States the missing element that blocks joint and several liability here.
reason.zh: 指出本案欠缺、因而阻却连带且分别责任的关键要件。

C.text: parents have the burden to prove that they did not cause the student's harm

reason.en: Burden shifts only after the plaintiff proves each defendant was negligent.
reason.zh: 仅在原告证明各被告均有过失后，举证责任才会转移。

reason.en: Parents baked separately at home and were not pursuing a common plan or design.
reason.zh: 家长各自在家烘焙，并非依共同计划或设计行事。

highlights.text: claiming that the parents are jointly and severally liable for her harm

reason.en: Frames the legal theory the student must establish against all three parents.
reason.zh: 界定学生须对三名家长主张的法律责任类型。

highlights.text: someone who made the cookies did not follow appropriate food-safety measures

reason.en: Limits the negligence finding to one unknown parent, not each defendant.
reason.zh: 过失认定仅指向一名未知家长，而非各被告均有过失。

highlights.text: not which specific parent made the contaminated cookies

reason.en: Creates indivisible harm but does not eliminate the need to prove each parent's negligence.
reason.zh: 虽形成不可分损害，但仍须证明各家长均有过失。

highlights.text: Three parents separately made chocolate chip cookies at their own homes, following their own recipes

reason.en: Undermines any acting-in-concert basis for joint liability.
reason.zh: 排除以共同行为作为连带责任基础的可能。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A politician and a businessman were passengers sitting in adjoining seats on an airline's flight. There were many empty seats on the aircraft.
During the flight, a flight attendant served the businessman eight drinks. As the businessman became more and more obviously intoxicated and attempted to engage the politician in a conversation, the politician chose to ignore the businessman. This angered the businessman, who suddenly struck the politician in the face, giving her a black eye.
If the politician asserts a claim for damages against the airline based on battery, will she prevail?

choices.A: No, because the businessman was not acting as an agent or employee of the airline.
choices.B: No, unless she can establish some permanent injury from the contact.
choices.C: Yes, because she suffered an intentionally inflicted harmful or offensive contact.
choices.D: Yes, if the flight attendant acted recklessly in continuing to serve liquor to the businessman.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Vicarious liability
(liability for tortious acts of another)
Respondeat superior Employee's conduct occurred within scope of employment—ie, under employer's control or while performing assigned work
Nondelegable duty Independent contractor's work involved abnormally or inherently dangerous activity, condition on land open to general public, or activity regulated by law
Parent Child committed tort while acting as parent's agent
Business partner Business partner's conduct occurred within scope of business
Automobile owner Family member drove car with permission (family-car doctrine) or any person drove car with permission under owner-liability statute
Dram shop & social host Alcohol sold (dram shop) or served at noncommercial setting (social liability) to visibly intoxicated person or minor

*Only applies when question provides dram-shop statute.

Vicarious liability is a type of strict liability in which a principal is liable for the tortious act (e.g., battery) of his/her agent if the act was committed within the scope of an agency relationship. An agency relationship exists when the parties mutually agree that the agent will act on the principal's behalf and subject to the principal's control (e.g., employer-employee).

Here, the businessman intentionally struck the politician in the face (battery) on the airline's flight. But since the businessman was not an employee of the airline or otherwise acting on its behalf (no agency relationship), the airline is not vicariously liable for the businessman's battery. Therefore, the politician will not prevail in her battery claim against the airline.

(Choice B) Battery merely requires proof of harmful or offensive contact—not permanent injury. Therefore, the politician's ability to show permanent injury will not affect the success of her claim against the airline. Instead, her claim will fail because the airline is not vicariously liable for the businessman's conduct.

(Choice C) The fact that the politician suffered an intentionally inflicted harmful or offensive contact when the businessman struck her face would support a battery claim against the businessman. But since the businessman was not the airline's agent, this fact will not allow the politician to prevail against the airline.

(Choice D) The airline could be vicariously liable for the flight attendant's (i.e., an employee's) negligence or recklessness in continuing to serve liquor to the businessman. But since the politician's battery claim against the airline is based on the businessman's conduct—not the flight attendant's negligence—the politician's claim will fail.

📌 Educational Objective

A principal is vicariously liable for a tort committed by his/her agent if the tort was committed within the scope of an agency relationship. An agency relationship exists when both parties agree that the agent will act on the principal's behalf and subject to the principal's control (e.g., employer-employee).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Agency § 7.03 (Am. Law Inst. 2006) (principal's liability for acts of its agents).
questions.zh-question:
一名政治家和一名商人是某航空公司航班上邻座的乘客。飞机上有很多空座位。

在飞行途中，一名空中乘务员为该商人上了八杯酒。当该商人变得越来越明显醉酒并试图与政治家交谈时，政治家选择不理睬他。这激怒了该商人，他突然打了政治家的脸，导致她眼部瘀青。

如果该政治家基于伤害罪向航空公司主张损害赔偿，她会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该商人并非作为航空公司的代理人或雇员行事。
zh-choices.B: 不会，除非她能证明此次接触造成了某种永久性伤害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为她遭受了故意造成的有害或冒犯性接触。
zh-choices.D: 会，如果空中乘务员在持续为该商人提供含酒精饮料方面的行为构成鲁莽。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Vicarious liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：雇主替员工负责（respondeat superior），但不能把一个和航空公司没有 代理关系（agency relationship） 的乘客，硬算成航空公司的“下属”。

三秒认题路径：

先找被告 → 再看代理 → 没有控制 → 不能归责 → 选 No

核心法律规则

替代责任（vicarious liability）的前提是：被告和实施侵权的人之间，先得有 代理关系（agency relationship）。考场意思：对方要“替你办事”，还要受你控制，才可能把他的错算到你头上。

雇主替代责任（respondeat superior）只管员工在 雇佣范围（scope of employment） 内的行为。考场意思：这题里打人的人只是乘客，不是航空公司的员工，更不是替航空公司行事的人，所以航空公司不背这口锅。

别被“空乘继续供酒”带偏：那最多是在想航空公司对 flight attendant 的过失是否负责，但题目现在追的是“乘客打人”这件事，责任链条断在乘客不是代理人。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Agency § 7.03 — 只有代理人在代理范围内作恶，才可能把侵权责任转给本人。

思维导图

航空公司被告 / 可能承担替代责任
→
先问：是否有代理关系？受控制、替他办事
→
本案乘客打人不是员工，也不是代理人
→
结果：不能归责航空公司不对这次 battery 负责
乘客的 battery 能不能算到航空公司头上？
先看：打人者是不是员工 / 代理人？
不是。只是乘客，和航空公司没有代理关系。
结论：没有替代责任，不能让航空公司替乘客的 battery 买单。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：空乘一直给他酒，他后来又打人，航空公司是不是也要负责。

但考试真正问的是：谁实施了 battery，以及这个人是不是航空公司的代理人；本题里打人的是乘客，不是员工。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（这题的类比点在于：不要把“航空公司有别的过失”偷换成“它一定要对乘客的故意侵权负责”。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 打人者是乘客，不是航空公司的员工或代理人，所以航空公司不承担替代责任，政治家不能靠这次 battery 直接胜诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 永久伤害误判

✕ B: 把 permanent injury 当成 battery 要件了。

❌ 法律适用 | 直接侵权误套

✕ C: 只看到被打就想直接算赢，忘了被告是航空公司。

❌ 事实误判 | 供酒责任偷换

✕ D: 把 served liquor 的过失，偷换成乘客 battery 的替代责任。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定被告和侵权人之间有没有代理关系，再决定能不能把故意侵权算到航空公司身上。

考场速记

记住一句：替代责任（vicarious liability）先看“是不是我的人”，再看“是不是在替我做事”。不是员工、不是代理人、也不在控制之下，就别急着把责任推给主事人。

这题的秒杀法：先找代理，再谈归责；没有代理，就没有 respondeat superior。

keywords.text: claim for damages against the airline based on battery

label.zh: 针对航空公司的殴打侵权索赔

reason.en: Frames the claim as battery against the airline, triggering vicarious liability analysis.
reason.zh: 将索赔定性为针对航空公司的殴打侵权，从而触发替代责任分析。

reason.en: Identifies the tort alleged, but liability against the airline still requires an agency relationship.
reason.zh: 标明所指控的侵权行为，但对航空公司承担责任仍需代理关系。

keywords.text: flight attendant served the businessman eight drinks

reason.en: May tempt selection of dram-shop or employee-negligence theories instead of vicarious battery liability.
reason.zh: 易诱使考生选择酒责法或雇员过失理论，而非替代殴打责任。

reason.en: Signals possible dram-shop liability but does not make a passenger the airline's agent.
reason.zh: 提示可能存在酒责责任，但不足以使乘客成为航空公司的代理人。

keywords.text: struck the politician in the face

reason.en: Establishes battery by the businessman but does not by itself impose airline liability.
reason.zh: 证明商人构成殴打，但本身不足以使航空公司承担责任。

reason.en: The sued party can only be liable if the batterer acted as its agent or employee.
reason.zh: 被诉方仅在其代理人或雇员实施侵权行为时方可承担责任。

A.text: agent or employee of the airline

reason.en: States the missing prerequisite for holding the airline vicariously liable for the passenger's battery.
reason.zh: 指出使航空公司对乘客殴打承担替代责任所缺失的要件。

reason.en: Misstates battery's injury requirement and distracts from the lack of vicarious liability.
reason.zh: 误述殴打的伤害要件，并转移对缺乏替代责任的注意力。

C.text: intentionally inflicted harmful or offensive contact

reason.en: Proves battery against the businessman but wrongly assumes that suffices against the airline.
reason.zh: 可证明商人构成殴打，但错误地认为足以使航空公司承担责任。

reason.en: Shifts to employee negligence in serving alcohol rather than vicarious liability for the passenger's battery.
reason.zh: 转向雇员供酒过失，而非对乘客殴打的替代责任。

reason.en: Targets flight-attendant conduct, not whether the airline is liable for the businessman's battery.
reason.zh: 针对空乘行为，而非航空公司是否对商人殴打承担责任。

highlights.text: claim for damages against the airline based on battery

reason.en: The issue is whether the airline is liable for another passenger's battery, not whether battery occurred.
reason.zh: 问题在于航空公司是否对另一名乘客的殴打承担责任，而非殴打是否发生。

highlights.text: struck the politician in the face

reason.en: Confirms intentional harmful contact by the businessman, but he is an independent passenger.
reason.zh: 确认商人故意有害接触，但其仅为独立乘客。

highlights.text: flight attendant served the businessman eight drinks

reason.en: May suggest employee fault or dram-shop liability, which does not satisfy a battery claim based on the passenger's act.
reason.zh: 可能暗示雇员过错或酒责责任，但不足以支持以乘客行为为基础的殴打索赔。

highlights.text: giving her a black eye

reason.en: Shows harm sufficient for battery without permanent injury, tempting choice C or B.
reason.zh: 表明伤害足以构成殴打且无需永久性损伤，易诱选C或B。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man's dog ran into the street in front of his home and began chasing cars. The man had seen the dog behave similarly on several prior occasions. A ride-share driver, who was driving a car on the street, swerved to avoid hitting the dog, struck a telephone pole, and was injured.
There is no statute or ordinance requiring dogs to be leashed on a public street.
If the driver asserts a claim against the man, will the driver prevail?

choices.A: No, because a dog is a domestic animal.
choices.B: No, because no statute or ordinance made it unlawful for the owner to allow a dog to be unleashed on a public street.
choices.C: Yes, because the man is strictly liable for injuries caused by his dog.
choices.D: Yes, because the man knew his dog had a propensity to chase cars and did not restrain it.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Elements of negligence
  • Duty – defendant owed duty of reasonable care because his/her conduct created foreseeable risk of harm to others
  • Breach – defendant breached duty by failing to use reasonable care
  • Causation – defendant's breach actually & proximately caused plaintiff's harm
  • Damages – plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, bodily injury or property damage)

Negligence is the typical tort claim for unintentional harms (eg, car-accident injuries). To prevail on a negligence claim, the plaintiff must prove all of the following elements by a preponderance of the evidence:

  • Duty – the defendant owed a duty of reasonable care because his/her conduct created a foreseeable risk of harm to others
  • Breach – the defendant breached that duty by failing to use reasonable care
  • Causation – the defendant's breach actually and proximately caused the plaintiff's harm
  • Damages – the plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, bodily injury or property damage)

A defendant fails to use reasonable care when he/she does not take reasonable steps to reduce the risk posed by his/her conduct.

Here, the man had a duty to use reasonable care since he knew that his dog had a propensity to chase cars. But he breached that duty when he failed to take reasonable steps to prevent the dog from running into the street (eg, by restraining it). And since this caused the driver to crash and sustain injuries, the driver will likely prevail.

(Choices A & C) The owner of a domestic animal is not strictly liable for injuries caused by that animal unless the owner knew, or should have known, that the animal had propensities that are more dangerous than normal for the species. So here, the dog's mere propensity to chase cars would not subject the man to strict liability. But the man is still subject to negligence liability for injuries caused by his dog.

(Choice B) Had the man violated a statute or ordinance requiring dogs to be leashed on public streets, his negligent conduct could be presumed under the doctrine of negligence per se. But the man's negligent conduct can still be proved since he knew of his dog's propensity to chase cars and did not restrain it.

📌 Educational Objective

Persons owe a duty of reasonable care when their conduct poses a foreseeable risk of harm to others. Therefore, persons who fail to take reasonable steps to mitigate that risk and cause another physical harm are liable for negligence.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 281 cmt. e (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that conduct is negligent when it tends to subject another to an unreasonable risk of harm).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子的狗在他家门前的街道上跑，并开始追逐汽车。该男子曾多次看到这只狗有类似的行为。一名在街上开车的网约车司机，为了躲避这只狗而急转弯，撞上了一根电线杆并受伤。

没有法律或法令要求在公共街道上必须用狗绳拴住狗。

如果司机对该男子提起诉讼，司机会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为狗是家养动物。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为没有法律或法令规定主人在公共街道上不给狗拴绳是违法的。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该男子对他的狗造成的伤害负有严格责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该男子知道他的狗有追逐汽车的习性，但没有对其进行约束。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Duty

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：狗主人知道自家狗会追车，却不去控制它时，是否因为可预见风险而对路人承担 过失（negligence） 责任。

三秒认题路径：

见狗追车 → 知道习性 → 不去控制 → 可预见风险 → 过失成立

核心法律规则

注意义务（duty of reasonable care） 的考试意思：只要自己的行为会给别人制造可预见的受伤风险，就要采取合理措施避险。违背义务（breach） 的考试意思：明知道有风险，却没有做合理防范。因果关系（causation） 的考试意思：这次没管住狗，正好导致司机撞车受伤，所以责任链条接上了。损害（damages） 的考试意思：司机真的受伤了，故可主张赔偿。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 281 cmt. e - 只要行为会把别人带入不合理受伤风险，没采取合理预防措施就可能构成过失。

思维导图

可预见风险
狗多次追车，说明主人早就知道它会冲进路面。
注意义务
既然会伤到路人，就得采取合理控制措施。
违背义务
没有拴住或约束，等于放任已知风险继续发生。
因果与损害
司机为避狗撞柱受伤，正好把责任链条闭合。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：domestic animal 就该走严格责任，或者没 leash statute 就不能告。

但考试真正问的是：这题不是在考法规罚不罚，而是在考主人有没有对已知危险做出合理防范。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 seen the dog behave similarly on several prior occasions，说明主人早知风险却没拴住，正好满足过失的注意义务与违背义务。

❌ 概念混淆 | 严格责任混淆

✕ A: 看到 domestic animal 就想当然地否认责任，把普通过失和严格责任混成一锅。

❌ 法律适用 | 法规缺失误判

✕ B: 没有 leashed statute 也不影响普通过失成立。

❌ 事实误判 | 规则门槛偷换

✕ C: 把 strictly liable 硬套进来，但这只要求知道危险后不去控制，不是怪兽级危险。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看主人是否知道危险，再看有没有采取合理控制；有这两步，就直接往过失走。

考场速记

记住一句：知道风险 + 不去控制 = 过失。动物题先别急着喊严格责任，先问主人是否早已看见这个危险会发生。

question_analysis.skill_tested: apply negligence duty for known animal propensity

reason.en: The dog's car-chasing habit creates foreseeable risk and triggers owner duty.
reason.zh: 狗追车的习性形成可预见风险并触发主人的注意义务。

keywords.text: seen the dog behave similarly on several prior occasions

reason.en: Shows the man knew of the dangerous propensity before the incident.
reason.zh: 表明男子在事发前已知该危险习性。

keywords.text: no statute or ordinance requiring dogs to be leashed

reason.en: Eliminates negligence per se but does not defeat ordinary negligence.
reason.zh: 排除依法推定过失，但不否定一般过失责任。

keywords.text: swerved to avoid hitting the dog

reason.en: Links the dog's conduct to the driver's crash and injury.
reason.zh: 将狗的行为与司机撞车受伤联系起来。

reason.en: Identifies the harmed party asserting the tort claim.
reason.zh: 指明主张侵权索赔的受害方。

reason.en: Satisfies the damages element of negligence.
reason.zh: 满足过失侵权的损害要件。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A homeowner resides downhill from a metal fabrication facility. She has sued both the owner of the facility and the supplier of a solvent used at the facility. She contends that contaminants, consisting mostly of the solvent, were released into the ground at the facility and have migrated and continue to migrate to her property, contaminating the soil, the groundwater, and her well. She alleges various acts of negligence on the part of the facility owner in causing the release of the contaminants into the ground. She also alleges that employees of the solvent supplier were negligent in frequently spilling some of the solvent onto the ground while filling a rooftop tank at the facility.
The solvent supplier has moved for summary judgment, arguing that if there was any contamination, the facility owner and the supplier independently contributed indeterminate amounts to the contamination and that therefore the homeowner cannot show how much damage each has inflicted on her.
There is no evidence that the facility owner and the solvent supplier acted in concert.
Should the court grant the summary judgment motion?

choices.A: No, because concurrent tortfeasors are jointly and severally liable for an indivisible injury.
choices.B: No, because the solvent supplier is vicariously liable for damage inflicted by the facility owner.
choices.C: Yes, because there is no basis for allocating damages against the solvent supplier.
choices.D: Yes, because there is no evidence that the facility owner and the solvent supplier acted in concert.

questions.explanation:
Liability of multiple negligent actors
Indivisible injuriesSeparable injuries
Acting independentlyJoint & several liability*Several liability only
Acting in concertJoint & several liability
*Default rule on MBE.

A movant is entitled to summary judgment when there is no genuine dispute of material fact and the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law—eg, when the nonmovant fails to prove his/her claim. A claim for negligence requires proof that a tortfeasor's conduct actually and proximately caused the alleged harm. If the harm was caused by multiple tortfeasors, then those tortfeasors can be held:

  • severally liable – when each tortfeasor is liable for a proportionate amount of damages because his/her independent actions caused separable injuries or
  • jointly and severally liable – when any tortfeasor can be held liable for the total amount of damages because his/her independent or concerted actions concurrently caused an indivisible injury.

Here, the solvent supplier's motion for summary judgment alleges that both parties contributed indeterminate amounts to the contamination. This allegation shows that the homeowner suffered an indivisible injury, so either the solvent supplier or the facility owner can be held jointly and severally liable for all of her harm—even though they did not act in concert. As a result, the solvent supplier is not entitled to judgment as a matter of law, and the court should deny its summary judgment motion (Choice C).

*When a plaintiff recovers the full amount of damages from any one of the tortfeasors, that tortfeasor can then sue the others for indemnity or contribution.

(Choice B) Under vicarious liability, a principal is strictly liable for its agent's tortious acts committed within the scope of an agency relationship (eg, employer-employee). Here, the solvent supplier is vicariously liable for the damage caused by its employees—but not for the damage caused by the facility owner.

(Choice D) Joint and several liability applies if the concerted or independent acts of multiple tortfeasors concurrently caused an indivisible injury. Therefore, evidence that the facility owner and the solvent supplier acted in concert is not required.

📌 Educational Objective

When multiple tortfeasors caused the plaintiff harm, each will be liable for a proportionate amount of damages if his/her independent actions caused separable injuries (ie, several liability) OR for the total amount if their independent or concerted actions concurrently caused an indivisible injury (ie, joint and several liability).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § A18 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (joint & several liability).

溶剂供应商已提出简易判决动议，辩称如果存在任何污染，工厂厂主和供应商是独立地造成了不确定数量的污染，因此房主无法证明各方对她造成了多少损害。

没有证据表明工厂厂主和溶剂供应商是共同行动的。

法院是否应批准该简易判决动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为并发侵权行为人对不可分割的损害承担连带责任。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为溶剂供应商对工厂厂主造成的损害负有替代责任。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为没有向溶剂供应商分配损害赔偿的依据。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为没有证据表明工厂厂主和溶剂供应商是共同行动的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Sharing Liability Among Multiple Defendants

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多个过失人独立造成同一处 不可分损害（indivisible injury） 时，是否要因为“算不出各自份额”就直接给被告判简易判决。

三秒认题路径：

独立过失 → 损害难分 → 看是否可分 → 不可分就连带 → 不能直接胜诉

核心法律规则

共同侵权人（concurrent tortfeasors）如果各自的独立行为一起造成同一个 不可分损害（indivisible injury），考试上通常要承担 连带责任（joint and several liability）：原告可以向任一被告追讨全部损害，不必先证明每个人精确占了多少比例。

相反，如果各自行为造成的是可分开的不同损害，才走 按份责任（several liability）。所以这题里，算不清“各占多少”不是被告脱身理由，反而说明损害可能是同一锅水，法院不能只因分摊困难就放行。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § A18 体现默认规则：独立行为若共同造成不可分损害，就可对任一被告追全额。

思维导图

先看：题干是不是在争“损害能不能分开算”?
是： 两个被告各自有过失，但都把污染推向同一块土地、同一口井。
规则： 独立行为 + 同时造成同一污染结果 = 不可分损害（indivisible injury）。
卡死点：不是要先算出每家污染比例，effectively reviewable 这类思路不适用；这里直接看能否向任一被告追全额。
结论： 不需要双方 acting in concert，仍可 joint and several liability。
答案： 所以不能给 solvent supplier 简易判决，应选 A 的方向。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然两家都“只贡献了不确定的一部分”，那就说明原告没法证明各自损失比例，应该直接判被告赢。

但考试真正问的是：法律程序上能不能把全部损害先压到任何一个共同致害人身上，不是看污染在物理上能不能立刻精确拆分。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干明确说两被告独立贡献了同一污染，属于 不可分损害，所以原告可向任一被告追全部损害，不能因“分不出比例”就判供应商胜诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代理责任乱套

✕ B: 把 vicarious liability 硬套到设施老板身上了。

❌ 法律适用 | 份额责任误搬

✕ C: 只盯着“算不出份额”，忽略了这里是不可分损害。

❌ 事实误判 | 共同行动偷换

✕ D: 题干已说 acted in concert 不是必需条件。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓损害是否可分，再决定是按份责任还是连带责任。

考场速记

记住一句话：独立行为 + 同一不可分损害 = 任一人可背全责；只有损害真能分开，才谈按份责任。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A farmer owns a large farm on which he allows his friends to hunt during quail-hunting season. He does not provide his friends with any instructions about gun safety. The neighbor who owns property adjacent to the farm knows of the friends' use of the property during the hunting season.
One day during the hunting season, without the farmer's knowledge or permission, the neighbor took a shortcut across the farm to visit an acquaintance. The neighbor was wounded by a shot fired by one of the farmer's friends, who was shooting at quail and carelessly failed to see the neighbor.
Traditional rules of landowners' and occupiers' liability apply.
In an action by the neighbor against the farmer to recover for the injuries, will the neighbor be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the farmer is not responsible for his friends' conduct.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor was trespassing.
choices.C: Yes, because the careless friend was permitted to hunt without safety training.
choices.D: Yes, because the use of firearms is an abnormally dangerous activity.

questions.explanation:
Land possessor's duty to land entrants
(traditional approach)*
Status Characteristics Duty
Trespasser
  • Intentionally enters land without permission
  • Known or frequent trespassers — warn of known artificial dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
  • Unknown or unanticipated trespassers — no duty
Licensee
  • Enters land with permission (eg, social guest)
  • Warn of known latent dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
Invitee
  • Enters land open to public (eg, churchgoer)
  • Enters land for business purpose (eg, store customer)
  • Inspect for unknown dangers
  • Make premises safe or provide adequate warnings
  • Prevent harm from active operations

*In jurisdictions that follow the modern approach, land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to all land entrants, except flagrant trespassers.

Under the traditional approach, persons who occupy and control land (ie, land possessors) owe foreseeable land entrants a duty to exercise reasonable care. But a land possessor owes no duty to trespassers—those who intentionally enter another's land without permission—unless the land possessor knows of, or can reasonably anticipate, their presence. The land possessor is then liable for negligence if he/she breaches this duty and causes the trespasser physical harm.

Here, the neighbor was a trespasser since the neighbor intentionally entered the farmer's land without permission. And the farmer did not know that the neighbor was on the farmer's land. Nor is there any indication that the farmer had reason to anticipate the neighbor's presence (eg, from frequently witnessing the neighbor cut across the farm). As a result, the farmer did not owe his neighbor a duty of care, and the neighbor is unlikely to prevail.

(Choice A) Although the farmer is not responsible (ie, vicariously liable) for his friends' conduct, the farmer could have been liable for his own negligent conduct if he had owed his neighbor a duty (not seen here).

(Choice C) Had the neighbor been a foreseeable land entrant, the farmer would have owed the neighbor a duty to use reasonable care in active operations on the farm—eg, by ensuring that his friends had gun-safety training. But since the neighbor was an unknown and unanticipated trespasser, the farmer owed the neighbor no duty.

(Choice D) Using firearms in rural areas during hunting season is not an abnormally dangerous activity that subjects a defendant to strict liability—ie, liability imposed regardless of fault—since this is a common activity whose risks can be mitigated by reasonable care.

📌 Educational Objective

A land possessor only owes a duty of reasonable care to foreseeable land entrants—not unforeseeable ones (eg, unknown and unanticipated trespassers).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 333 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (no duty to unknown trespassers).
questions.zh-question:
一个农民拥有一个大农场，在鹌鹑狩猎季节，他允许朋友们在农场上打猎。他没有向朋友们提供任何关于枪支安全的指导。拥有与该农场相邻地产的邻居知道，在狩猎季节，农民的朋友们会使用这片土地。

狩猎季节的一天，邻居在未经农民知情或许可的情况下，抄近道穿过农场去拜访一位熟人。邻居被农民的一位朋友开枪射伤，当时这位朋友正在射击鹌鹑，并因疏忽而未能看到邻居。

本案适用土地所有者和占有者的传统责任规则。

在邻居向农民提起的旨在就其伤害获得赔偿的诉讼中，邻居是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为农民不对其朋友的行为承担责任。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为邻居是非法侵入者。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为那个疏忽的朋友在未受过安全培训的情况下被允许打猎。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为使用枪支是一种异常危险的活动。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - The Standard Of Care

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：传统土地占有人规则下，未知且未预见的擅入者（unknown and unanticipated trespasser）能不能逼出农场主的注意义务。

三秒认题路径：

擅自进地 → 先看身份 → 是否擅入者 → 是否可预见 → 有没有义务

核心法律规则

传统规则下，土地占有人对可预见的进入者要尽到合理注意义务（reasonable care），但对擅入者（trespasser）通常没有义务（no duty）。

只有当占有人知道，或者能够合理预见擅入者会出现时，才可能对其负担有限义务；对未知、未预见的擅入者，考试上直接切掉注意义务这一关。

本题里，邻居是自己未经许可穿过农场的人，而且农场主并不知道、也没有理由预见他会来，所以结果是：没有注意义务，邻居很难胜诉。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 333 — 未知擅入者通常无义务，所以先看身份，不要先冲着过失细节跑。

思维导图

先问：邻居有没有先天的受保护身份？
NO邻居是未经许可进入（trespass），而且农场主不知情。
卡死点：未知、未预见的擅入者 → 通常 no duty
再问：能不能把案子拉回“朋友没受训”或“打猎很危险”？
NO这些都是背景噪音；先看农场主对邻居本身有没有义务。
没有义务，就不用继续算 breach。
最后结论：邻居能赢吗？
NO因为题目锁定的是擅入者无义务，所以答案落在 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：朋友没有枪械安全训练，农场主应该负责，所以邻居当然能告赢。

但考试真正问的是：农场主对这个邻居有没有先成立的注意义务；没有义务，后面的失误细节就救不回来。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的伤害看起来有多严重」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干最关键的触发点是邻居未经许可穿过农场，而农场主不知道也无法预见其存在，所以对他没有注意义务。

❌ 概念混淆 | 代位责任误判

✕ A: 把朋友的射击失误硬算成农场主的直接责任。

❌ 事实误判 | 安全培训偷换

✕ C: 只盯着gun safety，却忽略邻居先是擅入者。

❌ 法律适用 | 严格责任套错

✕ D: 把打猎当成abnormally dangerous，题目根本没走严格责任。

这题建议用什么方法？

先卡住土地占有人义务，再看例外；只要是未知擅入者，先别往过失细节里钻。

考场速记

记住一句话：先定身份，再定义务。传统规则下，未知、未预见的擅入者通常直接被排除在注意义务之外。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A fire that started in the defendant's warehouse spread to the plaintiff's adjacent warehouse. The defendant did not intentionally start the fire, and the plaintiff can produce no evidence as to how the fire started. However, the defendant had failed to install a sprinkler system, which was required by a criminal statute. The plaintiff can produce evidence that had the sprinkler system been installed, it could have extinguished the fire before it spread.
In an action by the plaintiff against the defendant to recover for the fire damage, is it possible for the plaintiff to prevail?

choices.A: No, because there is no evidence that the defendant negligently caused the fire to start.
choices.B: No, because the statute provides only for criminal penalties.
choices.C: Yes, because a landowner is strictly liable for harm to others caused by the spread of fire from his premises under the doctrine of Rylands v. Fletcher.
choices.D: Yes, because the plaintiff was harmed as a result of the defendant's violation of a statute that was meant to protect against this type of occurrence.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Elements of negligence per se
• Defendant violated statute or ordinance
• Plaintiff suffered type of harm statute or ordinance was intended to prevent
• Plaintiff is in class of persons statute or ordinance was intended to protect

Civil actions for accidental fire damage are typically based on negligence. To prevail on a negligence claim, the plaintiff must prove the following elements: duty, breach, causation, and damages. And under the doctrine of negligence per se, the elements of duty and breach are presumed if:

  • the defendant violated a statute
  • that statute was intended to prevent the type of harm suffered by the plaintiff and
  • the plaintiff is within a class of persons that the statute was intended to protect.

Here, the defendant violated a statute designed to protect buildings and people from fire by failing to install a sprinkler system. As a result, the defendant's duty and breach will be presumed. And though there is no evidence that he negligently caused the fire to start, there is evidence that a sprinkler system could have prevented the fire from spreading to the plaintiff's warehouse (Choice A). As a result, there is evidence that the defendant's failure to install a sprinkler system caused the plaintiff's loss—making it possible for the plaintiff to prevail.

(Choice B) The fact that a statute provides only for criminal penalties does not preclude it from establishing a duty of care for a civil negligence claim.

(Choice C) Under the modern interpretation of Rylands v. Fletcher, a landowner is strictly liable for harm caused by an abnormally dangerous activity on his/her land. Since there is no indication that the defendant was engaging in any such activity in his warehouse here, this precedent does not apply.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of negligence per se, duty and breach are presumed if (1) the defendant violated a statute, (2) that statute was intended to prevent the type of harm suffered by the plaintiff, and (3) the plaintiff is within a class of persons that the statute was intended to protect.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 288B (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that it is negligent per se to violate a statute that establishes a duty of care).
  • Rylands v. Fletcher [1868] UKHL 1, [1868] LR 3 (HL) 330 (appeal taken from Eng.) (holding the defendant strictly liable for storing water that flooded the plaintiff's adjacent land).
questions.zh-question:
一场始于被告仓库的火灾蔓延至原告相邻的仓库。被告并非故意纵火，且原告无法提供任何关于火灾起因的证据。然而，被告未能安装刑事法规所要求的自动喷淋系统。原告可以提供证据证明，如果安装了自动喷淋系统，火灾本可以在蔓延前被扑灭。

在原告向被告提起的火灾损害赔偿诉讼中，原告是否有可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为没有证据表明被告因过失导致火灾发生。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该法规仅规定了刑事处罚。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为根据 Rylands v. Fletcher 案的原则，土地所有者对其土地上火灾蔓延对他人造成的损害承担严格责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为原告所受的损害是被告违反一项旨在防止此类事件发生的法规所导致的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Breach of duty

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失本身（negligence per se）能不能把“没装喷淋系统”直接变成可追责的违反义务，而不是去追问火到底怎么起的。

三秒认题路径：

违法定规则 → 防火伤害 → 受保护人 → 义务过失成立 → 可胜诉

核心法律规则

过失本身（negligence per se）的考场意思：只要被告违反了本来就用来防这种伤害的法规，且原告属于该法规要保护的人，原告就能直接拿到“义务+违反义务”的推定。

这题里，强制安装喷淋系统（sprinkler system）的法规就是为了防火势蔓延；所以重点不是火怎么点着，而是没装喷淋系统让火没有被及时控制，最后烧到邻仓。

因此，原告不需要先证明被告故意或亲手点火，只要证明违法法规与这类火灾损害之间有连接，就可能赢。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 288B — 违反本来就设定义务的法规，可以在民事过失案中支持过失本身。

思维导图

先问：这是不是终局判决？
不是本题重点
本题不是上诉题，真正先看的是：有没有违反防火法规。
再看：被告有没有违反法规？
有
未安装喷淋系统
法规目的
防止建筑与人员被火伤害
原告身份
邻近仓库业主，属受保护范围
卡死结论
义务与违反义务可推定；火没说明白怎么起，不妨碍原告赢。
最后落点：能不能马上反驳 A？
不能
不需要证明被告起火，只要证明违法法规导致损失

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然看不出火怎么开始，就没法证明被告有过失。

但考试真正问的是：这条防火法规能不能把“没装喷淋系统”直接变成民事过失的起点，而不是追查点火人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的未安装喷淋系统正好违反了防火法规，而原告遭受的就是法规要防的火灾蔓延损害，所以可以走过失本身（negligence per se）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“没证据证明起火”当成致命点，忽略了法规违反本身就能立住义务和违反义务。

❌ 法律适用 | 刑民功能误判

✕ B: 看到 criminal penalties 就以为不能民用，错把处罚方式当成规则效力。

❌ 事实误判 | 严格责任偷换

✕ C: 硬塞 Rylands v. Fletcher，但题干没有异常危险活动，别把严格责任当过失。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找法规目的，再对照原告是否在保护范围内，最后直接把 A 的“起火原因”踢出分析。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“先看有没有违法防火法规，再看这条法规是不是就是为了防这种火害。”

一句话速记：法规管什么伤害，就用来抓什么伤害；不用先证明谁点的火。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The owner of a shopping mall hired a construction company to design and construct a new entryway to the mall. The construction company negligently selected an unusually slippery material for the floor covering. A week after the entryway was completed, a customer who had come to the mall to buy cosmetics slipped on the floor of the entryway, sustaining injuries. The customer sued the mall owner for the construction company's negligent design of the mall's entryway.
Will the injured customer be likely to recover damages?

choices.A: No, because no other customers had previously slipped on the floor.
choices.B: No, because the construction company will likely be considered an independent contractor.
choices.C: Yes, because the customer intended to make a purchase at the mall.
choices.D: Yes, because the mall owner's duty to maintain safe conditions was nondelegable.

questions.explanation:
Nondelegable duties
(duties that cannot be assigned to another to avoid liability)

Nondelegable duties
  • Maintain safe conditions on premises open to public (eg, store, restaurant)
  • Safely perform activities that:
    • are abnormally or highly dangerous
    • infringe on private property right (eg, nuisance, trespass)
    • are regulated by law or
    • are conducted in public place

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for torts committed by its independent contractor—one who performs work for another outside an employment relationship. However, vicarious liability will be imposed if the independent contractor's work breaches a nondelegable duty owed by the principal—a duty of care that cannot be assigned to a third party to avoid liability. This includes the duty of a land possessor who holds his/her land open to the public to keep the premises safe for business visitors.

Here, the construction company was likely an independent contractor since it was hired for a one-time job— to design and construct a new entryway to the mall. And though the mall owner ordinarily would not be liable for an independent contractor's torts, the mall owner had a nondelegable duty to maintain safe conditions for its customers (Choice B). Since the construction company's work—selecting a slippery material for the floor—breached that duty, the mall owner is vicariously liable for the customer's resulting injuries.

(Choice A) Proof of prior accidents could help show that the entryway was negligently designed. But such proof is not required here since (1) possessors have a nondelegable duty to use reasonable care to discover dangerous conditions on the land before an injury occurs and (2) the construction company's negligence is stipulated above.

(Choice C) Since the mall was held open to the public, the mall owner had a nondelegable duty to maintain safe premises for all business visitors (eg, window shoppers) not just those intending to make a purchase. Therefore, the customer's intention to make a purchase is irrelevant to her recovery.

📌 Educational Objective

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for its independent contractor's torts. However, vicarious liability will be imposed when the independent contractor breaches a nondelegable duty of care owed by the principal—eg, a land possessor's duty to keep the premises safe for business visitors.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 57 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (no vicarious liability generally for independent contractors).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 344 (nondelegable duty to keep business premises safe).
questions.zh-question:
一家购物中心的所有人聘请了一家建筑公司为该购物中心设计和建造一个新的入口通道。该建筑公司因过失选用了异常湿滑的材料作为地面铺装。入口通道完工一周后，一位前来购物中心购买化妆品的顾客在入口通道的地面上滑倒并受伤。该顾客因建筑公司对购物中心入口通道的过失设计而起诉购物中心所有人。

受伤的顾客是否可能获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为之前没有其他顾客在该地面上滑倒过。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该建筑公司很可能被视为一个独立承包商。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该顾客有意在购物中心进行消费。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为购物中心所有人维持安全状况的义务是不可转委托的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Vicarious liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：承包商通常不是雇员，但如果它替业主做了不可委托义务（nondelegable duty），业主还是可能要为它的过失负责。

三秒认题路径：

承包商 → 非雇员 → 业主义务 → 不可委托 → 业主担责

核心法律规则

独立承包人（independent contractor）一般不让委托人替它背锅；考试意思：先默认 mall owner 不为承包商的一般侵权负责。

但不可委托义务（nondelegable duty）例外会把责任拉回到业主身上；考试意思：有些安全责任不能“外包”掉。

对向公众开放的场所，场所占有人（land possessor）有义务保持安全；考试意思：商场、餐馆这类地方，安全责任不能靠找承包商躲开。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 344 — 对营业性场所，业主对访客安全负有不可委托义务。

思维导图

先看：施工方是雇员吗？
不是 独立承包人（independent contractor）
默认规则：业主一般不替它的侵权负责
再问 有没有不可委托义务（nondelegable duty）？
有 安全责任不能外包 商场对公众开放 → 维护安全 → 施工方选了很滑的地面 → 业主仍可能连带担责 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：施工方是independent contractor，那商场当然不用赔。

但考试真正问的是：商场有没有把本来不能外包的安全义务交给别人做了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的危险是不是已经发生」。

所以“以前有没有人摔过”不是决定点；决定点是商场对开放给顾客的入口，能不能把安全责任甩掉。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的shopping mall open to the public 触发了业主对访客的安全维护义务；承包商虽是独立承包人，但该义务不可委托（nondelegable）。

❌ 事实误判 | 先前事故偷换

✕ A: 把“以前没人摔过”当成必需条件，漏掉了商场本来就要先保安全。

❌ 法律适用 | 独包责任误判

✕ B: 看到 independent contractor 就停住了，没继续看不可委托义务。

❌ 概念混淆 | 顾客身份误判

✕ C: 把“想买东西”误当门槛，实际上开放给公众的访客都受保护。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判承包关系，再找有没有“不能外包”的业主安全义务。

考场速记

记住一句：独立承包人规则是默认，不可委托义务（nondelegable duty）是例外；商场对公众开放时，安全责任最容易被考成这个例外。

看到“营业场所 + 承包商过失 + 顾客受伤”，先想：不是问谁施工，而是问业主能不能把安全义务甩掉。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A longshoreman fell to his death through an open hatch on the deck of a ship. The longshoreman was an employee of a company that had contracted with the ship's owner to load and unload the ship. The fall occurred at night, when loading work was over for the day, and there was no reason for the longshoreman to have been near the hatch.
A negligence action was filed against the ship's owner for the death of the longshoreman. In that action, the owner has moved for summary judgment and has provided unrebutted evidence that it is customary for the crews of ships to open the hatches for ventilation after the longshoremen have left the ships.
How should the court respond to the motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion and submit the case to the jury with instructions that the custom is relevant but not conclusive on the issue of negligence.
choices.B: Deny the motion and submit the case to the jury with instructions that the ship's owner should win if the longshoreman was improperly near the hatch.
choices.C: Deny the motion, because the probability of serious injury caused by falling down an open hatch clearly outweighs the burden of keeping the hatch closed.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the custom should be considered conclusive on the issue of negligence.

questions.explanation:
Elements of negligence
  • Duty – defendant owed duty of reasonable care because his/her conduct created foreseeable risk of harm to others
  • Breach – defendant breached duty by failing to use reasonable care
  • Causation – defendant's breach actually and proximately caused plaintiff's harm
  • Damages – plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, bodily injury or property damage)

To determine whether a defendant was negligent, the trier of fact (eg, the jury) can consider all relevant factors—including whether the defendant complied with community or industry custom. But custom is not conclusive on the issue of negligence since, among other things, the entire community or industry may be negligent. Therefore, this court should deny the ship owner's summary judgment motion and instruct the jury that the custom of opening the hatches after the longshoremen have left the ship is relevant—but not conclusive ((Choice D)).

(Choice B) The fact that the longshoreman was improperly near the hatch could show that he was contributorily negligent—ie, failed to use reasonable care for his own protection. This would completely bar his recovery if the traditional common law rule applied. But under the comparative negligence rule (default rule on the MBE), contributory negligence only reduces recovery. Therefore, the ship's owner cannot win on this basis.

(Choice C) In determining negligence issues, the jury can consider whether the probability of harm outweighed the burden of avoiding that harm (ie, the Hand formula). But here, there is no indication that the probability of serious injury caused by falling down an open hatch outweighs the burden of keeping the hatch closed. This is particularly true since it is customary to only open the hatches after the longshoremen have left the ship.

📌 Educational Objective

Evidence that the defendant complied with (or deviated from) community or industry custom is relevant—but not conclusive—on the issue of negligence.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 295A (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that the customs of the community are relevant but not conclusive on the issue of negligence).

一名码头工人在船甲板上从一个敞开的舱口坠落身亡。该码头工人是一家公司的雇员，该公司与船主签订了装卸船只的合同。坠落事件发生在晚上，当时当天的装货工作已经结束，码头工人没有理由靠近该舱口。

就该码头工人的死亡，已向船主提起过失诉讼。在该诉讼中，船主已提出简易判决动议，并提供了无可辩驳的证据，证明船员在码头工人离开船只后打开舱口通风是惯例。

法院应如何回应此动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，并将案件提交给陪审团，并指示陪审团该惯例与过失问题相关，但并非决定性因素。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，并将案件提交给陪审团，并指示陪审团如果码头工人不当靠近舱口，则船主应胜诉。
zh-choices.C: 驳回动议，因为从敞开的舱口坠落造成严重伤害的可能性明显超过了保持舱口关闭的负担。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为该惯例应被视为过失问题上的决定性因素。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Breach of duty

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：行业惯例（custom） 在 过失（negligence） 里只是参考，不是自动定输赢的绝对规则。

三秒认题路径：

开口坠亡 → 看疏忽 → 先比惯例 → 惯例可看 → 但不终局

核心法律规则

过失（negligence） 要看义务、违反、因果关系和损害；其中 违反义务（breach of duty） 不是只看被告有没有照着大家都这么做的习惯来做。

社区或行业惯例（community or industry custom） 的考场意思：它能帮陪审团判断“常人会怎么做”，但不能直接把被告判成安全，也不能直接替原告宣判。

所以这里就算船方拿出“夜里关人后再开舱盖通风”的惯例，法官也不能因为这一个事实就直接判船方赢；这只是交给陪审团评估的证据。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 295A —— 习惯是相关证据，但不是对过失问题的终局答案。

思维导图

义务
船主对装卸工人负有合理注意义务；开舱盖会制造可预见危险。
违反
争点不是“有没有惯例”，而是“这个做法是不是仍然不够小心”。
惯例证据
夜里工人离船后再开舱盖通风，说明业内常这么做，但只能加分或减分。
决胜点
custom is not conclusive，所以不能直接据此判定无过失。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然船方做法符合行业惯例，那就说明它一定尽到注意义务。

但考试真正问的是：惯例只能“帮你判断”，不能“替你判案”；陪审团还是要看这做法本身是不是合理。

这题不是在问“大家平时怎么做”，而是在问“这样做在法律上够不够小心”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干给出 unrebutted evidence 证明有开舱盖通风的惯例；这只能说明可供陪审团参考，不能把 negligence 直接锁死。

❌ 概念混淆 | 近身过失误判

✕ B: 把工人靠近舱口当成船主稳赢点，偷换成了 contributory negligence。

❌ 法律适用 | Hand公式误套

✕ C: 硬套 Hand formula，但题干没给出可直接压倒的概率与负担比较。

❌ 事实误判 | 绝对化惯例

✕ D: 把“大家都这么做”夸成当然无责，错把惯例当成了终局裁判。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 custom 的证据属性，再判断它能否单独决定 breach，通常不能。

考场速记

记住一句：custom 只能帮你判断“像不像小心”，不能自动证明“已经尽到小心”。

看到行业惯例题，先问自己：这是参考证据，还是被命题人故意写成“终局答案”？

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man shared an apartment with his roommate in a crowded multistory apartment building. One late night, the man fell asleep in bed while smoking a cigarette. The cigarette fell onto the rug, which subsequently caught fire. The man woke up and fled the building, forgetting to wake up his roommate. As the rest of the apartment quickly caught fire, the roommate woke up. He first tried to extinguish the fire, and when that failed, he tried to escape. By that time, fire alarms had been set off throughout the building. Many tenants were panicking and running out of the apartment building as quickly as possible. In the chaos, the roommate was trampled by another tenant as they both tried to exit the building. The roommate sustained severe smoke inhalation injuries when he tried to extinguish the fire. Because of the roommate's undisclosed preexisting lung condition, the damage caused a lung infection requiring a month of costly in-patient care at a hospital. The roommate also suffered a broken arm when he was trampled by the other tenant.
If the roommate sues the man for negligence, for what injuries will the man be required to pay damages?

choices.A: No injuries, because there is no proper direct causal link between the man's negligence and the roommate's injuries.
choices.B: Only the lung infection, because the panicked escape of the other tenant was an unforeseeable intervening cause of the roommate's broken arm.
choices.C: Only the broken arm, because the man could not have predicted the extent of the roommate's injuries from the smoke.
choices.D: Both the lung infection and the broken arm, because the man's negligence was the factual and proximate cause of both injuries.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Relevance of foreseeability for negligence
Duty • Defendant's duty only extends to foreseeable risks of his/her conduct
Breach • Defendant fails to act like reasonable person under similar circumstances by not mitigating foreseeable risks
Causation • Actual (but for) cause - foreseeability irrelevant
• Proximate cause - plaintiff's harm must have been foreseeable consequence of defendant's breach
Damages • Foreseeability irrelevant (ie, eggshell-skull rule)

Negligence has four elements (see table above), including causation. To prove causation, the plaintiff must show that the defendant was the actual (e.g., factual) and proximate cause of the plaintiff's injuries.

Proximate cause requires the plaintiff to show that the plaintiff's harm was a reasonably foreseeable consequence of the defendant's conduct. Unforeseeable intervening acts (i.e., superseding causes) break the chain of causation, but negligent intervening acts are typically considered foreseeable and do not.

Here, the roommate suffered a broken arm and a severe lung infection because of the man's negligence in starting the fire. Injuries such as smoke inhalation are a reasonably foreseeable consequence of fire. And though another tenant caused the roommate's broken arm (negligent intervening act), it is foreseeable that a fire would cause other tenants of the multi-story apartment building to panic and try to escape. This means that there is a proper causal link between the man's negligence and both of the roommate's injuries. (Choices A and B)

Once causation is established, the plaintiff may recover damages for any physical injury and emotional distress resulting from the defendant's negligence. And under the eggshell-plaintiff rule (i.e., thin-skull rule), the defendant need not have foreseen the extent of damages to be subject to liability for all damages.

Here, the man could not have predicted the extent of the roommate's injuries from the smoke, as he was unaware of the roommate's preexisting lung condition. But the man need not have foreseen the extent of the damages resulting from his negligence ((Choice C)). Therefore, if the roommate sues the man for negligence, the man will be required to pay damages for both the lung infection and the broken arm because his negligence was the factual and proximate cause of both.

📌 Educational Objective

Negligence requires proof that the defendant's breach of duty was the actual and proximate cause of the plaintiff's harm. And under the eggshell-plaintiff rule (i.e., thin-skull rule), the defendant is subject to liability for all resulting damages—even those that were not foreseeable.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 435 (Am. L. Inst. 1965) (explaining that a tortfeasor can be liable for harm that he/she neither foresaw nor should have foreseen).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical & Emotional Harm § 31 (Am. L. Inst. 2010) (setting forth the thin-skull rule).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子与其室友合住在一栋拥挤的多层公寓楼里。一天深夜，这名男子躺在床上抽烟时睡着了。香烟掉到地毯上，随后引发火灾。男子醒来后逃离大楼，却忘了叫醒室友。随着公寓其余部分迅速起火，室友醒了过来。他先试图扑灭火灾，但未能成功，于是尝试逃生。到那时，整栋楼里都已经响起了火警报警器。许多住户惊慌失措，争相尽快跑出公寓楼。在混乱中，室友与另一名住户同时试图离开大楼时被对方踩踏。室友在试图扑灭火灾时还遭受了严重的 smoke inhalation injuries（吸入浓烟损伤）。由于室友未披露的既往肺部疾病，这种损伤导致肺部感染，需要在医院进行为期一个月且费用高昂的住院治疗。室友还在被另一名住户踩踏时摔断了胳膊。
如果室友以 negligence（过失）起诉该男子，男子需要就哪些损害承担赔偿责任？

zh-choices.A: 不承担任何损害赔偿，因为男子的过失与室友的损害之间没有适当的直接因果关系。
zh-choices.B: 仅对肺部感染承担赔偿责任，因为另一名住户惊慌逃生属于不可预见的 intervening cause（介入原因），导致室友胳膊骨折。
zh-choices.C: 仅对胳膊骨折承担赔偿责任，因为男子无法预见室友因烟雾而遭受损害的程度。
zh-choices.D: 对肺部感染和胳膊骨折都承担赔偿责任，因为男子的过失既是两项损害的事实原因（factual cause），也是近因（proximate cause）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失侵权里，火灾引发的烟害和逃生踩伤，是否都属于可预见的近因损害，而薄颅规则只管损害程度，不帮你切断责任。

三秒认题路径：

起火失火 → 看近因 → 先判可预见 → 再看薄颅 → 选全赔

核心法律规则

过失（negligence）要证明 duty、breach、causation、damages。考试里最关键的是 近因（proximate cause）：只要伤害是被告行为的合理可预见后果，就能追责。

事实因果（actual cause）看“没有这次失火，伤会不会发生”；近因（proximate cause）看“这种结果会不会太离谱”。中间有人慌乱逃跑，通常仍是可预见的 介入行为（intervening act），不会自动切断责任。

薄颅规则（eggshell-plaintiff rule）的考场意思：被告不需要预见损害有多重，只要该类损害本来就能连到他的过失，他就要把全部后果买单。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 435 和 Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liability for Physical & Emotional Harm § 31 一起锁定本题：没预见到“伤得多重”不等于免赔。

思维导图

1. 起火过失
睡着抽烟 → 香烟掉落 → 公寓起火。这里先满足 事实因果（actual cause）。
2. 烟害
烟吸入是火灾的典型后果，属于 可预见 的近因损害。
3. 踩伤
楼里人群惊慌逃命 → 互相踩踏，属于火灾中常见的逃生反应，不是切断责任的怪事。
4. 薄颅规则
不知道对方有肺病，也照样赔；你不用预见损害严重到什么程度。
5. 结论
近因不断链 → 肺感染和骨折都算在被告头上。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：另一名租客把他踩伤了，听起来像 intervening cause，所以骨折不该算在被告头上。

但考试真正问的是：这个介入行为是不是火灾里本来就会发生的慌乱逃生；如果是，就还是可预见的链条，不是切断责任的 超强介入原因（superseding cause）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这题也一样：不是看事实够不够惨，而是看损害类型有没有被火灾的风险覆盖。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 失火 直接引发烟害和慌乱逃生，烟感染与踩伤都能接上 事实因果（actual cause） 和 近因（proximate cause），所以两项都赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 因果全盘否定

✕ A: 把火灾后的连锁伤害全当成断链，忽略了近因本来就覆盖可预见后果。

❌ 法律适用 | 介入原因误判

✕ B: 只看到 intervening cause，没看到慌乱逃生本来就是火灾常见反应。

❌ 事实误判 | 薄颅规则偷换

✕ C: 把“不知道肺病”当成免责点，误把损害大小和责任有无混为一谈。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定火灾近因，再用薄颅规则排除“没预见到伤得这么重”的假抗辩。

考场速记

记忆口诀：可预见的类型要负责，薄颅规则不管有多重。先问“这类伤害能不能从火灾里自然长出来”，再问“是不是只是更严重一点”。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man decided to have lunch at a new restaurant. While the man was eating his lunch, an accidental fire broke out in the kitchen, and the dining room quickly filled with smoke. The other restaurant patrons experienced mild discomfort, which did not require medical treatment. However, the man had been born with an acute and discerning sense of smell, and he had a job as a senior perfumer at a fragrance corporation. He subsequently sued the restaurant in negligence for the injury to the olfactory sensory cells in his nasal cavity that left him unable to work. His annual salary had been $250,000 before the accident.
Assuming that the man can otherwise establish the elements of negligence, can he recover damages for the injury to his olfactory sensory cells as well as for his loss of employment?

choices.A: No, because economic damages due to loss of employment are not recoverable in a negligence action.
choices.B: No, because the man's acute and discerning sense of smell was a preexisting condition.
choices.C: Yes, because the man can recover even if the extent of his injuries was not reasonably foreseeable.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's damages were severe and exceeded those of the other restaurant patrons.

questions.explanation:
Recovery of compensatory damages
(initial harm + normal consequences)
Initial physical harm
Subsequent physical harm
Subsequent economic harm
Subsequent emotional harm

A successful negligence claim requires proof that the plaintiff suffered physical harm (ie, personal injury or property damage) as a result of the defendant's negligent conduct. Assuming all other elements are proved, the plaintiff can then recover compensatory damages for his/her initial physical harm AND any subsequent harm (physical, economic, or emotional) that is traceable to that initial harm. This is true even if the extent of the harm was unusual or unforeseeable because "the defendant takes the victim as found."

Here, the man suffered injuries to his olfactory sensory cells (initial physical harm) as a result of the fire. This left the man unable to perform his job as a senior perfume tester (economic harm traceable to initial harm). Therefore, the man can recover compensatory damages for the injury to his olfactory sensory cells as well as for his lost employment—even if the extent of his injuries was not reasonably foreseeable.

*This is known colloquially as the "thin-skull" or "eggshell plaintiff" rule.

(Choice A) A plaintiff who suffers economic damages (eg, due to loss of employment) without any related personal injury or property damage cannot recover in a negligence action. But economic damages stemming from physical harm (as seen here) are recoverable.

(Choice B) The physical harm required for negligence includes the exacerbation of a preexisting condition, so the fact that the man's acute and discerning sense of smell was a preexisting condition does not defeat his claim.

(Choice D) While a negligence plaintiff must prove actual damages, the damages need not be severe or exceed those suffered by others who did not have a preexisting condition.

📌 Educational Objective

A successful negligence plaintiff can recover compensatory damages for his/her initial physical harm as well as any subsequent harm (physical, economic, or emotional) that stems from that initial harm. This is so even if the extent of the harm was unusual or unforeseeable.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 31 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (preexisting conditions and unforeseeable harm).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子决定去一家新餐厅吃午饭。该男子在用餐时，厨房意外起火，餐厅迅速充满了烟雾。其他餐厅的顾客感到了轻微不适，但无需医疗。然而，该男子天生嗅觉敏锐，他在一家香水公司担任高级调香师。他随后以negligence（过失）为由起诉该餐厅，诉称其鼻腔嗅觉感觉细胞受损，导致他无法工作。事故发生前，他的年薪为25万美元。

假设该男子能够证明negligence（过失）的所有要素，他是否可以就其嗅觉感觉细胞的损伤以及失业损失获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为在negligence（过失）诉讼中，因失业造成的经济损失是不可获赔的。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为该男子敏锐的嗅觉是其既存状况。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为即使其伤害程度并非合理可预见，该男子仍然可以获得赔偿。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为该男子的损害严重，并超过了其他餐厅顾客的损害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Damages

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：侵权法里，初始身体损害（initial physical harm）一旦成立，后续的经济损失（economic harm）也能一起赔，而且不用要求伤害程度可预见。

三秒认题路径：

初始受伤 → 之后失业 → 损害可追溯 → 不看可预见性 → 选能赔

核心法律规则

在过失（negligence）里，先要有身体伤害或财产损害；一旦这个门槛过了，原告可以拿到与初始伤害相连的全部补偿性损害赔偿（compensatory damages）。考场意思：只要后面的失业、疼痛或情绪损害是从这次初始受伤里长出来的，就能赔。

这里适用薄壳原告规则（eggshell plaintiff rule）：被告要接受“受害人本来的样子”，所以伤得比一般人重、后果比一般人惨，也不把赔偿挡掉。考场意思：你不用证明这种程度的后果本来就能预见。

但如果只有纯粹的纯经济损失（pure economic loss），没有相关身体伤害，通常不能单独在过失里拿赔偿。考场意思：本题不是“只丢工作就能赔”，而是“先有身体伤，再带出工作损失”。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts § 31 的思路锁定本题：初始身体伤害之后的可追溯损害，哪怕很意外，也照样可赔。

思维导图

初始身体损害
题干里有火灾烟雾导致嗅觉细胞受损，这就是先成立的身体伤害。
后续经济损害
因为嗅觉受损，他做不了高级调香师，失业和收入损失都和初始伤害连着。
可预见性门槛
这里不用卡“会不会想到这么重”，因为规则本来就接受异常后果。
薄壳原告
他天生嗅觉敏锐，只是让后果更重，不会把赔偿权打掉。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他本来就很特别、伤得比别人重，所以赔偿太夸张了。

但考试真正问的是：后果是不是从这次身体伤害一路接出来的，而不是一般人会不会也伤成这样。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

换句话说，preexisting condition 不是挡箭牌；只要不是凭空出现的纯经济损失，就别被“我比别人惨很多”这个细节带跑。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的嗅觉细胞受伤是初始身体损害，后面的失业只是它带出来的后果，所以即使结果很特别，也照样能赔。

❌ 事实误判 | 纯损失偷换

✕ A: 把loss of employment当成独立纯经济损失了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 预存条件误判

✕ B: 看到preexisting就以为不能赔，但这只是让后果更重。

❌ 法律适用 | 严重性误判

✕ D: 把“比别人更严重”误当成额外门槛了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找最早的身体伤，再顺着追后续损害；只要是同一条因果链，别被可预见性吓住。

考场速记

记住一句：先有身体伤，再看后续损害；后果怪不怪，不影响赔不赔。Eggshell plaintiff 就是“被告把原告的脆弱性一起接盘”。

reason.zh: 确定适用补偿性赔偿的侵权框架。

reason.en: Provides the required personal injury that anchors all recoverable damages.

keywords.text: acute and discerning sense of smell

reason.en: Narrows the issue to damages rather than liability.

reason.en: Misleads by treating all economic damages as nonrecoverable in negligence.

reason.en: Ignores that employment loss here stems from physical injury.

B.text: acute and discerning sense of smell

reason.en: Reframes the plaintiff's vulnerability as a bar to damages.
reason.zh: 将原告特殊脆弱性曲解为赔偿障碍。

reason.en: States the correct rule that unforeseeable extent does not bar recovery.
reason.zh: 指出不可预见损害程度不妨碍赔偿的正确规则。

reason.en: Targets the foreseeability-of-extent issue controlled by eggshell plaintiff doctrine.
