questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A hiker sustained a head injury when he was struck by a limb that fell from a tree. At the time of his injury, the hiker was walking through a forest on private property without the property owner's knowledge or permission. It was determined that the limb fell because the tree was infested with termites.
In an action by the hiker against the property owner to recover for his head injury, will the hiker likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the property owner breached no duty to the hiker, who was a trespasser.
choices.B: No, because the property owner could not foresee that anyone would be injured.
choices.C: Yes, because the property owner had a duty to prevent the trees on his property from becoming dangerous.
choices.D: Yes, because the property owner is liable for hidden dangers on his property.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Land possessor's duty to land entrants
(traditional approach)*
StatusCharacteristicsDuty
Trespasser
  • Intentionally enters land without permission
  • Known or frequent trespassers — warn of known artificial dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
  • Unknown or unanticipated trespassers — no duty
Licensee
  • Enters land with permission
    (eg, social guest)
  • Warn of known latent dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
Invitee
  • Enters land open to public (eg, churchgoer)
  • Enters land for business purpose (eg, store customer)
  • Inspect for unknown dangers
  • Make premises safe or provide adequate warnings
  • Prevent harm from active operations

*In jurisdictions that follow the modern approach, land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to all land entrants, except flagrant trespassers.

Land possessors are in the best position to prevent harm to those who enter their land. As a result, they owe a duty of reasonable care to foreseeable land entrants. But no such duty is owed to trespassers — ie, persons who intentionally enter another's land without permission — unless the land possessor knows of, or has reason to anticipate, their presence on the land.

Here, the hiker was injured by a falling tree limb while walking through a forest on private property. The hiker was a trespasser because he intentionally entered the forest without the property owner's permission, and since there is no evidence that the owner knew of—or had reason to anticipate—the hiker's presence, he was an unforeseeable trespasser. As a result, the owner owed no duty to the hiker and the hiker will not recover for his injury.

(Choice B) Had the hiker been an invitee, the owner would have owed him a duty to make reasonable inspections of the property. In that case, the owner likely would have discovered the weak tree limbs and foreseen that they could injure someone. But the owner owed no such duty to the hiker since he was a trespasser.

(Choice C) The owner would have owed the hiker a duty to prevent the trees on his property from becoming dangerous (or to provide adequate warnings) had the hiker been an invitee—not a trespasser.

(Choice D) Land possessors must warn discovered or anticipated trespassers about hidden, artificial (ie, man-made) dangers on the land of which the land possessor is aware. But even if the hiker had been such a trespasser, the owner would not be liable since he had no knowledge of this hidden, natural danger.

📌 Educational Objective

A land possessor owes a duty of reasonable care to foreseeable land entrants. But no such duty is owed to unforeseeable land entrants (eg, undiscovered or unanticipated trespassers).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 333 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (no duty to unknown trespassers).
questions.zh-question:
一名徒步旅行者被一根从树上掉落的树枝击中，导致头部受伤。受伤时，该徒步旅行者正在一处私人财产的森林中行走，并未获得业主的知晓或许可。经查明，树枝掉落的原因是该树遭到了白蚁的侵蚀。

在该徒步旅行者就业主提起的旨在为其头部伤害获得赔偿的诉讼中，该徒步旅行者是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为业主未对作为非法侵入者的徒步旅行者违反任何义务。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为业主无法预见会有人受伤。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为业主有义务防止其财产上的树木变得危险。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为业主对其财产上的隐藏危险负有责任。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - The Standard Of Care

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：土地占有人对未知、未预见的 trespasser（擅自闯入者）通常不负注意义务，所以他被树枝砸伤也不能直接追究主人责任。

三秒认题路径：

未经许可 → trespasser → 未知未预见 → 无注意义务 → 选 A

核心法律规则

传统规则下，土地占有人对trespasser（擅自闯入者）考场意思：不是自动保护对象，通常no duty（无义务）。如果是licensee（许可进入者）或invitee（受邀进入者），义务会更高，但本题不是这两类。

只有在占有人知道或应当预见对方会进来时，才可能对已知危险或人工危险承担更高义务；本题里主人不知道这个徒步者会来，所以考试结论就是：no duty，不赔。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 333 — 对未知、未预见的 trespasser 通常不负义务。

思维导图

先看进入身份：他是合法进入吗？
否无许可进入私有林地 → trespasser（擅自闯入者）
再看例外主人知道或应当预见他的存在吗？
本题卡死点：题干没有任何“知道 / 预见”事实 → 不是可预见 trespasser
结果未知、未预见 trespasser → 通常 no duty
顺手排除干扰：树上有白蚁，不等于主人对 trespasser 负一般安全检查义务。
结论没有注意义务 → 不能因落枝受伤而胜诉 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：树里有白蚁，主人应该早点发现并把树修好，所以应当赔。

但考试真正问的是：这个受伤的人是不是主人需要保护的foreseeable land entrant（可预见进入者）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的树枝有没有掉下来」。

这题最容易被“看起来很危险”带跑，但危险本身不够，先看身份：是 trespasser，就先掉进“通常无义务”的门槛。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干明确写了他在私人林地上without the property owner's knowledge or permission，所以他是未知、未预见的 trespasser，主人通常无义务。

❌ 事实误判 | 预见事实偷换

✕ B: 把“会不会受伤”偷换成主人“能不能预见这人会来”。

❌ 法律适用 | 受邀人义务误套

✕ C: 这是把 duty to inspect 硬套给 trespasser。

❌ 概念混淆 | 隐藏危险误认

✕ D: 把“隐藏危险”当成对所有进入者都要警告。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定进入者身份，再决定有没有义务；不要先看伤得重不重。

考场速记

记住一句：未知 trespasser → 通常 no duty；先问“他能不能算主人应保护的人”，再问“危险大不大”。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A patron at a diner suffered a severe allergic reaction after her waiter accidentally served her the wrong meal. A doctor sitting at the adjoining booth noticed that the patron was struggling to breathe. However, the doctor did not provide any medical assistance because he had just completed a hectic 12-hour shift and wanted to enjoy his meal. The patron's throat swelled, and she eventually passed out. Later, the patron died due to oxygen deprivation. It was determined that swift medical attention would have prevented her death.
The patron's spouse has brought a wrongful death action against the doctor in a jurisdiction that has enacted a Good Samaritan statute.
Will the spouse likely recover?

choices.A: No, because the doctor had no duty to aid the patron.
choices.B: No, because the patron assumed the risk of eating in the diner.
choices.C: Yes, because a reasonable doctor would have assisted the patron.
choices.D: Yes, because the jurisdiction has enacted a Good Samaritan statute.

questions.explanation:
A wrongful death action allows a decedent's spouse, next of kin, or personal representative to sue a defendant for wrongfully causing the decedent's death. These actions are typically based on negligence—i.e., a breach of the defendant's duty to use reasonable care that caused physical harm. However, a defendant generally has no duty to aid a person facing a foreseeable risk of physical harm unless:

  • the defendant's conduct created that risk or
  • the defendant and that person share a special relationship.

Here, the patron suffered a severe allergic reaction while he was eating at a diner. Although swift medical attention would have saved her life, the doctor sitting at an adjoining booth had no duty to aid her since his conduct did not create this risk and they did not share a special relationship. Therefore, the patron's spouse likely will not recover from the doctor.

"However, the patron's spouse may be able to recover from the diner since one of its employees created the risk by accidentally serving the patron the wrong meal and a special relationship existed between the patron and the diner."

(Choice B) Assumption of the risk is a defense that reduces or bars recovery if the injured person voluntarily exposed him/herself to a known risk of harm. This defense does not apply here because the patron did not know that the wrongly served meal would cause an allergic reaction.

(Choice C) The fact that a reasonable doctor would have assisted the patron does not mean that the doctor here had a duty to do so. That is because the law generally does not require a defendant to aid another unless the defendant created the foreseeable risk of physical harm or had a special relationship with that person.

(Choice D) Many states have enacted Good Samaritan laws that relieve medical professionals of malpractice liability for voluntarily rendering emergency first aid. These laws are designed to encourage medical professionals to provide such assistance without the threat of a lawsuit, but they do not create a duty to aid.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant generally has no duty to aid a plaintiff who is at risk of physical harm unless the defendant's conduct created that risk OR the defendant and the plaintiff share a special relationship.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 6 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (negligence liability).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 7 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (general duty requirement).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 37 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (no duty to aid).
questions.zh-question:
一名食客在餐馆用餐时，因服务员意外上错菜而引发了严重的过敏反应。邻桌的一名医生注意到该食客呼吸困难。然而，这名医生因为刚结束了12小时的繁忙轮班，想好好吃顿饭，所以没有提供任何医疗救助。食客的喉咙肿胀，最终昏了过去。之后，该食客因缺氧而死亡。经查明，及时的医疗救助本可以避免她的死亡。

该食客的配偶在一个已颁布 Good Samaritan statute（善意撒玛利亚人法）的司法管辖区内，对该医生提起了非正常死亡之诉。

该配偶是否可能获得赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为医生没有救助该食客的义务。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为食客承担了在餐馆用餐的风险。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为一个通情达理的医生会救助该食客。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该司法管辖区颁布了 Good Samaritan statute。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Duty to aid

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：旁观者一般没有救助义务（duty to aid），除非他自己制造了风险，或者和受害人有特殊关系（special relationship）。

三秒认题路径：

旁观者不救 → 有无创险 → 有无特殊关系 → no duty → 选 A

核心法律规则

只需要记住的规则

一般侵权里，过失（negligence）要先有义务（duty），但法律通常不强迫陌生旁观者去救人。只有两类情况会把“没义务”改成“有义务”：一是被告自己的行为制造了危险；二是被告和原告之间存在特殊关系（special relationship）。本题里，医生只是坐在旁边看见患者发作，既没有制造这次过敏风险，也不是和她有救助型特殊关系的人，所以结论还是no duty。

核心判例：Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不在这里适用；本题真正锁定结论的是侵权法的“无救助义务”规则：没创险、没特殊关系，就不能因为“应该帮”而硬造出义务。

思维导图

先问：被告是不是这个风险的制造者？
NO医生只是旁观者，没把患者送进这次过敏危机。
再问：双方有没有特殊关系？
NO邻座医生不是照护者、雇主、保安、客运承运人这类可被强加救助义务的人。
最后看考试陷阱：reasonable doctor 会不会去救？
卡死点：会帮 ≠ 法律必须帮
只要终局后还能评价“该不该赔”，就不是这里的问题；本题问的是义务，不是道德好坏。
结论
这题直接落到 无救助义务 → 选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：医生明明看到她快窒息了，而且及时救治就能活，怎么会没有责任？

但考试真正问的是：法律程序上能不能把“旁观不救”变成义务，而不是事实看起来有多可怜。

所以“reasonable doctor 会帮忙”只是道德直觉，不是本题的义务来源；真正决定答案的是有没有创险，或者有没有特殊关系。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里医生只是邻座旁观者，既没制造过敏风险，也没和患者形成救助型特殊关系，所以no duty，不能因为“本来能救”就追责。

❌ 概念混淆 | 风险自担误判

✕ B: 把她吃饭当成知险自担，偷换了她并不知道会过敏的事实。

❌ 法律适用 | 以善意代义务

✕ C: 觉得reasonable doctor 会帮，就误把“应该帮”当成“法律要求帮”。

❌ 事实误判 | 善法功能误读

✕ D: 把Good Samaritan 当成强制救助法，其实它是护航免责，不是造义务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“谁制造风险”，再抓“有没有特殊关系”；两关都没有，就直接排除旁观者责任。

考场速记

记住一句话：见险不救不等于一定有侵权，先看创险或特殊关系。本题口诀：“没创险、没关系，通常就没救助义务。”

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
After her husband died in a hospital, a widow directed the hospital to send her husband's body to a funeral home for burial. The hospital negligently misidentified the husband's body and sent it to be cremated. When she was informed of the hospital's mistake, the widow suffered serious emotional distress. She has sued the hospital.
Is the hospital likely to be held liable to the widow?

choices.A: No, because the widow did not witness the cremation.
choices.B: No, because the widow was never in any danger of bodily harm.
choices.C: Yes, because hospitals are strictly liable if they do not properly dispose of corpses.
choices.D: Yes, because the negligent handling of the husband's body was especially likely to cause his widow serious emotional distress.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Negligent infliction of emotional distress
Theories of recoveryRequired elements
Zone of danger
  • Defendant's negligence put plaintiff in danger of immediate bodily harm
  • Danger caused plaintiff serious emotional distress
Bystander
  • Defendant negligently injured plaintiff's close relative
  • Plaintiff contemporaneously perceived that event
  • Event caused plaintiff serious emotional distress
Special situations
  • Defendant negligently:
    • delivered erroneous announcement of death or illness
    • mishandled corpse or bodily remains
    • contaminated food with repulsive foreign object
  • Caused plaintiff serious emotional distress

A plaintiff can recover for negligent infliction of emotional distress (NIED) under one of three theories: (1) zone of danger, (2) bystander, or (3) special situations. The special-situations theory applies to three scenarios where the defendant's negligence is especially likely to cause the plaintiff serious emotional harm. Liability arises under this theory when the plaintiff suffers serious emotional distress because the defendant negligently:

  • delivered an erroneous announcement of death or illness
  • mishandled a corpse or bodily remains or
  • contaminated food with a repulsive foreign object (eg, a used condom in a soda bottle).

Here, the hospital negligently mishandled the husband's corpse by mistakenly cremating it. And since the widow suffered serious emotional harm after learning of that mistake, the hospital will likely be liable to the widow for NIED.

(Choice A) A plaintiff must contemporaneously perceive an event to recover under the bystander theory for NIED. Since the widow did not witness the cremation, she cannot recover under that theory. However, she can still prevail under the special-situations theory, which does not require contemporaneous perception.

(Choice B) A plaintiff must be placed in danger of immediate bodily harm to recover under the zone-of-danger theory for NIED. The widow cannot recover under this theory since she was never in danger of bodily harm. However, she can still prevail under the special-situations theory, which does not require imminent physical danger.

(Choice C) A defendant may be strictly liable (ie, liable without a finding of fault) for physical harm caused by his/her participation in an abnormally dangerous activity (eg, storing explosives in a thickly populated area). Although the mishandling of corpses will likely cause serious emotional distress, it is not considered an abnormally dangerous activity. Therefore, the hospital is not strictly liable for improperly disposing of the husband's corpse.

(Choice D) A defendant may be strictly liable (ie, liable without a finding of fault) for physical harm caused by his/her participation in an abnormally dangerous activity (eg, storing explosives in a thickly populated area). Although the mishandling of corpses will likely cause serious emotional distress, it is not considered an abnormally dangerous activity. Therefore, the hospital is not strictly liable for improperly disposing of the husband's corpse.
📌 Educational Objective

Negligent infliction of emotional distress occurs under the special-situations theory when the plaintiff suffers serious emotional distress because the defendant negligently: (1) delivered an erroneous announcement of death or illness, (2) mishandled a corpse or bodily remains, or (3) contaminated food with a repulsive foreign object.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 47(b), cmt. f (Am. Law Inst. 2012)
questions.zh-question:
一名寡妇的丈夫在医院去世后，她指示医院将其丈夫的遗体送往殡仪馆进行安葬。医院因疏忽错误地辨认了丈夫的遗体，并将其送去火化。当寡妇被告知医院的错误后，她遭受了严重的情绪困扰。她已经起诉了该医院。

医院是否可能要对该寡妇承担责任？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为寡妇没有亲眼目睹火化过程。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为寡妇从未处于任何身体伤害的危险之中。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为如果医院未能妥善处理尸体，则应承担严格责任。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为对丈夫遗体的过失处理特别可能导致其寡妇遭受严重的情绪困扰。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Special Rules Of Liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失致精神损害（negligent infliction of emotional distress, NIED）里，特殊情形（special situations）能不能让家属因为医院错误处理尸体而直接拿到赔偿。

三秒认题路径：

尸体被误火化 → 精神损害 → special situations → 不用亲眼看见 → 选 D

核心法律规则

这条规则怎么用

过失致精神损害（NIED）不只看有没有身体伤害；在特殊情形（special situations）下，只要被告的过失本来就特别容易让人受严重精神打击，原告就能因纯精神损害获赔。考场上最常见的三类就是：错误宣布死亡或疾病、尸体或遗骸处理不当（mishandled corpse or bodily remains）、以及食物里混入令人反胃的异物。这里医院把丈夫尸体误送去火化，正落在第二类。

注意，旁观者理论（bystander theory）才要求你亲眼同步感知事件；危险区理论（zone of danger）才要求你曾处在立即身体伤害危险中。这个题都不是关键，因为题干已经给了更直接的特殊情形路径。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts § 47(b) comment f — 把“错误死亡通知、尸体处理不当、异物污染食物”这三类特殊情形直接锁进 NIED 赔偿范围。

思维导图

先看原告是不是要走 NIED？
是：情绪受害来自医院错误处理丈夫尸体。
要不要先卡 bystander / zone of danger？
卡死点：这里直接命中特殊情形，不必先找“亲眼看见”或“身处危险”。
特殊情形：mishandled corpse or bodily remains
医院误认尸体 → 送去火化 → 直击家属严重精神痛苦
结论：谁赢？
原告胜
因为这正是特殊情形 NIED，答案落在 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她没有亲眼看见火化，所以只能走 bystander，那就输了。

但考试真正问的是：医院把尸体误火化，本身就是 特殊情形（special situations），这条路根本不要求同步目击。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 mishandled corpse 直接命中 NIED 的特殊情形，医院误火化后又导致 widow 严重精神痛苦，所以可赔。

❌ 事实误判 | 目击条件偷换

✕ A: 把 did not witness 当成唯一门槛。

❌ 法律适用 | 危险区套错题

✕ B: 把 danger of bodily harm 套到尸体处理案。

❌ 概念混淆 | 严格责任误认

✕ C: 把 strictly liable 和本题的过失责任混为一谈。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找 NIED 的特殊情形，再看题干有没有直接命中“尸体处理不当”这个关键词。

考场速记

口诀：NIED 先记三路：zone of danger、bystander、special situations。看到尸体、死亡通知、异物污染食物，先别绕远路，直接想“特殊情形”就够了。

reason.en: Establishes the hospital's negligent mishandling of bodily remains.
reason.zh: 确立医院对遗体的过失性错误处理。

reason.en: Triggers the special-situations NIED category for mishandled corpses.
reason.zh: 触发特殊情形过失精神损害中的遗体处置不当类别。

reason.en: Required injury element for any NIED recovery theory.
reason.zh: 任何过失精神损害理论均须具备的伤害要件。

reason.en: Shows distress followed learning of the error, not contemporaneous perception.
reason.zh: 表明精神痛苦源于事后得知错误，而非 contemporaneous 感知。

reason.en: Identifies the plaintiff as the decedent's spouse, relevant to relationship-based theories.
reason.zh: 确认原告为死者配偶，与基于亲属关系的理论相关。

reason.en: Shows the hospital breached the widow's directed disposition of the body.
reason.zh: 表明医院违反了遗孀对遗体处置的指示。

reason.en: Imports the bystander theory's contemporaneous-perception requirement, which does not govern here.
reason.zh: 引入旁观者理论的 contemporaneous 感知要件，但本案不适用该理论。

B.text: never in any danger of bodily harm

reason.en: Applies the zone-of-danger bodily-harm requirement that special situations does not require.
reason.zh: 套用危险区域理论的身体伤害要件，但特殊情形理论不要求此项。

reason.en: Misstates the basis of liability; mishandling corpses is not an abnormally dangerous activity.
reason.zh: 误述责任基础；遗体处置不当不属于异常危险活动。

reason.en: Correctly identifies the conduct but wrongly frames recovery as strict rather than negligent liability.
reason.zh: 正确识别行为类型，但错误地将责任定性为严格责任而非过失责任。

D.text: negligent handling of the husband's body

reason.en: Matches the special-situations NIED category for mishandled bodily remains.
reason.zh: 符合特殊情形过失精神损害中遗体处置不当的类别。

reason.en: Reflects the doctrine that certain negligent acts are especially likely to cause serious emotional harm.
reason.zh: 体现特定过失行为尤其可能导致严重精神损害的规则。

highlights.text: The hospital negligently misidentified the husband's body and sent it to be cremated

reason.en: This conduct fits the special-situations NIED category for mishandled bodily remains.
reason.zh: 该行为符合特殊情形过失精神损害中遗体处置不当的类别。

highlights.text: the widow suffered serious emotional distress

label.zh: 过失精神损害所需伤害

reason.en: Satisfies the serious emotional distress element needed for NIED liability.
reason.zh: 满足过失精神损害责任所需的严重精神痛苦要件。

highlights.text: When she was informed of the hospital's mistake

reason.en: Shows recovery does not depend on witnessing the event, ruling out bystander theory.
reason.zh: 表明救济不取决于亲眼目睹事件，从而排除旁观者理论。

highlights.text: Is the hospital likely to be held liable to the widow?

label.zh: 过失精神损害责任问题

reason.en: Frames the task as selecting the correct theory for negligent infliction of emotional distress.
reason.zh: 将问题框定为选择正确的过失精神损害理论。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A customer went to a restaurant for lunch. The customer told the server that he had a severe peanut allergy and requested that the chef be extra cautious about not putting peanuts in his food. The server conveyed this information to the head chef. The head chef then asked a line cook to prepare the customer's meal and told the line cook not to put any peanuts in it because the customer was allergic to them. The line cook, who had a mental disability, did not think that the dish he was preparing for the customer would taste good without peanuts. He chopped up a few peanuts and added them to the dish, thinking that a few peanuts would not harm the customer. The customer took a bite of his meal, went into anaphylactic shock, and was rushed to a nearby hospital.
If the customer files a negligence action against the line cook, is the customer likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the line cook did not act in bad faith when he decided to put peanuts in the customer's food.
choices.B: No, because the line cook's mental disability prevented him from understanding the effect of putting peanuts in the customer's food.
choices.C: Yes, because a person with a mental disability is held to the same standard as someone of ordinary intelligence and knowledge.
choices.D: Yes, because the line cook intentionally put peanuts into the customer's food.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Standards of care for negligence
Adult Must act in same manner as ordinary, reasonable adult in similar circumstances
• Standard adjusted for physical disabilities, superior skill & knowledge, involuntary intoxication
• Standard not adjusted for mental & emotional disabilities, voluntary intoxication
Professional Must demonstrate same knowledge, skill & care as another professional in similar community
• National (not community) standard applied to medical specialists*
Child Must act in same manner as reasonable child of same age, intelligence & experience
• Adult standard applied to children engaged in dangerous adult activity
• Children under five years old incapable of negligence

*A modern trend applies a national standard to all physicians.

In negligence cases, the standard of care most often imposed is that of a reasonably prudent person under the circumstances. Under this standard, a defendant is presumed to have the same mental abilities and knowledge as an average member of the community. A defendant's own mental or emotional disability is not a factor in determining whether the defendant was negligent (unless the defendant is a child). Therefore, a mentally incompetent person is held to the same standard as someone of ordinary intelligence and knowledge.

Here, a person of ordinary intelligence and knowledge who knew that the customer had a severe peanut allergy would not have put peanuts in the customer's food. The line cook will be held to that standard, even if his mental disability prevented him from understanding the ramifications of putting peanuts in the customer's food (Choice C). And since the line cook failed to conform to this standard (ie, breached his duty of care) and caused the customer's injuries, the customer is likely to prevail.

(Choice A) The standard of care for negligence is an objective one; it is measured by what a reasonably prudent person would have done rather than whether a particular defendant acted in good faith or used his/her best efforts. Therefore, the fact that the line cook did act in bad faith when he decided to put peanuts in the customer's food will not be considered in determining whether he breached his duty of care.

(Choice D) It is not enough that the line cook intentionally put peanuts in the customer's food. For negligence liability, the line cook also must have breached a duty that he owed the customer (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

In negligence cases, a mentally incompetent person is held to the same standard as a reasonably prudent person with ordinary intelligence and knowledge.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts § 11 cmt. e (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that an adult's mental or emotional disability is not a factor in determining whether he/she was negligent).
questions.zh-question:
一位顾客去餐厅吃午餐。该顾客告诉服务员自己有严重的花生过敏症，并要求厨师特别小心，不要在他的食物中放入花生。服务员将此信息传达给了主厨。主厨随后让一位流水线厨师为该顾客准备餐点，并告诉该厨师不要在其中放入任何花生，因为顾客对花生过敏。该流水线厨师有精神障碍，他认为为顾客准备的菜肴若不加花生味道会不好。他切碎了几颗花生并加入菜肴中，认为几颗花生不会伤害到顾客。顾客吃了一口餐点后，立即出现过敏性休克，并被紧急送往附近医院。

如果该顾客对该流水线厨师提起过失诉讼，顾客是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该流水线厨师在决定将花生放入顾客食物中时并非出于恶意。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该流水线厨师的精神障碍使其无法理解将花生放入顾客食物中的后果。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为有精神障碍的人需遵循与具有普通智力和知识的个人相同的标准。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该流水线厨师故意将花生放入顾客的食物中。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - The Standard Of Care

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：成人原告主张的过失责任里，精神障碍（mental disability）不会降低被告的注意义务标准，被告仍按普通谨慎人来算。

三秒认题路径：

精神障碍 → 注意标准 → 客观判断 → 不降标准 → 选 C

核心法律规则

这题只看这一条规则

过失（negligence）的核心是客观标准：合理谨慎人（reasonably prudent person）会怎么做，而不是这个被告主观上“有没有认真”。

对成年人来说，精神或情绪障碍（mental or emotional disability）一般不调低标准；所以考场意思就是：就算他真的没理解后果，法律还是按普通人知道“给严重花生过敏的人加花生是危险的”来判断。

因此，这题里线厨是否有心智缺陷，不会帮他逃过注意义务（duty of care）的判断；真正要问的是他有没有偏离普通谨慎人的做法。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts § 11 的思路 - 成年人的精神障碍通常不影响过失标准。

思维导图

1. 被告是谁
成人线厨，先按普通成人的客观标准看。
2. 争点是什么
不是“有没有主观善意”，而是“是否违反普通谨慎人标准”。
3. 干扰事实
他的精神障碍只是在解释他为什么没懂，不改法律尺子。
4. 关键触发
明知严重花生过敏 还往餐里加花生，普通人会知道这是危险行为。
5. 结论
违反客观注意标准，构成过失；答案落在 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他有精神障碍，没真正明白放花生会伤人，所以应该不算过失。

但考试真正问的是：成年人是否达到普通谨慎人的客观标准，不是他主观上懂没懂。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的骗点就是把“同情被告”偷换成“降低标准”；但过失法更看重的是行为是否偏离客观尺子。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 严重花生过敏 已告诉被告风险存在，精神障碍也不降低成年人的客观注意标准，所以客户很可能胜诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 bad faith 当成过失要件了。

❌ 事实误判 | 心智能力偷换

✕ B: 题目不给他减标准，mental disability 不是免责点。

❌ 法律适用 | 故意过错混用

✕ D: 把故意放花生当成自动成立过失，漏了注意义务分析。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓被告类型，再看注意标准是否被精神障碍改写；成年过失题默认客观尺子优先。

考场速记

记住一句：成年人精神障碍不降过失标准，但儿童和身体缺陷是另一个判断框架。

下一次看到“他不懂后果”别先同情，先问：法律是在看主观心情，还是看普通谨慎人会不会这么做。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
An expert skater and a novice skater were ice-skating in a recreational skating rink. The expert was skating backward, against the flow of the other skaters, and listening to music through her earphones. The novice was skating too fast in the direction of the expert and did not know how to slow down. The novice yelled loudly at the expert to move out of the way, but the expert could neither see nor hear the novice. Because of this, the novice accidentally ran into the expert, and both parties fell onto the ice and sustained injuries. The expert skater brought an action in a jurisdiction that applies a pure comparative-negligence theory of recovery. At trial, it was established that novice skaters were common in the recreational skating rink and that skating backward was permitted. The jury determined that the expert's total damages amounted to $100,000, that the expert was 60% at fault, and that the novice was 40% at fault.
What is the maximum amount that the expert skater can recover from the novice skater?

choices.A: Nothing, because the expert skater is more at fault than the novice skater.
choices.B: Nothing, because the expert skater's negligence is a complete bar to recovery.

To determine the amount of compensatory damages a negligence plaintiff may recover in this jurisdiction, the court must apply the rule of pure comparative negligence. Under this rule of recovery, when the plaintiff's negligence contributes to the plaintiff's own harm, the plaintiff's total recovery is reduced by the plaintiff's proportionate share of fault.

Here, the jury determined that the expert's total damages were $100,000. The jury also found that the expert was 60% at fault and that the novice was 40% at fault. Because this is a pure comparative-negligence jurisdiction, the expert's recovery must be reduced by her proportionate share of fault-i.e., 60% of $100,000, ($60,000) (Choice D). Therefore, the maximum amount that the expert can recover from the novice is $40,000 ($100,000 - $60,000 = $40,000).

(Choice A) In a modified comparative-negligence jurisdiction, the plaintiff's recovery is barred if the plaintiff is more at fault than the defendant. But in a pure comparative-negligence jurisdiction (as seen here), the plaintiff's recovery is simply reduced by her proportionate share of fault.

(Choice B) At common law, a plaintiff's contributory negligence is a complete bar to recovery. But here, pure comparative negligence applies, allowing the expert to recover $40,000 from the novice.

📌 Educational Objective

Under pure comparative negligence, a negligent plaintiff's recovery is reduced by her proportionate share of fault.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § 7 (Am. Law Inst. 2000) (pure comparative negligence).

一名滑冰高手和一名滑冰新手在一个休闲滑冰场（recreational skating rink）里滑冰。高手正倒滑（skating backward），逆着其他滑冰者的流动方向滑行，而且戴着耳机听音乐。新手则以过快的速度朝高手的方向滑去，并且不知道如何减速。新手大声冲高手喊叫让其让开，但高手既看不见也听不见新手。由于这一原因，新手不小心撞上了高手，双方都摔倒在冰面上并受伤。高手在一个适用纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence）赔偿理论的管辖区提起诉讼。庭审中已查明，休闲滑冰场里经常有滑冰新手，而且倒滑是被允许的。陪审团认定，高手的总损失为100,000美元，高手承担60%的过错，新手承担40%的过错。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence）下，原告自己有多少过错，就按比例砍掉多少赔偿。

三秒认题路径：

纯比较过失 → 看原告过错 → 按比例扣减 → 不是全赔 → 选 $40,000

核心法律规则

在纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence）里，原告即使也有过错，仍然能拿赔偿，只是按自己过错比例减少。比较过失（comparative negligence）的考场意思：先算总损害，再乘上原告那部分责任。这里总损害是 $100,000，专家自己占 60%，所以只能拿剩下的 40%。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Apportionment of Liab. § 7 —— 纯比较过失就是按原告责任比例扣减，不是一刀切全输。

思维导图

先看州法：这题是纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence）。
结论路径原告有过错，不会直接归零。
算账总损害 $100,000 → 原告 60% 责任 → 先扣 $60,000。
卡死点：不是“原告更有错就零赔”，那是 modified comparative negligence 才会出现。
答案剩余可回收 = $40,000 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：原告 60% 更有错，应该直接不能拿钱。

但考试真正问的是：这个州是不是 pure comparative negligence，不是 modified comparative negligence。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「谁看起来更该输」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干已给出总损害 $100,000 和专家 60% 过错，纯比较过失下只扣掉自己的比例，所以最多只能拿 $40,000。

❌ 法律适用 | 纯比改错位

✕ A: 把 more at fault 当成一票否决了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 普通法误搬

✕ B: 这是把 contributory negligence 的全拒规则硬套进来。

❌ 事实误判 | 把总损害当全额赔

✕ D: 忽略了专家自己要先承担 60% 责任。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认比较过失类型，再把原告责任比例直接折算成扣减金额。

考场速记

记忆口诀：纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence） = “有错也能赔，按比例砍”。先算总损害，再减原告那一份，别把它和全输的 contributory negligence 混在一起。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A rancher owns a herd of cattle that are permitted to freely roam his ranch. The cattle's blood is more alkaline than normal because their diet consists primarily of the natural grasses that grow in the ranch's slightly alkaline soil. The primary source of water for the ranch is a stream that runs through it.
Two upstream landowners use water from the stream to operate mills. Recently, each landowner has negligently increased the alkaline nature of the water. As a result, several of the rancher's cattle have died from alkalosis, a disease caused by an animal's bodily fluids being too alkaline, and the rancher has had to treat the rest of his herd to prevent their deaths. The alkali added to the water by each landowner was a substantial factor in causing the injuries to the rancher's cattle. Although each alkali addition alone would have been a factual cause of the injuries to the cattle, neither landowner added enough alkali to the water to have caused the injuries in the absence of the naturally occurring alkali in the stream.
The rancher has brought a negligence action against the two landowners for the harm suffered by his herd.
Is each landowner's conduct a cause in fact of the damage suffered by the rancher?

choices.A: No, because neither landowner's conduct as the sole source of alkali in the stream would have caused the damage.
choices.B: No, because neither landowner's conduct was the "but for" cause of the damage since it would have been caused by the action of the other landowner.
choices.C: Yes, because each landowner's conduct in adding additional alkali to the stream was a substantial factor in causing the damage.
choices.D: Yes, because it was foreseeable that each landowner's negligence in adding alkali to the stream could cause alkalosis.

questions.explanation:
Tort causation
Actual (factual) cause
  • Single cause – but for defendant's conduct, plaintiff would not have been harmed
  • Multiple causes:
    • Second Restatement (majority rule) – defendant's conduct was substantial factor causing plaintiff's harm
    • Third Restatement (minority rule) – defendant's conduct regarded as factual cause of plaintiff's harm
Proximate (legal) cause Plaintiff's harm was reasonably foreseeable consequence of defendant's conduct

A negligence action requires proof that the defendant's conduct was a cause in fact (ie, actual cause) of the plaintiff's injury. The predominant test for actual causation is the but-for test, which is satisfied if the plaintiff's injury would not have occurred without the defendant's conduct. However, this test will not work if multiple forces combine to cause the plaintiff's injury and any one alone would have been sufficient to cause the injury. In that case, the test is whether the defendant's conduct was a substantial factor in causing the injury.

Here, each landowner negligently added alkali to the stream, and each addition was sufficient to cause the injuries to the rancher's cattle when combined with the naturally occurring alkali in the stream. As a result, the substantial-factor test (not the but-for test) applies. And since the facts stipulate that each landowner's conduct was a substantial factor in causing the injuries to the rancher's cattle, each landowner's conduct is a cause in fact of the damage suffered by the rancher (Choices A & B).

(Choice C) Yes, because each landowner's conduct in adding additional alkali to the stream was a substantial factor in causing the damage.

(Choice D) The foreseeability of the plaintiff's harm is relevant to proximate cause, which is considered only after a defendant's conduct is determined to be a cause in fact of that harm.

📌 Educational Objective

Where multiple forces combine to cause the plaintiff's injury and any one alone would have been sufficient to cause the injury, the test for actual causation is whether the defendant's conduct was a substantial factor in causing the injury.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 432(2) (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (substantial-factor test for multiple causes).
questions.zh-question:
一名牧场主拥有一群牛，这些牛被允许在他的牧场上自由漫步。由于这些牛的饮食主要由生长在牧场微碱性土壤中的天然牧草构成，它们的血液比正常情况下更具碱性。牧场的主要水源是一条流经其中的溪流。

上游的两名土地所有者使用溪水来经营磨坊。最近，每位土地所有者都因过失增加了水的碱性。结果，牧场主的几头牛因碱中毒（一种因动物体液碱性过高而引起的疾病）死亡，并且牧场主不得不对其余的牛进行治疗以防止它们死亡。每位土地所有者向水中添加的碱是造成牧场主牛只受损的实质性因素。虽然单独来看，每次添加的碱都构成了对牛只损害的事实原因，但如果没有溪流中天然存在的碱，任何一位土地所有者单独添加的碱都不足以造成损害。

牧场主对这两名土地所有者提起了过失之诉，要求赔偿其牛群所遭受的损害。

每位土地所有者的行为是否是牧场主所受损害的事实原因？

zh-choices.A: 不是，因为任何一位土地所有者的行为，作为溪流中碱的唯一来源，都不会造成该损害。
zh-choices.B: 不是，因为任何一位土地所有者的行为都不是损害的“若无，则不”原因，因为损害本可由另一位土地所有者的行为造成。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为每位土地所有者向溪流中添加额外碱的行为是造成损害的实质性因素。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为每位土地所有者因过失向溪流中添加碱可能导致碱中毒是可预见的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Causation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多人共同加重同一种损害时，实际因果关系（actual cause）不用死盯 but-for，而要看每个被告是不是 实质因素（substantial factor）。

三秒认题路径：

多人加害 → 单独不够 → 合并致害 → 看 substantial factor → 选 C

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

过失（negligence） 先问 实际因果关系（actual cause），通常用 but-for test；考场意思：如果没有这个被告，伤害就不会发生，才算因果。

但如果是多个力量一起把伤害推出来，而且任何一个单独看都可能不够用，考场就改看 实质因素（substantial factor）；考场意思：不是问“少了他会不会完全没事”，而是问“他有没有真正把结果推到发生”。

可预见性（foreseeability） 属于 近因（proximate cause），要等实际因果先成立后才轮到；考场意思：先别急着想“后果远不远”，先把“是不是他导致的”答完。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 432(2) — 多个原因并发、单独都可能不足时，用 substantial factor 锁定实际因果。

思维导图

题干先给什么？
两名上游土地所有人都 疏忽加碱，而且题目明说：each addition was a substantial factor。
第一问：是不是只能用 but-for？
卡死点：不是。多个力量合并致害时，but-for 会失灵。
改用：实质因素（substantial factor）
题干已直接交代两人各自的加碱都是 substantial factor，所以两人都构成实际因果。
别被带偏：“是否可预见”不是先问点。
近因（proximate cause）要放后面，不能拿来否定已成立的 actual cause。
落点：每个 landowner 都是 cause in fact → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然两个人各自都“不够单独造成伤害”，那就不能算因果。

但考试真正问的是：多个原因叠加时，谁真的把伤害推出来了；题干已经告诉你两人的加碱都达到 实质因素（substantial factor）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干直接说两次加碱都 substantial factor，而且是多重原因合并致害，所以两名 landowner 都是 actual cause。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“单独不够”误当成“一定不是因果”。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间因果误判

✕ B: 还在死守 but-for，没看到多重原因要换测试。

❌ 事实误判 | 近因前置误判

✕ D: 把可预见性拿来抢答 actual cause，顺序错了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先辨认是不是多重原因合并致害，再用 substantial factor 替代 but-for。

考场速记

记忆口诀：单因看 but-for，多因看 substantial factor；先答 actual cause，再想 proximate cause。

reason.en: The question asks whether each defendant's conduct satisfies factual causation.
reason.zh: 题目询问各被告行为是否构成事实上的因果关系。

keywords.text: negligently increased the alkaline nature of the water

reason.zh: 各土地所有者过失提高水体碱性的行为是待检验的被告行为。

keywords.text: naturally occurring alkali in the stream

reason.en: Natural alkali combines with each defendant's addition, defeating a simple but-for analysis.
reason.zh: 天然碱性与各被告添加物结合，使单纯但因果检验无法适用。

reason.en: Establishes that actual causation must be proved as an element of negligence.
reason.zh: 表明过失侵权需证明事实因果关系这一要件。

reason.en: Identifies the specific harm that the causation analysis must explain.
reason.zh: 明确因果关系分析所要解释的特定损害类型。

A.text: sole source of alkali in the stream

reason.en: Wrongly demands that each defendant alone supply enough alkali to cause harm.
reason.zh: 错误要求各被告单独添加的碱就足以致害。

reason.en: Applies the but-for test where combined forces make substantial factor the proper test.
reason.zh: 在多重因素结合致害时仍适用但因果检验。

C.text: substantial factor in causing the damage

reason.en: Correctly states the governing actual-causation test on these stipulated facts.
reason.zh: 正确指出在题设事实下适用的事实因果关系检验。

reason.en: Confuses proximate cause with the actual-causation issue posed by the question.
reason.zh: 将近因与题目所问的事实因果关系相混淆。

highlights.text: The alkali added to the water by each landowner was a substantial factor in causing the injuries to the rancher's cattle.

reason.en: This sentence directly supplies the answer under the substantial-factor test.
reason.zh: 该句直接依据重要因素检验得出答案。

highlights.text: neither landowner added enough alkali to the water to have caused the injuries in the absence of the naturally occurring alkali in the stream

reason.en: Shows why but-for causation fails and triggers the substantial-factor rule.
reason.zh: 说明但因果检验为何不适用，从而触发重要因素规则。

highlights.text: Is each landowner's conduct a cause in fact of the damage suffered by the rancher?

reason.en: Frames the precise legal question without asking about proximate cause.
reason.zh: 界定所问 precisely 为事实因果关系，而非近因。

highlights.text: each landowner has negligently increased the alkaline nature of the water

reason.en: Two independent negligent additions set up the multiple-cause causation problem.
reason.zh: 两名土地所有者各自过失添加碱性物质，构成多重原因致害情境。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A municipal builder constructed a strip mall in an area designated as a flood zone, which had a one percent annual chance of flooding. The municipal builder negligently failed to adhere to a local building code that set forth flood-resistant construction requirements on structures built within the zone and imposed penalties for failing to meet those requirements.
Upon completing construction, the municipal builder leased storefronts to various local businesses. The following year, one of the storefronts flooded, destroying all of the merchandise therein. Even if the builder had adhered to the local building code, however, the storefront would have suffered the same damage due to the unusual severity of the flood.
The tenant of the flooded storefront sued the municipal builder in a negligence action for the value of the merchandise destroyed by the flood.
The jurisdiction continues to follow traditional rules regarding municipal tort immunity.
Will the tenant be likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the municipal builder enjoys immunity from tort liability.
choices.B: No, because the storefront would have suffered the same damage even if the municipal builder had adhered to the local building code.
choices.C: Yes, because the municipal builder's failure to adhere to the local building code was negligence per se.
choices.D: Yes, because the risk of damage to the merchandise was the type of risk that the local building code was intended to prevent.

questions.explanation:
Government immunity from tort liability
Federal government
  • Immunity governed by Federal Tort Claims Act
  • U.S. government waives immunity in tort actions except for:
  • certain enumerated torts (not including negligence)
  • discretionary functions
  • government contractors in products liability cases
  • certain traditional government activities
State governments Immunity governed by state tort-claims acts (which vary greatly)
Municipalities
  • Immunity governed by state tort-claims acts
  • Traditional rule - immunity for performance of traditional government functions but not proprietary functions
  • Public-duty rule - no liability to one citizen for failure to fulfill duty owed to public at large unless special relationship exists
Government officials Immunity for discretionary acts done without malice or improper purpose but not ministerial acts (eg, driving while on government business)

Traditionally, the immunity of a municipal actor depended on the act giving rise to the tort claim.* Immunity attached to the performance of traditional government functions (eg, police, court systems) but not to the performance of a proprietary function that is often performed by a private company (eg, utilities, parking lots). Building a shopping mall falls under the latter category, so the municipal builder here is not immune from tort liability (Choice A).

However, the tenant will only prevail in this negligence action if the tenant proves that the builder's negligent failure to adhere to the local building code actually and proximally caused the tenant's harm. Actual causation exists when, but for the defendant's tortious conduct, the plaintiff's harm would not have occurred. Since the storefront would have suffered the same damage even if the builder had adhered to the building code, the builder's negligence was not the actual cause of that harm. Therefore, the tenant is unlikely to prevail.

*Today, municipal tort liability is usually governed by the provisions of state tort-claims acts.

(Choice C) Violating a statute (eg, building code) can constitute negligence per se (ie, negligence as a matter of law). But unless that negligence actually and proximally caused the plaintiff's injuries, there can be no liability.

(Choice D) While the risk of flood damage (eg, destruction of merchandise) was the very risk that the local building code was imposed to address, compliance with the code would not have prevented the damage to the storefront here.

📌 Educational Objective

Traditionally, municipal tort immunity attached to the performance of traditional government functions but not to the performance of proprietary functions that are usually performed by a private company.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 895C cmt. e (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (governmental and proprietary functions).
questions.zh-question:
一家市政建设单位在一个被指定为洪水区的地带建造了一个带状购物中心，该地区每年有百分之一的洪水几率。该市政建设单位因过失未能遵守当地建筑法规，该法规规定了在该区域内建造的建筑物的抗洪建筑要求，并对未能满足这些要求的行为规定了罚则。

工程完工后，该市政建设单位将店面出租给多家当地商家。第二年，其中一间店面遭遇洪水，摧毁了其中的所有商品。然而，即使建设单位遵守了当地建筑法规，由于洪水的异常严重性，该店面仍会遭受同样的损失。

被淹店面的租户以过失为由对市政建设单位提起诉讼，要求赔偿被洪水摧毁的商品价值。

该司法管辖区继续遵循关于市政侵权豁免的传统规则。

租户是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为市政建设单位享有侵权责任豁免。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为即使市政建设单位遵守了当地建筑法规，该店面仍会遭受同样的损失。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为市政建设单位未能遵守当地建筑法规的行为构成了 negligence per se。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为商品受损的风险正是当地建筑法规旨在防止的那类风险。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：市政建筑虽然不享有免责，但原告还是得证明 实际因果关系（actual causation）；既然就算守法也会被同样的洪水毁掉，原告就输在因果关系。

三秒认题路径：

市政体 | 非终局 | 看因果 | 守法也坏 | 不能赢

核心法律规则

先抓规则，再看这题怎么落地

地方政府豁免（municipal tort immunity） 传统上只偏向 政府性职能（traditional government functions），像警察、法院这种；像建商、停车场、商店租赁这种更像 经营性职能（proprietary functions），通常不靠豁免挡掉责任。

但这题真正卡的是 实际因果关系（actual causation）：如果没有被告的过错，原告的损害还是会发生，那就没有 but-for causation，赔偿请求过不了。negligence per se 只能帮你证明违章是过失，不会自动补上因果关系。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 895C cmt. e —— 传统政府职能才更接近豁免；经营性项目通常不靠这层盾牌。

思维导图

先问：市政 builder 能不能直接靠豁免赢？
NO 建 strip mall = 经营性职能
下一关 再看 negligence 的因果关系
关键事实 就算守法，洪水也会毁同样的货物
第三步卡死：没有 but-for causation，损害不是由违规真正造成
YES 才会去想的误区 违反 building code ≠ 自动赔钱
结论 选 B：原告大概率败诉

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他明明违反了 building code，而且洪水损失看起来很惨，所以应该按 negligence per se 直接判原告赢。

但考试真正问的是：这次违规有没有把损失 真正造成 出来，而不是它看起来“很不合理”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里也是一样：就算违章存在，只要同样的损害照样会发生，原告还是输。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干最关键的 even if the builder had adhered 已经把 but-for causation 打掉了，所以就算有违章，原告也难赢。

❌ 概念混淆 | 豁免套错

✕ A: 把 municipal builder 直接当免赔盾牌，忽略了经营性职能。

❌ 法律适用 | 过失推定误判

✕ C: 只盯着 negligence per se，忘了还要证明损害真是它造成的。

❌ 事实误判 | 风险对应偷换

✕ D: 你抓对了 risk of flood，却漏看“守法也会淹”的决定性事实。

这题建议用什么方法？

先排豁免，再做因果关系测试；看到“守法也会同样受损”就直接锁定 B。

考场速记

记住一句：违章只管“错没错”，因果才管“有没有赔”。 这题的快判口诀就是：no but-for causation, no liability。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
The day after a man completed the sale of his house and moved out, one of the slates flew off the roof during a windstorm. The slate struck the man's former neighbor, who was on the public sidewalk. The neighbor was seriously injured. Both the man and the neighbor were aware that the roof is old and had lost several slates in ordinary windstorms on other occasions.
If the neighbor sues the man to recover damages for his injuries, will the neighbor likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the man was neither the owner nor the occupier of the house when the neighbor was injured.
choices.B: No, because the neighbor knew that in the past slates had blown off the roof during windstorms.
choices.C: Yes, because the man was aware of the condition of the roof and should have realized that it was dangerous to persons outside the premises.
choices.D: Yes, because the roof was defective when the man sold the house.

questions.explanation:
Sellers of real property

(negligence liability arising from dangerous condition on land)

Injured partySeller's liabilityDuration of liability
Person
on land		Liable for physical harm caused by natural or artificial condition if:
• condition existed at time of sale
• seller knew or should have known condition existed & posed unreasonable risk to persons on land
• buyer neither knew nor should have known of condition or risk and
• seller had reason to believe buyer would not discover condition or realize risk		• If seller created or actively concealed condition, liability until buyer discovers condition & has reasonable opportunity to remedy
• Otherwise, liability until buyer has reasonable opportunity to discover & remedy condition
Person
off land		Liable for physical harm caused by artificial condition if:
• condition existed at time of sale and
• seller knew or should have known condition existed & posed unreasonable risk to persons off land

Obligations associated with real property are generally owed by whoever occupies and controls the land—
ie, the current land possessor. But a seller (previous possessor) remains liable for negligence to persons off the land for physical harm caused by an artificial condition on the land that:

• existed at the time of sale and
• the seller knew, or should have known, existed and posed an unreasonable risk of harm to such persons.

That liability continues at least until the buyer has had a reasonable opportunity to discover and
remedy the condition.*

Here, the day after the man sold his home and moved out, a slate flew off the roof (artificial condition) during a windstorm and struck his former neighbor on the public sidewalk. The man knew that the roof was old and had lost several slates in previous windstorms, so he should have realized that it was dangerous to persons outside the premises. And since the new owner had not yet had a reasonable opportunity to discover and remedy this danger, the neighbor will likely prevail against the man (Choice A).

* If the seller created or actively concealed the condition, the seller's liability continues until the buyer has discovered and had a reasonable opportunity to remedy the condition.

(Choice C) in comparative negligence jurisdictions (default rule on the MBE), a plaintiff's recovery is reduced (not barred) if the plaintiff failed to exercise reasonable care. Therefore, the fact that the neighbor knew that slates had blown off the roof during windstorms and walked on the sidewalk anyway does not bar his claim.

(Choice B) in comparative negligence jurisdictions (default rule on the MBE), a plaintiff's recovery is reduced (not barred) if the plaintiff failed to exercise reasonable care. Therefore, the fact that the neighbor knew that slates had blown off the roof during windstorms and walked on the sidewalk anyway does not bar his claim.

(Choice D) Although the roof was defective when the man sold the house, he is only liable for negligence if he knew or should have known that the defect existed and was dangerous.

Educational objective:
A seller remains liable to persons off the land for physical harm caused by an artificial condition on the land that (1) existed at the time of sale and (2) the seller knew, or should have known, existed and posed an unreasonable risk of harm to such persons.

References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 373 (duty of sellers to those off the land).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子完成房屋出售并搬出后的第二天，一场暴风雨中，一块石板瓦从屋顶上被吹落。石板瓦击中了该男子的前邻居，当时他正在公共人行道上。邻居受了重伤。该男子和邻居都知晓屋顶老旧，并且在之前的普通风暴中也曾掉落过几块石板瓦。

如果邻居起诉该男子，要求为其伤害进行损害赔偿，邻居是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为在邻居受伤时，该男子既非房屋的所有人，也非占有人。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为邻居知道过去曾有石板瓦在暴风雨中从屋顶上被吹落。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该男子知晓屋顶的状况，并且本应意识到这对房屋外的人员是危险的。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为在该男子出售房屋时，屋顶存在缺陷。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖房后，前屋主对屋内外的危险人工瑕疵，是否还要对屋外第三人承担过失责任。

三秒认题路径：

卖房已完成 → 旧屋顶脱落 → 伤到路人 → 看卖家知风险 → 选 C

核心法律规则

对于土地上的人工条件（artificial condition），卖方在出售时若该危险已存在，且卖方知道或应当知道它会对他人造成不合理风险，卖方对受害人仍可能负过失责任（negligence liability）。“知道或应当知道”在考场意思上就是：不是要你证明他亲眼见过事故，只要旧屋顶反复掉瓦、危险明显，就够了。

对屋外的人，关键还要看伤害发生时新的占有人是否已经有合理机会去发现并修好；在此之前，前卖方不能因为已经交屋就直接脱身。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 373 — 卖方对屋外第三人的危险人工瑕疵，在出售后仍可能承担责任，直到买方有合理机会修复。

思维导图

先看：卖房后，前屋主还会不会对屋外的人负责？
第一关伤害来自人工条件（artificial condition），不是单纯偶发天灾。
第二关条件在出售时就已经存在，且卖家知道或应当知道它对外面的人有不合理风险。
第三关新买家还没来得及发现并修好时，前卖方不能靠“我已经搬走了”脱责。
卡死点：不是看房子现在谁住，而是看卖家当时是否知道危险会伤到屋外的人。
本题结论旧屋顶掉瓦伤到 sidewalk 上的邻居，卖家明知屋顶老旧且曾掉瓦，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：房子都卖掉了，前屋主不再控制房屋，应该不用赔。

但考试真正问的是：出售前就存在的危险人工瑕疵，会不会继续追到卖家头上，直到新买家有合理机会修复。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个常见误区是把邻居“知道旧瓦会掉”当成直接挡掉诉权；在comparative negligence（比较过失）里，这通常只是减赔，不是全盘否定。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干旧屋顶反复掉瓦，说明卖家明知或应知危险人工条件会伤到屋外行人，所以他不能因已交屋就免责。

❌ 概念混淆 | 所有权混淆

✕ A: 把“不是现任占有人”当成绝对免责。

❌ 事实误判 | 自担风险误判

✕ B: 邻居知道旧瓦会掉，只是comparative negligence问题，不是直接挡掉索赔。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看缺陷存在

✕ D: 只盯着“房屋有缺陷”，却漏了卖家还得知道它危险。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“卖后责任”再查卖家是否知道危险、再看受害人是在屋内还是屋外。

考场速记

记住一句：卖房不等于卖掉旧危险。只要危险人工瑕疵在出售时已存在，卖家知道或应知它会伤到屋外的人，前卖方仍可能负责。

如果题目再带“能不能立刻上诉”那类程序词，就先想：终局判决、法定中间上诉、collateral-order doctrine，别被背景故事带跑。

A.text: neither the owner nor the occupier

reason.en: Invites assumption-of-risk thinking, but comparative negligence only reduces recovery.

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A driver negligently ran into a pedestrian who was walking along a road. The pedestrian sustained an injury to his knee, causing it to buckle from time to time. Several months later, the pedestrian sustained an injury to his shoulder when his knee buckled, causing him to fall down a flight of stairs. The pedestrian then brought an action against the driver for the injuries to his knee and shoulder.
In his action against the driver, for which of his injuries may the pedestrian recover damages?

choices.A: For the injuries to his knee and shoulder, because the driver takes the victim as he finds him.
choices.B: For the injuries to his knee and shoulder, if the jury finds that the pedestrian's fall down a flight of stairs was a normal consequence of his original injury.
choices.C: For the injury to his knee only, because the injury to the pedestrian's shoulder is separable.
choices.D: For the injury to his knee only, if the jury finds that the driver could not have foreseen that his negligent driving would cause the pedestrian to fall down a flight of stairs.

questions.explanation:
Recovery of compensatory damages

(initial harm + normal consequences)
Initial physical harm
Subsequent physical harm
Subsequent economic harm
Subsequent emotional harm

To prevail on a negligence claim, the plaintiff must prove each element by a preponderance of the evidence. Once the plaintiff has done so, he/she is entitled to recover compensatory damages for (1) his/her initial physical harm (ie, personal injury, property damage) and (2) any subsequent harm - physical, economic, or emotional - that occurs as a normal consequence of that initial harm.

Here, the pedestrian suffered a knee injury when he was struck by the driver. Several months later, the pedestrian's knee buckled, causing him to fall and injure his shoulder. The pedestrian can recover compensatory damages for his knee injury because it was caused by the driver's negligence. And if the jury finds that the pedestrian's fall was a normal consequence of his original knee injury, then he can also recover compensatory damages for his shoulder injury.

(Choice A) Under the eggshell-skull rule, a tortfeasor "takes the victim as he finds him." This means that tortfeasor is liable for the full extent of the victim's harm, even if the victim was unusually vulnerable. But here, there is no indication that the pedestrian was unusually vulnerable to either injury when the driver hit him.

(Choice B) When multiple tortfeasors cause the plaintiff to sustain separable (ie, distinct) injuries, each tortfeasor is only liable for the specific injury he/she caused - ie, no joint and several liability. But here, the separability of the pedestrian's injuries is irrelevant since they were both caused by a single tortfeasor.

(Choice C) Foreseeability applies to duty and proximate cause - not damages. Therefore, the driver could be liable for both of the pedestrian's injuries even if the driver could not have foreseen that his negligent driving would cause the pedestrian to fall down a flight of stairs.

(Choice D) The driver could be liable for both of the pedestrian's injuries if the fall was a normal consequence of the original harm.

📌 Educational Objective

A successful plaintiff for negligence and other tort claims can recover compensatory damages for (1) the initial harm caused by the defendant's tort and (2) any subsequent harm that was a normal consequence of that initial harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 460 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a negligent defendant is liable for subsequent harm when it was a normal consequence of the initial harm).
questions.zh-question:
一名司机因过失撞上了一名沿路行走的行人。该行人膝盖受伤，导致膝盖时常无力弯曲。数月后，该行人因膝盖无力弯曲，从楼梯上摔下，导致肩部受伤。随后，该行人就其膝盖和肩部的伤害对司机提起了诉讼。

在该行人对司机的诉讼中，行人可以就哪些伤害获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 就其膝盖和肩部的伤害，因为司机须接受受害者的既有状况。
zh-choices.B: 就其膝盖和肩部的伤害，如果陪审团认定行人从楼梯上摔下是其最初伤害的正常后果。
zh-choices.C: 仅就其膝盖的伤害，因为行人肩部的伤害是可分割的。
zh-choices.D: 仅就其膝盖的伤害，如果陪审团认定司机无法预见到其过失驾驶会导致行人从楼梯上摔下。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Damages

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：原始侵害之后，只要后续损害是该侵害的正常后果，侵权人也要赔。

三秒认题路径：

先看初始伤 → 再看后果伤 → 是否正常延伸 → 能否一起赔

核心法律规则

补偿性损害赔偿（compensatory damages）不只赔最初那一下，还赔由它自然带出来的后续伤害。正常后果（normal consequence）的意思是：后来的伤不是另起炉灶，而是前面那次侵害顺着发展出来的结果，所以也算在被告账上。

可预见性（foreseeability）主要管的是 duty 和 proximate cause，不是这里的 damages 选择题重点；本题只要抓住“后续伤是不是原始膝伤的正常后果”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 460 — 只要后续损害是初始伤害的正常后果，被告就要一起赔。

思维导图

起点：司机撞人，先有膝伤
关卡 1：膝伤是否由被告过失造成？
是 → 初始伤害先可赔
关卡 2：几个月后摔下楼梯的肩伤，和膝伤是什么关系？
如果是膝盖突然打软带来的连锁伤害，就是 正常后果（normal consequence）。
卡死点：需不需要证明“司机能预见”这一下？
不需要；这里看 damages，不看用 foreseeability 去卡肩伤。
终点：结论
膝伤 + 肩伤都能赔，对应正确选项。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：肩伤是“后来才发生的”，好像应该单独算、只能赔膝伤。

但考试真正问的是：后来的摔伤是不是前面膝伤的正常延伸；只要是连锁后果，就一起赔。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的伤有没有隔了几个月才出现」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 膝盖打软后摔下楼梯，说明肩伤可能是原始膝伤的正常后果，所以膝伤和肩伤都能赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 蛋壳规则误判

✕ A: 把 takes the victim 当成本题核心，错把易受伤体质当成正常后果。

❌ 事实误判 | 分离伤害偷换

✕ C: 说肩伤“可分离”，但这里是同一被告引发的连锁损害。

❌ 法律适用 | 可预见性错位

✕ D: 盯着 could not have foreseen，却把 duty / proximate cause 的词搬来赔偿问题。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定初始伤，再问后续伤是不是正常后果；别被可预见性带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：初始伤 + 正常后果 都能赔；只要后面的伤是前面的连锁结果，别让“时间隔了很久”骗走分数。

这题的速记就是：先问“是不是同一条伤害链”，再问“是不是正常后果”。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A pedestrian was injured when hit by a chair that was thrown from an upper-story hotel window. The pedestrian sued the occupants of all the rooms from which the chair might have been thrown.
At trial, the pedestrian has been unable to offer any evidence as to the exact room from which the chair was thrown. The defendants have filed a motion for a directed verdict.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because it is unreasonable to expect the pedestrian to prove which of the defendants caused the harm.
choices.B: No, because of the doctrine of alternative liability.
choices.C: Yes, because a plaintiff always has the burden to prove that a particular defendant's conduct was the factual cause of the plaintiff's physical harm.
choices.D: Yes, because the pedestrian has failed to offer evidence that the defendants jointly engaged in tortious conduct.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Liability of multiple negligent actors
Indivisible injuriesSeparable injuries
Acting independentlyJoint & several liability*Several liability only
Acting in concertJoint & several liability
*Default rule on MBE.

Tort claims for personal injury generally require proof that a particular defendant's tortious conduct was the actual and proximate cause of the plaintiff's harm. But when two or more defendants jointly engage in tortious conduct (ie, act in concert)—and at least one of them causes the plaintiff's harm—all of the defendants are jointly and severally liable for the harm (Choice C).

(Choice D) Here, the pedestrian was injured by a chair that was thrown from a hotel window. She then sued the occupants of all the rooms from which it might have been thrown. Since she offered no evidence as to the exact room from which the chair was thrown, she cannot prove which defendant(s) caused her injury. And since she also offered no evidence of joint tortious conduct, the defendants' motion for a directed verdict should be granted.

(Choices A & B) The doctrine of alternative liability applies when (1) there were multiple tortfeasors, (2) at least one of them caused the plaintiff's harm, and (3) it is impossible to tell which one of them did. The burden then shifts to each defendant to prove that he/she did not cause the harm. Here, it may be unreasonable to expect the pedestrian to prove which defendant caused her harm. But alternative liability only applies if each defendant's tortious conduct is proved (not seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

When multiple defendants engage in joint tortious conduct and one or more of them causes the plaintiff's harm, all of the defendants are jointly and severally liable for the harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 876 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a defendant is subject to liability if he/she does a tortious act in concert with others or pursuant to a common design).
questions.zh-question:
一名行人被一把从酒店楼上窗户扔下的椅子砸伤。该行人起诉了所有可能扔下椅子的房间的住客。

在庭审中，该行人未能提供任何证据证明椅子是从哪个确切的房间扔下的。被告已申请作出指示裁决。

法院应否批准该动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为期望行人证明是哪名被告造成了损害是不合理的。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为存在择一责任原则。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为原告始终负有举证责任，以证明某一特定被告的行为是造成其身体伤害的事实原因。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，因为行人未能提供证据证明被告共同实施了侵权行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Sharing Liability Among Multiple Defendants

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多个被告里，只有在能证明他们共同实施侵权行为（acting in concert / joint tortious conduct）时，才会一起承担连带责任；单纯“找不到到底是谁扔的”，还不够。

三秒认题路径：

找不到凶手 → 看是否共同行为 → 没有共同侵权 → 原告举证失败 → 直接判被告胜

核心法律规则

实际原因（actual cause）和近因（proximate cause）通常要落到“某一个被告”头上，所以原告一般要证明是谁造成了伤害。

但如果多个被告协同行为（acting in concert），也就是一起做了侵权事，且其中至少一人造成了损害，大家就可能一起承担连带责任（joint and several liability）。

这题里，原告只说“可能是这些房间里的某个人”，却没有证据证明他们有共同设计或共同作案，所以规则走不到连带责任那一步。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Torts § 876 — 共同设计或协同行为成立时，才会把责任一起压到多个被告身上。

思维导图

先看：能不能把伤害归到“某一个被告”身上？
能走普通举证：证明该被告的侵权行为是伤害原因。
不能再问：有没有共同侵权（joint tortious conduct）？
有共同设计或协同行为？
有→ 多被告都可能连带责任（joint and several liability）
没有→ 卡死点：缺少共同侵权，不能把“找不到谁干的”自动变成被告输
本题结论原告没证据证明共同侵权，也没证据锁定具体肇事者 → 被告的 directed verdict 成立

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然原告根本不知道是哪一个房间扔的，法院就应该帮她把责任摊到所有可疑被告身上。

但考试真正问的是：这些被告有没有被证明是一起干的；没有共同侵权（joint tortious conduct），就不能直接上连带责任。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只说椅子可能来自多个房间，却没有任何共同侵权证据；原告既没锁定具体加害人，也没法把多人一起拖进连带责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 举证转移误判

✕ A: 以为“难证明”就能自动赢，其实还没到转移举证责任那一步。

❌ 法律适用 | 共同侵权错套

✕ B: 把 alternative liability 硬套进来，但题干没证明每个被告都实施了可归责的侵权行为。

❌ 事实误判 | 绝对化举证责任

✕ C: “永远都要锁定某一人”说太满了；本题输在原告没有共同侵权证据。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“找不到谁干的”还是“能不能把多人一起算作共同作案”。

考场速记

记住一句：找不到凶手不等于自动连带责任；先看有没有共同侵权（acting in concert），没有就别把所有被告一起判输。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A student had weekly sessions with a psychotherapist. During every session, the student would tell the psychotherapist that he was convinced that his roommate was impersonating him and slowly trying to take over his life. For the past several weeks, the student had become more and more agitated when speaking about the roommate, and at their most recent session, the student told the psychotherapist about his plans to kill the roommate. The student explained to her that he had not quite figured out how he was going to carry out his plan, but that he planned to kill the roommate before the upcoming winter break.
A statute in the jurisdiction imposes an affirmative duty to act "for the protection of another whom the individual has found in peril."
Is the psychotherapist under a legal duty to warn the roommate?

choices.A: No, because the psychotherapist has no affirmative duty to act.
choices.B: No, because the student's threats of future harm do not put the roommate in imminent danger.
choices.C: Yes, because the student has made credible threats of physical violence against the roommate.
choices.D: Yes, because under the statute, the psychotherapist has an affirmative duty to act.

By contract Duty to use care when performing contractual obligations
By authority Duty to exercise reasonable control over third party whom defendant has actual ability & authority to control
• Examples: parent over child, custodian over person in custody, employer over employee, mental-health professional over patient
By relationship Duty to protect, aid, or assist plaintiff with whom defendant shares unique relationship
• Examples: business proprietor with patron, common carrier with passenger, innkeeper with guest, employer with employee, parent with child
By statute Statute imposes obligation to act for another's protection
Land possessor Duty to mitigate risks posed by natural or artificial conditions on land

A person generally has no duty to control another unless the parties share a special relationship. Mental-health professionals share a special relationship with their patients, so they have a duty to use reasonable care to identify dangerous patients and mitigate the risks they pose to others. So when a patient makes a credible threat of physical violence against an ascertainable victim, the mental-health professional has a duty to warn the would-be victim or take other steps to mitigate the risk posed by the patient (eg, notify law enforcement).

Here, the student told the psychotherapist that he planned to kill his roommate before the upcoming winter break. This was a credible threat of physical violence, especially since the student had become increasingly agitated when speaking to the psychotherapist about the roommate over the past several weeks. And because of the psychotherapist's special relationship with the student, he has a legal duty to warn the roommate of the student's plan. (Choice A)

*Whether a threat of physical violence is credible is determined by the objective standard of a reasonable mental-health professional in the same circumstance.

(Choice B) Threats of future harm do not put others in apprehension of imminent danger and therefore cannot support a claim for assault. But imminence is irrelevant in determining whether a mental-health professional's duty to warn has attached.

(Choice D) The psychotherapist's duty to warn the roommate arises from the psychotherapist's special relationship with the student who poses a risk of harm to the roommate—not from the jurisdiction's statute. Additionally, it is unclear whether the statute would even apply here since the psychotherapist did not necessarily "find the roommate in peril."

Educational objective:

A special relationship exists between mental-health professionals and their patients. Therefore, if a patient makes a credible threat of physical violence against an ascertainable victim, the mental-health professional must warn the would-be victim of the risk posed by the patient or take other steps to mitigate that risk.

References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 41 (Am. Law Inst. 2010) (duty to third parties based on special relationship with person posing risks).
questions.zh-question:
一名学生每周都与一位心理治疗师进行会谈。在每次会谈中，该学生都会告诉心理治疗师，他确信其室友正在冒充他，并试图慢慢接管他的生活。在过去的几周里，该学生在谈论其室友时变得越来越激动。在最近的一次会谈中，该学生告诉心理治疗师他计划杀死其室友。该学生向她解释说，他还没有完全想好如何实施该计划，但他计划在即将到来的寒假前杀死其室友。

该司法管辖区的一项法规规定了心理治疗师有积极作为的义务，“为保护个人发现处于危险中的他人”而采取行动。

该心理治疗师是否有法律义务警告其室友？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该心理治疗师没有积极作为的义务。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该学生对未来伤害的威胁并未使其室友处于迫在眉睫的危险之中。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为根据该法规，该心理治疗师有积极作为的义务。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为根据普通法，当存在可信威胁时，特殊关系会创设警告义务。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Torts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：心理健康专业人员面对患者对可识别第三人发出的可信暴力威胁时，是否负有警告义务。

三秒认题路径：

心理咨询师 → 可信杀人威胁 → 可识别受害人 → 特殊关系 → 要警告

核心法律规则

只记本题会用到的规则

一般人对他人没有主动控制义务；但特殊关系（special relationship）会把义务打开。心理健康专业人员对患者有义务用合理注意识别危险患者，并采取合理措施降低对他人的风险。

如果患者对一个可识别受害人（ascertainable victim）发出可信的身体暴力威胁（credible threat of physical violence），考场意思：这时不是“要不要劝劝他”，而是“要不要警告目标对象或通知执法机关”。

这里的关键不是威胁是否已经立刻要发生，而是专业人员是否已经看见了足够真实的危险信号。只要威胁可信，警告义务就可能成立。

核心判例：Restatement (Third) of Torts § 41 — 这种“对第三人发出的风险”通常来自对施险者的特殊关系，而不是一般性旁观义务。

思维导图

先看：心理健康专业人员和患者之间有没有特殊关系？
YES有，患者关系会打开对第三人的保护义务。
再看：患者是不是对明确对象发出可信暴力威胁？
YES学生说要在寒假前杀掉室友，且近几周越来越激动。
最后卡死：能不能等到事后再说？
不能只等“事后补救”——此时应警告室友或采取其他减险措施。
结论
答案有警告义务，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：威胁还没马上发生，所以不算“紧急危险”，也就不用警告。

但考试真正问的是：心理健康专业人员看到可信暴力风险后，能不能立刻采取保护第三人的措施。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

别被“未来才动手”带偏；这里不要求像 assault 那样的立即性，只看威胁是否可信、受害人是否可识别。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 planned to kill the roommate 加上持续激化的表现，已经足够构成可信暴力威胁，所以心理治疗师应警告可识别的室友。

❌ 概念混淆 | 义务来源误判

✕ A: 把“无一般义务”偷换成“完全没义务”，忽略了特殊关系。

❌ 法律适用 | 紧迫性误判

✕ B: 把 imminent danger 当成门槛，但这里看的是可信威胁，不是即时袭击。

❌ 事实误判 | 法条来源偷换

✕ D: 只盯着 statute，却忽略题干真正给的是患者风险与特殊关系。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“特殊关系+可信暴力威胁”，再判断是否需要对可识别第三人采取警告或减险措施。

考场速记

记住这句：患者对明确对象发出可信暴力威胁时，精神健康专业人员不是等出事，而是要先警告、再减险。

速记口诀：special relationship + credible threat = warn the target。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A door attendant at a downtown hotel also served as the hotel's security guard. He regularly exchanged greetings with a woman who passed the hotel on her way to and from work. One day, the attendant saw a first-time hotel guest exit the hotel and proceed down the street behind the woman. Just after the two left the hotel's property, the attendant observed the guest reach into the woman's purse and remove her wallet. The attendant later confessed to the woman that he had failed to act despite seeing the guest take the wallet.
The woman has brought a negligence action against the hotel to recover the money taken from her by the guest.
Which of the following best describes the standard by which the attendant's conduct as an employee of the hotel should be judged in this matter?

choices.A: As a security guard employed by an innkeeper, the attendant had a duty to prevent the hotel guest from harming the woman.
choices.B: As an employee of a business with no special relationship with the woman, the attendant was not under an affirmative duty to act.
choices.C: As an employee of a property owner, the attendant had a duty to warn the woman of the concealed danger that the pickpocketing guest presented.
choices.D: As an employee of an innkeeper, the attendant was required to act with the highest degree of care with regard to the woman and is responsible for even slight negligence.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Special relationships
imposing duty to protect others
  • Parent/child
  • Hospital/patient
  • Employer/employees
  • Shopkeeper/business invitees
  • Common carrier/passengers
  • Custodian/person in custody
  • Innkeeper/guests
Mnemonic: Please Help Eliminate Safety Concerns Causing Injuries

A person generally has no duty to protect another from harm. However, a person in a special relationship with another may have an affirmative duty to use reasonable care to protect the other from harm arising within the scope of that relationship. For example, an innkeeper has a duty to use reasonable care to protect its guests while they are on the premises.

Here, the hotel (innkeeper) did not have a special relationship with the woman, who was merely a passersby and not a guest at the hotel. Consequently, neither the hotel nor its employees had an affirmative duty to protect her from the pickpocketing guest. Therefore, the attendant's conduct as an employee of the hotel should be judged by this standard.

(Choice A) A person with the actual ability and authority to control another may have a duty to use reasonable care to prevent that person from injuring others.* But here, even as the hotel's security guard, the attendant had no control over a hotel guest off the premises.

*This duty generally is only imposed if the person in control knows or should know that the other is likely to commit the injuring act. And here, the attendant had no reason to know that the first-time guest was a pickpocket.

(Choice C) Property owners (the hotel) generally owe no duty to persons off the premises (the woman) unless the owner or someone under his/her control conducts an activity on the premises that poses an unreasonable risk of harm to persons off the premises. Here, the pickpocketing guest was not under the hotel's control and did not act on the hotel's premises.

(Choice D) At common law, innkeepers and their employees owed the highest duty of care to their guests and could be liable for even slight negligence. But here, the woman was not the hotel's guest. And even if she were, most courts today hold that an innkeeper and its employees are liable only for ordinary negligence.

📌 Educational Objective

A person in a special relationship with another (eg, an innkeeper with its guests) has a duty to use reasonable care to protect the other from harm arising within the scope of that relationship.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Phys. & Emot. Harm § 40 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (duty based on special relationship).

市中心一家酒店的门童也兼任酒店的保安。他经常与一位上下班路过酒店的女士打招呼。一天，该门童看到一位首次入住的酒店客人走出酒店，跟在该女士身后走在街上。就在两人离开酒店物业范围后，门童看到该客人伸手进该女士的手提包并取走了她的钱包。该门童后来向该女士承认，尽管他看到了客人拿走钱包，但他没有采取任何行动。

该女士已对酒店提起过失之诉，要求追回被客人拿走的钱款。

在此事中，以下哪项最能描述该门童作为酒店雇员的行为应依据的标准？

zh-choices.A: 作为旅店经营者雇佣的保安，该门童有责任防止酒店客人伤害该女士。
zh-choices.B: 作为与该女士没有特殊关系的企业雇员，该门童没有积极作为义务。
zh-choices.C: 作为物业所有人的雇员，该门童有责任就扒手客人所构成的隐藏危险向该女士发出警告。
zh-choices.D: 作为旅店经营者的雇员，该门童被要求以最高程度的注意义务对待该女士，并且即便有轻微过失也应承担责任。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Duty

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：酒店员工看到门外路人被陌生客人偷钱包时，侵权法上的注意义务（duty）有没有成立。

三秒认题路径：

路人受害 → 酒店外 → 无特定关系 → 无积极救助义务 → 选 B

核心法律规则

一般来说，注意义务（duty）不会自动要求你去保护别人的安全。只有在特殊关系（special relationship）里，才会出现积极义务：比如 innkeeper/guest、hospital/patient、parent/child、employer/employee。

考试上只看一件事：被告和受害人之间有没有这种关系。这里受害人只是路过酒店的行人，不是酒店客人，所以酒店和员工对她没有“必须出手保护”的义务。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Phys. & Emot. Harm § 40 —— 特殊关系才会把“可不管”变成“必须合理保护”。

思维导图

先问：酒店对这个女人有没有 特殊关系（special relationship）？
NO她只是路过街上的行人，不是酒店客人。
卡死结论：没有积极保护义务（no affirmative duty）
所以员工“没出手”不能直接按 duty 违背来定责。
再看干扰选项：看到客人偷窃，就能把酒店硬说成“必须控制第三人”吗？
NO客人离开酒店范围后，酒店对他没有可执行控制权。
因此不是“谁都要防”，而是先找受害人是否落入关系保护圈。
最终答案：B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然员工亲眼看见偷窃，就应该负责阻止。

但考试真正问的是：酒店对这个路人有没有法律上的积极义务，不是看你事后觉得“应该帮忙”。

这道题最容易把“看见坏事”误当成“必须救人”，可 duty 先看关系，再看行为。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干路人不是酒店客人，酒店和员工都不在特殊关系里，所以没有对她的积极保护义务。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 security guard 直接当成对路人有保护义务。

❌ 事实误判 | 题外控制偷换

✕ C: 把酒店对场外行人的义务夸大成对所有危险都要警告。

❌ 法律适用 | 高度注意误套

✕ D: 把 highest degree 硬套给非住客。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定受害人身份，再查有没有特殊关系；没有关系就没有积极保护义务。

考场速记

记住一句：特殊关系（special relationship） 才会把“旁观者”变成“必须保护的人”。本题口诀可记成 Please Help Eliminate Safety Concerns Causing Injuries，也就是亲子、医患、雇佣、店主-顾客、承运人、看管人、旅馆-住客。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
When a tire of a motorist's car suffered a blowout, the car rolled over and the motorist was badly injured. Vehicles made by the manufacturer of the motorist's car have been found to be negligently designed, making them dangerously prone to rolling over when they suffer blowouts. A truck driver who was driving behind the motorist when the accident occurred stopped to help. Rescue vehicles promptly arrived, and the truck driver walked along the side of the road to return to his truck. As he approached his truck, he was struck and injured by a speeding car. The truck driver has sued the manufacturer of the injured motorist's car.
Is the truck driver likely to prevail in a suit against the car manufacturer?

choices.A: No, because the car manufacturer's negligence was not the proximate cause of the truck driver's injuries.
choices.B: No, because the truck driver assumed the risk of injury when he undertook to help the motorist.
choices.C: Yes, because it is foreseeable that injuries can result from rollovers.
choices.D: Yes, because the car manufacturer's negligence caused the dangerous situation that invited the rescue by the truck driver.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Actual & proximate causation
(rescue doctrine)

In a negligence suit, the plaintiff must prove actual and proximate cause. Proximate cause is satisfied when the plaintiff's harm was a foreseeable consequence of the defendant's negligence. And when a defendant negligently endangers him/herself or others, the law deems it foreseeable that someone will be injured in a rescue attempt. As a result, a plaintiff can recover for negligence under the rescue doctrine if:

  • the plaintiff was injured while attempting to rescue another and
  • that person's peril was caused by the defendant's negligence.

Here, the motorist was badly injured when his car suffered a blowout and rolled over. The car manufacturer's negligent design made the car dangerously prone to this type of accident, thereby causing the motorist's peril and inviting rescue by another. The truck driver, who had stopped to help the motorist, was then struck and injured by a speeding car. Since injury to rescuers is sufficiently foreseeable to satisfy proximate cause, the truck driver will likely prevail in a suit against the manufacturer (Choice A).

(Choice B) A rescuer does not assume the risk of injury by undertaking a rescue attempt unless he/she (1) knew the rescue attempt was dangerous and (2) could have proceeded in a reasonable alternative manner. Here, there is no indication that the truck driver had a reasonable alternative. And even if he did, this would merely reduce (not bar) his recovery in most jurisdictions.

(Choice C) Although it is foreseeable that injuries can result from rollovers, the truck driver cannot prevail unless the also shows that the defendant's negligence caused the motorist's peril.

Educational objective:
Injuries to rescuers are sufficiently foreseeable to satisfy proximate cause. As a result, a rescuer can recover for negligence if (1) he/she was injured while attempting to rescue another and (2) that person's peril was caused by the defendant's negligence.

References

Restatement (Second) of Torts § 294 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a defendant's conduct may be negligent to a potential rescuer even though that conduct poses no direct risk to the rescuer.)
questions.zh-question:
一名驾驶者的汽车爆胎后，车辆翻滚，驾驶者严重受伤。该驾驶者车辆的制造商所生产的车辆被认定存在过失设计，导致其在爆胎时有危险的翻滚倾向。事故发生时，一名跟在驾驶者后面的卡车司机停车施救。救援车辆迅速抵达后，该卡车司机沿路边走回自己的卡车。在他走近卡车时，被一辆超速行驶的汽车撞伤。该卡车司机起诉了受伤驾驶者车辆的制造商。

卡车司机对该汽车制造商提起的诉讼是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为汽车制造商的过失并非卡车司机受伤的近因（proximate cause）。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为卡车司机在对驾驶者进行施救时自愿承担了受伤的风险（assumed the risk）。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为车辆翻滚可能导致伤害是可预见的。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为汽车制造商的过失造成了危险情境，从而引致了卡车司机的施救行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Causation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：救援规则（rescue doctrine）下，救援者受伤时，原始被告的疏忽是否仍构成近因（proximate cause）。

三秒认题路径：

救人受伤 → 找近因 → 看可预见 → 救援规则 → 选 D

核心法律规则

在过失（negligence）里，原告必须证明实际因果关系（actual cause）和近因（proximate cause）。这里的考场意思很简单：只要救援者受伤，是因为被告先前制造了一个需要救援的危险局面，法律通常就把救援者的受伤当作可预见后果。

救援规则（rescue doctrine）的关键不是“车为什么翻”，而是“被告有没有把别人推到危险里，顺手把救援者也带进风险里”。所以本题只要抓住：救援者是在救人时受伤，而且被救的人之危险是被告疏忽造成的，就能把近因接上。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 294 — 被告即使没有直接伤到救援者，也可能对潜在救援者构成过失责任。

思维导图

先问：这是不是“救援者受伤后起诉原始肇事者”的题？
YES 先看被救的人是否因被告疏忽陷入危险。
YES 再看原告是否真的是去救人，而不是路过看热闹。
YES 卡死点：近因不要求被告直接碰到救援者，只要救援受伤本身可预见。
结论 被告把人推入危险 → 也把救援风险一起放进来 → 近因成立 → 选 D。
联想 看到 rescue doctrine，脑中直接跳到：foreseeable rescuer。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：救援者最后是被speeding car撞伤，似乎和原始制造商没那么直接。

但考试真正问的是：谁把“需要救援的危险”先制造出来了；救援者的受伤只是那个危险链条里，法律本来就会预见到的一环。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里同理：看的是近因能不能接上，不是看最后一撞是不是最显眼。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 dangerously prone to rolling over 说明制造商先制造了危险局面，救援者受伤在 rescue doctrine 下可被视为可预见后果，所以能成立近因。

❌ 法律适用 | 近因误判

✕ A: 把“最后一撞”当成切断点，忽略了救援者伤害本来就可预见。

❌ 概念混淆 | 风险承担误判

✕ B: 把 assumed the risk 说成自动挡，题干根本没给自愿知险的关键信息。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看翻车后果

✕ C: 只盯着“翻车会伤人”，却漏掉必须先有被告造成被救者危险这一层。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“谁制造了危险”，再接“救援者受伤是否仍属可预见后果”。

考场速记

记住一句话：先造危险的人，通常也要预见救援者受伤。

下一次看到救援题，先问“被救的人是不是因为被告疏忽才陷入危险”，这一步过了，近因就容易接上。
