questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A saleswoman, who was driving at an excessive speed, applied her brakes to stop at a traffic light. Due to damp, fallen leaves, her car skidded and came to a halt perpendicular to the roadway. A delivery truck driver, who was also driving at an excessive speed and was immediately behind the saleswoman, saw her car perpendicular to the roadway. Although the truck driver had sufficient distance to come to a slow, controlled stop, he decided not to slow down but, rather, to swerve to the left in an effort to go around the saleswoman's car. Due to oncoming traffic, the space was insufficient and the delivery truck collided with the car, severely injuring the saleswoman.
The saleswoman filed a personal injury action against the truck driver in a jurisdiction in which contributory negligence is a bar to recovery.
Will the saleswoman prevail?

choices.A: No, if the jury finds that, in speeding, the saleswoman assumed the risk.
choices.B: No, if the jury finds that the saleswoman's conduct was in any way a legal cause of the accident.
choices.C: Yes, if the jury finds that the truck driver had the last clear chance.
choices.D: Yes, if the jury finds that the truck driver was more than 50% at fault.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Contributory negligence
(traditional common law)
General rulePlaintiff's negligence completely bars recovery
Exception
(last clear chance)		Recovery permitted if defendant:
• had last clear chance to avoid plaintiff's injury and
• failed to use reasonable care to do so

In this jurisdiction and at common law, the plaintiff's contributory negligence, ie, failure to use reasonable care for his/her own safety—is a complete bar to recovery. This is a harsh rule for plaintiffs because it ignores any negligence by the defendant. To mitigate this harshness, courts recognize an exception called the last-clear-chance rule. This rule allows a contributorily negligent plaintiff to recover if the defendant (1) had the last clear chance to avoid the plaintiff's injury but (2) failed to use reasonable care to do so.

Here, the saleswoman's negligent, excessive speeding caused her car to skid and stop in the roadway. The truck driver saw this and had sufficient distance to come to a slow, controlled stop (last clear chance). Instead, he decided to swerve in an effort to go around her car (failure to use reasonable care). As a result, the saleswoman will likely prevail in her personal injury action against the truck driver.

(Choice A) Assumption of the risk is a defense to negligence when the plaintiff voluntarily exposed him/herself to a known risk of harm. Here, although the saleswoman voluntarily exposed herself to the risks of her own excessive speeding, she did not voluntarily expose herself to the truck driver's negligence.

(Choice B) The saleswoman's conduct may have been a legal (ie, proximate cause of the accident if it was a foreseeable consequence of her excessive speed. But this would not preclude her recovery since the accident was also a foreseeable consequence of the truck driver's negligence and he had the last clear chance.

(Choice D) Had this been a modified comparative negligence jurisdiction, the saleswoman's (plaintiff's) negligence would completely bar recovery unless the truck driver (defendant) was more than 50% at fault. But comparative fault is irrelevant in this traditional contributory negligence jurisdiction.

📌 Educational Objective

The last-clear-chance rule allows a plaintiff to recover despite his/her contributory negligence if the defendant (1) had the last clear chance to avoid the plaintiff's injury and (2) failed to use reasonable care to do so.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 479–80 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a contributorily negligent plaintiff can still recover if the defendant had the last clear chance to avoid the plaintiff's harm).
questions.zh-question:
一名女销售员超速驾驶，在交通灯前刹车试图停车。由于路面有潮湿的落叶，她的车发生侧滑，最终横停在车道上。一名同样在超速驾驶并紧随其后的送货卡车司机，看到了她横停在路上的车。尽管该卡车司机有足够的距离可以缓慢、有控制地停车，但他决定不减速，而是向左急转，试图绕过女销售员的车。由于对向有来车，空间不足，送货卡车与轿车相撞，导致女销售员严重受伤。

女销售员在一个将与有过失（contributory negligence）作为赔偿绝对障碍的司法管辖区，对卡车司机提起了人身伤害诉讼。

女销售员会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，如果陪审团认定女销售员在超速驾驶时自负了风险。
zh-choices.B: 不会，如果陪审团认定女销售员的行为在任何程度上是事故的法律原因。
zh-choices.C: 会，如果陪审团认定卡车司机拥有最后明显机会。
zh-choices.D: 会，如果陪审团认定卡车司机的过错超过50%。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：传统 共同过失（contributory negligence） 之下，原告虽然自己也有过失，但如果被告已经有 最后清楚机会（last clear chance） 仍未合理避险，原告还能不能赢。

三秒认题路径：

共同过失 → 原告也错 → 被告看见了 → 还能避开 → 最后清楚机会

核心法律规则

先记规则，再看这题怎么落地

共同过失（contributory negligence） 的考场意思：原告自己只要有过失，通常就直接被挡在门外，不能恢复赔偿。

最后清楚机会（last clear chance） 的考场意思：如果被告后来还有最后一次真正能避开伤害的机会，却没用合理注意，就能把原告从“全输”里拉回来。

所以这题不看谁先开始犯错，而看 卡死前的最后一步 是谁还来得及刹车。这里卡死点在于：卡车司机看见车已横在路上，明明能慢慢停下，却选择绕行，正好踩中例外。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts §§ 479–80 的规则就是：原告有过失也不一定死局，只要被告有最后清楚机会却没合理避免，原告仍可恢复。

思维导图

先问：原告的过失是不是在传统 共同过失（contributory negligence） 体系里，已经会把案子直接打死？
YES原告超速，自己先有过失，默认不能赔。
下一关被告有没有 最后清楚机会（last clear chance）？
本题事实卡车司机看见横着停的车，距离足够，能慢慢停下。
卡死点：他没刹车，反而硬绕，说明有机会却没合理避险。
结论例外成立，原告仍可恢复赔偿。
答案走向：C Yes, if the truck driver had the last clear chance.

考点陷阱

你可能会想：原告自己也超速，既然有过失，应该直接输。

但考试真正问的是：被告后来有没有更好的逃生窗口，明明能停却没停。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的事故已经发生了没有」。 这题不是在比谁更坏，而是在找“最后还来得及的人”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干关键是 卡车司机看见了横停车辆，而且本来能慢停，却改选绕行；这正是 最后清楚机会（last clear chance），能把原告的共同过失挡板掀开。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 assumed the risk 套进来，混成“自找风险”了。

❌ 法律适用 | 因果误判

✕ B: 盯着 legal cause 就以为原告一有因果就必输。

❌ 事实误判 | 过失比例偷换

✕ D: 把 more than 50% 的比较过失规则硬搬来。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定过失制度是传统共同过失，再只查“被告最后有没有机会刹住”。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“原告先错不一定死，被告最后能救却不救，才是 last clear chance。”

这类题先看 共同过失（contributory negligence），再问有没有 最后清楚机会（last clear chance）；只要被告有最后一次合理避险窗口，原告就可能翻盘。

reason.zh: 表明卡车司机未合理利用最后机会停车。

reason.zh: 确立女销售员自身过失，否则将阻却其赔偿请求。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man suffered from a serious, though not immediately life-threatening, impairment of his circulatory system. The man's cardiologist recommended a cardiac bypass operation and referred the man to a cardiothoracic surgeon. The surgeon did not inform the man of the 2% risk of death associated with this operation. The surgeon defended this decision based on his best personal judgment that "the man was a worrier and it would have significantly lessened his chances of survival to be worried about the nonsurvival rate."
After obtaining the patient's consent, the surgeon successfully performed the bypass operation and the man made a good recovery. However, when the man learned of the 2% risk of death associated with the operation, he was furious that the surgeon had failed to disclose this information to him. The man would have refused the operation had he been informed of the risk.
If the man asserts a claim against the surgeon based on negligence, will the man prevail?

choices.A: No, because the operation was successful, and the man suffered no harm.
choices.B: No, because the surgeon used his best personal judgment in shielding the man from the risk statistic.
choices.C: Yes, because a patient must be told the risk factor associated with a surgical procedure to give an informed consent.
choices.D: Yes, because the man would have refused the operation had he been informed of the risk.

questions.explanation:
Tort liability under informed-consent doctrine
Negligence
Did physician fail to disclose risk of treatment or procedure to patient?
Yes
Was there a duty to disclose?
Duty exists unless:
• risk commonly known
• patient unconscious or otherwise incapable of giving consent
• patient waived right to information or
• disclosure threatened patient’s well-being.

Physicians have a duty to disclose the risks of a medical treatment or procedure to a patient so that the patient can give informed consent to the treatment or procedure. In most jurisdictions, the required level of disclosure of risks is governed by custom among physicians. Failure to make the required disclosure subjects the physician to negligence liability when:

  • the failure to disclose caused the patient to consent to the treatment or procedure (ie, the patient would not have done so had the risk been disclosed) and
  • the undisclosed risk materialized and caused the plaintiff physical harm.

Here, the surgeon failed to inform the man of the 2% risk of death associated with the operation before performing it. The man likely needed to be told of this risk to give informed consent, and he would have refused the operation had he been so informed. But since the surgery was successful and the man suffered no harm, he will not prevail in a negligence suit against the surgeon.

A “significant minority” holds that the physician must disclose “material risks.” A material risk is one that a reasonable person in the patient’s position would consider when deciding whether to undergo the treatment or procedure.

In contrast, failure to obtain the patient’s consent to a treatment or procedure may subject the physician to battery liability.

(Choice B) A physician has no duty to disclose a risk when the physician reasonably believes that disclosure would threaten a patient’s well-being. However, that belief must be based on the sound medical judgment—not the physician’s best personal judgment (as seen here).

Educational objective:

Under the informed-consent doctrine, a physician who fails to disclose the risks of a medical treatment or procedure to a patient is liable for negligence if (1) the failure to disclose caused the patient to consent and (2) the undisclosed risk materialized and resulted in physical harm.

📚 References
  • Canterbury v. Spence, 464 F.2d 772, 790 (D.C. Cir. 1972) (establishing that negligence based on informed-consent doctrine requires that the patient suffer physical harm).
  • 61 Am. Jur. 2d Physicians, Surgeons, and Other Healers § 167 (2020) (discussing the informed-consent doctrine).

一名男子患有严重的循环系统障碍，但没有立即危及生命。该男子的心脏病专家建议进行心脏搭桥手术，并将他转诊给一位心胸外科医生。该外科医生没有告知该男子此项手术有2%的死亡风险。该外科医生为自己的决定辩护，称其基于他个人最佳判断，认为“该男子是个容易忧虑的人，如果让他担心存活率，会显著降低他的生存机会。”

在获得患者同意后，该外科医生成功地进行了搭桥手术，该男子恢复良好。然而，当该男子得知手术存在2%的死亡风险时，他对外科医生未能向他披露此信息感到非常愤怒。如果被告知该风险，该男子本会拒绝该手术。

如果该男子以过失为由向该外科医生提出索赔，他会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为手术很成功，且该男子没有遭受任何损害。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该外科医生运用其个人最佳判断，未告知该男子风险统计数据。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为为了作出知情同意，患者必须被告知与外科手术相关的风险因素。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为如果该男子被告知风险，他本会拒绝手术。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Informed consent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：医生没告知手术风险后，病人即使事后说“我会拒绝”，也必须再看 未披露风险（undisclosed risk） 是否真的造成了身体损害（physical harm），否则不能赢过失。

三秒认题路径：

未告知风险 → 已同意手术 → 手术成功 → 没有伤害 → 不成立过失

核心法律规则

在知情同意（informed consent）题里，医生通常要披露重大风险（material risk），考场意思：让病人自己决定要不要做手术。若医生故意不披露，只有在这两个点都成立时才会构成过失（negligence）：第一，隐瞒真的让病人同意了；第二，没说出的那个风险后来真的发生，并造成身体损害。

所以，本题里病人虽然会因“2%死亡风险”而拒绝手术，但手术成功、没有受伤，考试上就卡在第二步：physical harm 没有发生，过失赔偿就断掉了。

核心判例： Canterbury v. Spence — 确立知情同意下，隐瞒风险要想成立过失，必须有实际身体伤害。

思维导图

先看：医生有没有隐瞒手术风险？
有 进入知情同意审查，不是普通“同不同意”这么简单。
再看 病人是否因隐瞒而做了手术？
如果知道 2% 死亡风险，会拒绝吗？
会拒绝 说明隐瞒确实影响了同意决定。
最后一关：未披露的风险有没有真的造成身体损害？
这里被卡死：手术成功、无伤害 → effectively reviewable 不是问题，本题是“没有损害”
没有 直接结论： 不能靠过失获赔，选“否”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然病人说“早知道就不做了”，那医生应该负责。
但考试真正问的是：法律程序上能不能救济，而不是物理上的秘密有没有泄露。

这题最容易被“would have refused”骗走；它只说明同意被影响了，还不够，你还要看到未披露风险真的落到病人身上并造成伤害。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 手术成功、病人无伤害 是关键，知情同意下即使隐瞒影响了同意，过失仍要等未披露风险造成身体损害才成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把 best personal judgment 当成免责理由。

❌ 法律适用 | 重大风险泛化

✕ C: 只背“要披露风险”却漏掉还要有实际伤害。

❌ 事实误判 | 拒绝意愿夸大

✕ D: 只抓住 would have refused，忽略了本题没受伤。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有实际伤害”，再看隐瞒是否真的改变了同意。

考场速记

记住一句：知情同意不是只看“没告诉”，而是要看“没告诉 + 真的受伤”。这题一旦没有身体损害，答案就回到“否”。

reason.en: The undisclosed risk that must materialize to support negligence liability.
reason.zh: 未披露且须实际发生方能支持过失责任的风险。

reason.en: Establishes breach of the informed-consent disclosure duty.
reason.zh: 表明违反知情同意披露义务。

reason.en: Shows the undisclosed risk never materialized into injury.
reason.zh: 表明未披露风险未转化为实际身体伤害。

reason.en: Satisfies causation that disclosure would have changed consent.
reason.zh: 满足若披露则会改变同意的因果关系要件。

reason.en: Triggers the informed-consent negligence framework, not battery.
reason.zh: 适用知情同意过失责任框架，而非殴打。

reason.en: Correctly identifies the missing harm element for negligence liability.
reason.zh: 正确指出过失责任所缺的身体损害要件。

reason.zh: 误将个人判断当作有效的医疗不披露例外。

reason.zh: 只强调披露义务，忽略须发生的身体损害。

reason.zh: 陈述真实义务但遗漏过失赔偿的损害要件。

reason.en: Establishes breach of the physician's informed-consent disclosure duty.
reason.zh: 确立医师违反知情同意披露义务。

highlights.text: successfully performed the bypass operation and the man made a good recovery

reason.zh: 手术成功表明未披露风险未造成身体损害。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A schizophrenic patient who was institutionalized in a psychiatric facility pushed a nurse down a stairwell at the facility. The nurse, a paid employee of the facility who was trained to care for schizophrenic patients, was injured. The patient is an indigent whose care is paid for by the government.
The jurisdiction generally follows the rule that a person with a mental deficiency is held to the standard of a reasonable person. In a negligence action brought by the nurse against the patient, the patient's lawyer will argue that the patient should not be held responsible for the nurse's injury.
Which of the following facts will be LEAST helpful to the patient's lawyer's argument?

choices.A: At the time she pushed the nurse, the patient thought she was being attacked by an elephant.
choices.B: The nurse was a professional caregiver.
choices.C: The nurse was trained to care for patients with schizophrenia.
choices.D: The patient is an indigent whose care is paid for by the government.

questions.explanation:
Assumption of the risk
(voluntary exposure to known risk of harm)
Traditional contributory negligence • Bars plaintiff's recovery
Pure comparative negligence* • Majority view: Reduces recovery by plaintiff's proportionate share of fault
• Minority view: Bars plaintiff's recovery

*Default rule on MBE.

In this jurisdiction, persons with mental deficiencies (eg. schizophrenia) are held to the standard of care of a reasonable person, which means that mental deficiency is not a defense to negligence. But in pure comparative negligence jurisdictions (default rule on the MBE), assumption of the risk is a defense that can either reduce (majority view) or bar (minority view) the plaintiff's recovery. This defense applies if the plaintiff:

  • knew about the risk of harm (eg. based on prior training or experience) and
  • voluntarily accepted that risk (eg. by agreeing to confront the risk for compensation).

Here, the schizophrenic patient pushed the nurse down a stairwell, and the nurse sued the patient for negligence. But the nurse should have known about this risk since he was a professional caregiver trained to care for patients with schizophrenia (Choices B & C). And by agreeing to work at a psychiatric facility, the nurse voluntarily accepted the risks posed by hallucinating patients (Choice A). Therefore, these arguments are helpful to establishing assumption of the risk, which would reduce or negate the patient's responsibility for the nurse's injury.

However, inability to pay is never a defense to tort liability. As a result, the patient's least helpful argument is that she is an indigent whose care is paid for by the government.

📌 Educational Objective

Assumption of the risk is a defense to negligence that either reduces or bars recovery if the plaintiff knew about and voluntarily accepted the risk that caused that plaintiff's harm. But inability to pay is never a defense to tort liability.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 496C (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a plaintiff cannot recover for negligence when he/she fully understood and voluntarily confronted a risk).

一名被收治于某精神病治疗机构的精神分裂症患者，在该机构将一名护士推下楼梯井。该护士是该机构的受薪雇员，曾受过照顾精神分裂症患者的培训，并在事件中受伤。该患者是一名贫困者，其医疗费用由政府支付。

该司法管辖区通常遵循的规则是，有精神缺陷的人应被要求遵守理性人的标准。在护士对患者提起的过失诉讼中，患者的律师将主张患者不应对护士的伤害负责。

以下哪一项事实对患者律师的论点最没有帮助？

zh-choices.A: 在推护士的时候，患者认为自己正在被一头大象攻击。
zh-choices.B: 该护士是一名专业护理人员。
zh-choices.C: 该护士曾受过照顾精神分裂症患者的培训。
zh-choices.D: 该患者是一名贫困者，其医疗费用由政府支付。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Defenses to negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告能否用 已知风险自愿承担（assumption of the risk） 来减轻或阻却责任，而不是拿“没钱付赔偿”当抗辩。

三秒认题路径：

精神缺陷 → 仍按理性人 → 已知且自愿 → 可用风险抗辩 → 没钱无关

核心法律规则

精神缺陷（mental deficiency）在 过失（negligence） 里通常不是抗辩，考场上还是按 理性人标准（reasonable person standard） 看。已知风险自愿承担（assumption of the risk） 的意思是：原告明知风险，还自己选择去碰这个风险，所以赔偿可以被减轻，甚至被挡掉。无法支付（inability to pay） 不是侵权责任抗辩，考试里不能因为“他穷”就免掉责任。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 496C —— 原告如果真正知道并自愿面对风险，就不能再按这个风险来要回全部赔偿。

思维导图

先看：患者的精神分裂症能不能直接当过失抗辩？
NO： 这类 精神缺陷（mental deficiency） 仍按 理性人标准（reasonable person standard） 处理，不能直接免责。
再看：护士有没有 已知风险自愿承担（assumption of the risk）？
YES： 护士是 专业护理人员，又 受训照护精神分裂患者，还主动去精神科工作，说明“知道风险 + 自愿接触风险”。
卡死点：这条路只会帮助患者减轻或阻却对护士的责任，不会给“没钱赔”开口子。
最后排除：indigent / 政府代付是否能救患者？
NO： 支付能力不是侵权抗辩。 所以正确答案就是找那个“最没用”的事实。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：患者有精神疾病，或者护士面对的是高风险病人，所以患者应该少担责。

但考试真正问的是：哪一个事实最能帮上“已知风险自愿承担”的抗辩，哪一个只是情绪上显得可怜。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里的 indigent 和 government-paid care 只是在说付不付得起钱，和能不能成立 已知风险自愿承担（assumption of the risk） 没关系。

❌ 事实误判 | 幻觉情节误读

✕ A: 把 thought she was being attacked 当成关键，其实这句更像在帮“知道风险”的方向。

❌ 概念混淆 | 职业身份当抗辩

✕ B: 只看“专业护理人员”就想跳到免责，但这反而更像原告懂风险。

❌ 法律适用 | 受训事实套错位

✕ C: 受训照护精神分裂患者更能证明 knew about the risk，不是削弱它。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找能不能做 assumption of the risk，再挑那个对这个抗辩最没帮助的事实。

考场速记

记住：精神缺陷（mental deficiency）通常不救过失，被告最该找的是“原告知险且自愿碰险”；而 没钱（inability to pay） 永远不是侵权抗辩。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man entered a drug store to make some purchases. As he was searching the aisles for various items, he noticed a display card containing automatic pencils. The display card was on a high shelf behind a cashier's counter. The man saw a sign on the counter that read, "No Admittance, Employees Only." Seeing no clerks in the vicinity to help him, the man went behind the counter to get a pencil. A clerk then appeared behind the counter and asked whether she could help him. He said he just wanted a pencil and that he could reach the display card himself. The clerk said nothing further.
While reaching for the display card, the man stepped sideways into a hidden, open shaft and fell to the basement, ten feet below. The clerk knew of the presence of the open shaft but assumed incorrectly that the man had noticed it.
The man sued the drug store to recover damages for the injuries he sustained in the fall. The jurisdiction has adopted a rule of pure comparative negligence, and it follows traditional common law rules governing the duties of a land possessor.
Will the man likely recover a judgment against the drug store?

choices.A: No, because the man was a trespasser.
choices.B: No, because the man's injuries did not result from the defendant's willful or wanton misconduct.
choices.C: Yes, because the clerk had reason to believe that the man was unaware of the open shaft.
choices.D: Yes, because the premises were defective with respect to a public invitee.

questions.explanation:
Land possessor's duty to land entrants

Invitees Inspect for unknown dangers, make safe or warn, & prevent harm from active operations
Licensees Warn of known latent defects & use reasonable care in active operations
Known or anticipated trespassers Warn of known artificial dangers & use reasonable care in active operations
Unknown or unanticipated trespassers No duty

Under the traditional common law approach, "land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to foreseeable land entrants-including invitees. But an invitee is treated as a trespasser if that person intentionally enters an area without permission. And if that person is a known or anticipated trespasser, the landowner owes a limited duty to:

  • warn the trespasser about hidden, artificial (ie, man-made) dangers that are known to the land possessor but unlikely to be discovered by the trespasser and
  • use reasonable care in active operations (ie, activities conducted on the land).

A land possessor who breaches this duty and causes the trespasser physical harm is liable for negligence. And if the land possessor is an employer, the doctrine of respondeat superior holds the land possessor vicariously liable for its employees' negligence while on the job.

Here, the man was an invitee when he entered the drug store to shop. But he became a trespasser when he intentionally went behind the cashier's counter without permission (Choice D). Nevertheless, the clerk owed him a duty to warn since she knew he was there and had reason to believe that he was unaware of the hidden, open shaft (Choice C). And since her failure to warn the man caused him to fall into the shaft and suffer harm, the man will likely obtain a judgment from the drug store (employer) for the clerk's (employee's) negligence.

The traditional approach is followed in about half the jurisdictions. The other half follow the modern approach, under which land possessors owe a duty of reasonable care to all land entrants (except flagrant trespassers).

(Choice B) Although the man's injuries did not result from the drug store's willful or wanton (ie, intentional or reckless) misconduct, the store is still vicariously liable for its employee's negligence under the doctrine of respondeat superior.

📌 Educational Objective

A land possessor owes a duty to known or anticipated trespassers to (1) warn them about hidden, artificial dangers that are known to the land possessor but unlikely to be discovered by trespassers and (2) use reasonable care in active operations.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 337 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (duty to known trespassers).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子进入一家药店购物。当他在货架间寻找各种商品时，他注意到一个挂有自动铅笔的展示牌。该展示牌位于收银台后面的一个高架上。该男子看到柜台上有一个牌子，上面写着“闲人免入，仅限员工”。由于附近没有店员可以帮助他，该男子便走到柜台后面去拿一支铅笔。这时，一名店员出现在柜台后面，问他是否需要帮助。他回答说他只是想要一支铅笔，并且他自己可以够到那个展示牌。店员没有再说什么。

在伸手去拿展示牌时，该男子侧身踩入一个隐藏的、未加盖的竖井，摔落到十英尺深的地下室。店员知道这个未加盖竖井的存在，但错误地认为该男子已经注意到了它。

该男子起诉该药店，要求赔偿其因摔落而受到的伤害。该司法管辖区采纳了纯粹比较过失原则（pure comparative negligence），并遵循有关土地占有者义务的传统普通法规则。

该男子是否可能获得对药店的胜诉判决？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为该男子是一名侵入者。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为该男子的伤害并非由被告的故意或恣意的不当行为造成。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为店员有理由相信该男子没有意识到那个未加盖的竖井。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为对于一名公共受邀者而言，该场所存在缺陷。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：传统普通法下，已知或可预见的 trespasser（已知或可预见的擅入者）享有哪些有限保护，尤其是店员明知暗坑却没提醒时，商店能不能因疏忽赔。

三秒认题路径：

先看进门身份 → 再看越界后身份 → 再看坑洞是否已知 → 再看是否该提醒 → 结论：可赔

核心法律规则

传统普通法里，land possessor（土地占有人）对一般来客要尽合理注意义务；但人一旦故意进了“No Admittance”后面的区域，就可能从 invitee（受邀人）变成 trespasser（擅入者），考场意思：身份一变，义务就变轻。

对known or anticipated trespasser（已知或可预见的擅入者），占有人至少要对hidden, artificial dangers（隐藏的人工危险）作提醒，并在现场活动中保持合理注意；考场意思：不是完全没义务，而是“知道有这个人、又知道他不知道危险”时，得开口提醒。

如果店员知道有open shaft（开放竖井），又有理由以为对方没发现，这个不提醒就会把案件推回到negligence 里，商店还可能因 respondeat superior（雇主替代责任） 承担责任。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 337 — 已知或可预见擅入者遇到隐藏人工危险时，占有人要提醒。

思维导图

先问：他在店里时是什么身份？
YES，仍是 invitee： 进入公共营业区时，店家义务较高，要看是否未尽合理注意。
NO，进了“员工区”： 故意越过柜台后，他变成 trespasser，不能再按普通 invitee 规则全套保护。
再问：店员对危险知道什么？
已知： 开放竖井是隐藏的 artificial danger，而且店员亲眼知道。
关键卡点： 店员还以为他看见了竖井，但事实相反；“以为他知道”不能替代提醒。
最后落点：能不能让商店赔？
能： 店员没提醒 → 义务没尽 → 伤害直接发生 → 商店可因员工疏忽担责。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他一开始是顾客，后面摔得很惨，所以店里应该对他一直按 invitee（受邀人） 标准负责。

但考试真正问的是：他越过柜台后已经变成trespasser（擅入者），真正要看的是店员是否知道暗坑、又是否该提醒。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里不是比谁更可怜，而是比谁知道危险、谁没提醒。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 clerk knew of the hidden shaft，又有理由认为他没看见；对已知擅入者，这正是必须提醒的触发点，所以商店可能赔。

❌ 事实误判 | 身份没分层

✕ A: 只抓他先是顾客，漏掉越过柜台后身份已经变了。

❌ 法律适用 | 误套恶性标准

✕ B: 把 willful or wanton 当成唯一门槛，忽略这里本来就是疏忽责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 邀请人规则错位

✕ D: 把“有缺陷的场所”直接等同于 public invitee，但题目卡的是擅入者提醒义务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定进入区域后的身份，再查占有人是否知道隐藏危险并有提醒义务。

考场速记

记住一句：先分身份，再看危险是否隐藏且已知。顾客越界进员工区，往往先变擅入者；只要店员知道暗坑却没提醒，题目就很容易从“他自己不小心”转成“店方要赔”。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A complaint filed on behalf of a woman against a nursing home and an ambulance service included the following allegations:
The woman, who was 86 years old and unable to speak after suffering a stroke, was picked up from her daughter's house by the ambulance service and taken to the nursing home to stay while her daughter was out of town. When the woman's daughter returned a few days later, the ambulance service picked up the woman from the nursing home and returned her to the daughter's house. The daughter was shocked to discover that the woman had a broken leg; her leg had been uninjured when she left for the nursing home.
A physician's report attached to the complaint stated that the woman's leg injury would not have occurred in the absence of negligence.
The complaint further alleged that the woman was under the control, successively, of the ambulance service and the nursing home during the time when she must have sustained the injury, and that either the ambulance service or the nursing home must have negligently moved or handled the woman, causing the injury to her leg.
Both defendants have argued that the allegations in the complaint are inadequate to support a negligence claim.
What is the best response to the defendants' argument?

choices.A: Both defendants owed a duty to the woman.
choices.B: One of the two defendants probably caused the injury, and the circumstances of the injury are primarily within the knowledge and control of the defendants rather than the woman or her representative.
choices.C: The defendants are concurrent tortfeasors, so each is vicariously liable for any tortious act committed by the other.
choices.D: There are grounds for the fact finder to infer that both defendants were negligent.

questions.explanation:
Res ipsa loquitur—“the thing speaks for itself”
(Byrne v. Boadle)

The ambulance service and nursing home argued that the allegations in the woman’s complaint are inadequate to support her negligence claim. This is likely because the woman cannot identify the direct cause of her injury—the ambulance service’s or nursing home’s negligence. In such a situation, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows a defendant’s negligence to be inferred from circumstantial evidence when:

  • the plaintiff suffered a type of harm that is usually caused by negligence of someone in the defendant’s position (as stated in the physician’s report) and
  • the evidence tends to eliminate other potential causes of that harm (eg, evidence that the injury did not exist before the woman left her daughter’s house).

This suggests that evidence regarding the cause of the woman’s injury is primarily within the defendants’ knowledge and control and allows the fact finder to infer that one of the defendants caused the injury. Therefore, res ipsa loquitur is the woman’s best response to support her negligence claim.

(Choice A) Both defendants owed the woman a duty of reasonable care because she was entrusted to their control. But this is not her best response since it does not address the other elements of her negligence claim-namely, the cause of her injury.

(Choice C) Even if the defendants are concurrent tortfeasors, they are not vicariously liable for each other’s actions since they do not share an agency relationship (eg, employer-employee).

(Choice D) The woman alleged grounds for the fact finder (eg, jury) to infer that one (not both) of the defendants was negligent.

📌 Educational Objective

The doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows a defendant’s negligence to be inferred from circumstantial evidence if (1) the plaintiff suffered a type of harm that is usually caused by negligence of someone in the defendant’s position and (2) the evidence tends to eliminate other potential causes of that harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 328D (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (defining the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur).
  • Collins v. Superior Air-Ground Ambulance Serv., Inc., 789 N.E.2d 394, 402 (Ill. App. Ct. 2003) (explaining how res ipsa loquitur can be alleged in an action involving multiple defendants).
questions.zh-question:
代表一名妇女向一家养老院和一家救护车服务公司提起的诉讼包含以下指控：

该妇女现年86岁，因中风而无法说话，救护车服务公司从她女儿家接走她，送往养老院，以便在她女儿外出期间暂住。几天后，当该妇女的女儿回来时，救护车服务公司又从养老院接走该妇女，并将其送回女儿家。女儿震惊地发现该妇女的腿骨折了；而她前往养老院时，腿部并未受伤。

诉状所附的一份医生报告指出，如果没有过失行为，该妇女的腿部伤害不会发生。

诉状进一步指控，在该妇女必定遭受伤害的期间，她先后处于救护车服务公司和养老院的控制之下，并且必定是救护车服务公司或养老院在移动或处理该妇女时存在过失，导致其腿部受伤。

两名被告均辩称，诉状中的指控不足以支持一项过失索赔。

对被告的论点，最佳的回应是什么？

zh-choices.A: 两名被告都对该妇女负有义务。
zh-choices.B: 两名被告之一很可能造成了该伤害，且伤害发生时的情况主要由被告而非该妇女或其代表所知悉和控制。
zh-choices.C: 被告是共同侵权行为人，因此每一方都对另一方实施的任何侵权行为负有转承责任。
zh-choices.D: 事实裁定者有理由推断两名被告均存在过失。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Breach of duty

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：当原告说不清到底是哪一个被告弄伤自己时，能不能用 res ipsa loquitur（事实自证） 让陪审团推定对方有过失。

三秒认题路径：

伤因不明 → 两被告接手 → 事前无伤 → 医生说像过失 → 推定过失

核心法律规则

只看本题够用的规则

res ipsa loquitur（事实自证） 的考场意思：原告不用直接点名“是谁碰坏的”，也能靠间接证据让事实裁判者推断被告有过失。

它通常要看两点：第一，伤害类型通常不会在没有过失时发生；第二，其他原因基本被排除，尤其是伤害发生前原告是完好的。

本题里，护理和搬运过程都在被告控制下，原告又无法直接知道哪一方出了问题，所以最强的回应不是先争 duty，而是直接把 res ipsa loquitur（事实自证） 拉出来。

核心判例：Byrne v. Boadle — “the thing speaks for itself”；Collins v. Superior Air-Ground Ambulance Serv., Inc. 说明多被告情形下也能这样主张。

思维导图

原告说不清到底是谁弄伤的？
先看1：伤害类型是否“通常不会无过失发生”？
医生报告 + 骨折本身 → 像过失造成
再看2：其他原因是否基本排除？
离开女儿家前没伤 → 伤因不在原告一侧
再看3：关键事实是否在被告控制下？
救护车 + 护理院连续控制 → 伤因主要在被告掌握
结论：可推定“其中一方有过失”，无需先精确锁定是谁。
所以选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然两家机构都接触过老人，那就应该先去争 duty（注意义务），或者直接说两被告都负责任。

但考试真正问的是：原告现在缺的是“谁弄伤的”这一段证明，不是“有没有照顾义务”这一段。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以这里的门槛不是把每个被告都定成肇事者，而是先让陪审团合理推定：伤害很可能出在被告控制的过程中。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 伤前无伤、伤后骨折，又加上医生报告和被告连续控制，正好符合 res ipsa loquitur（事实自证） 的推定路径。

❌ 概念混淆 | 义务替代因果

✕ A: 只盯着 duty，却没补上“谁导致骨折”的关键一步。

❌ 法律适用 | 连带责任误套

✕ C: 把共同接触误当成彼此 vicariously liable，但这里没有代理关系。

❌ 事实误判 | 双方同时过失

✕ D: 题干要推的是“其中一方”，不是“两方都已证明过失”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“伤因不明 + 被告控制 + 事前无伤”，再直接套 res ipsa loquitur（事实自证）。

考场速记

记住一句话：res ipsa loquitur（事实自证） 不是替你证明“谁”，而是替你先跨过“怎么证明”的门槛。

口诀：“伤害像过失、原因在被告、原告看不见”，就先想 res ipsa loquitur。

highlights.text: would not have occurred in the absence of negligence

reason.zh: 满足事实自证过失中伤害通常由过失所致的要件。

highlights.text: under the control, successively, of the ambulance service and the nursing home

reason.en: Places injury causation primarily within defendants' knowledge and control.
reason.zh: 将致害原因主要置于被告的知悉与控制范围内。

reason.zh: 正确答案须证明间接推论可弥补诉状证明之不足。

highlights.text: unable to speak after suffering a stroke

reason.en: Explains why res ipsa inference is needed to meet pleading requirements.
reason.zh: 说明为何需要借助事实自证过失推论以满足诉状要求。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A patient in a hospital was placed in a wheelchair with his broken leg extended straight out in front of him. As a nurse employed by the hospital was pushing the wheelchair through a set of automatic doors at a normal pace, the doors closed on the patient's foot, injuring it. The nurse attempted to pull the wheelchair back through the doors. This action caused the doors to close more tightly on the patient's foot, injuring it further.
The patient sued the hospital, alleging improper maintenance of the doors. The patient has produced no evidence of specific conduct or neglect on the part of the hospital that would have caused the automatic doors to malfunction. The hospital has moved for summary judgment.
Should the court grant the hospital's motion?

choices.A: No, because a jury could find that there was a latent defect in the doors.
choices.B: No, because a jury could find the hospital liable for negligence based on res ipsa loquitur.
choices.C: Yes, because proof of an accident, by itself, does not establish that an injured person was a victim of negligence.
choices.D: Yes, because the nurse's action was a superseding cause of the injury.

questions.explanation:
Negligence doctrines
ApplicabilityEffect
Res ipsa loquitur
  • Plaintiff suffered type of harm usually caused by someone in defendant's position
  • Evidence eliminates other potential causes of harm
Permissible inference that defendant was negligent
Negligence per se
  • Defendant violated statute
  • Statute was intended to prevent plaintiff's type of harm
  • Plaintiff is within class of persons statute was intended to protect
Rebuttable presumption that defendant was negligent

Lawsuits alleging improper maintenance of equipment are often based on negligence, which generally requires direct evidence that the defendant was negligent. But in the absence of such evidence, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows the fact finder (eg, jury) to infer that the defendant was negligent if:

  • the plaintiff suffered a type of harm that is usually caused by negligence of someone in the defendant's position and
  • the evidence tends to eliminate other potential causes of that harm.

Here, the hospital's automatic doors closed on the patient's foot, injuring it. Although there is no direct evidence of the hospital's negligence, automatic doors should not malfunction when properly maintained. And though the nurse's action caused the doors to close more tightly on the patient's foot, injuring it further, the nurse was pushing his wheelchair at a normal pace when the initial injury occurred—eliminating other potential causes of harm. Therefore, a jury could infer the hospital's negligence, and the court should deny its motion for summary judgment.

(Choice A) Product defects can also be inferred under the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur. But that inference is inappropriate here since (1) the patient sued the hospital—not a seller of automatic doors—and (2) the patient alleged improper maintenance—not a latent defect.

(Choice B) No, because a jury could find the hospital liable for negligence based on res ipsa loquitur.

(Choice C) Proof of an accident, by itself, does not establish that an injured person was a victim of negligence. But here, the hospital's negligence can be inferred from the nature and circumstances of the patient's accident.

(Choice D) The nurse's action was not a superseding cause of the patient's injury since it was foreseeable that a nurse would (1) push patients in wheelchairs through the hospital's doors and (2) attempt to help a patient who had been injured by a hospital door.

📌 Educational Objective

Negligence can be inferred under the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur if (1) the plaintiff suffered a type of harm that is usually caused by negligence of someone in the defendant's position and (2) the evidence tends to eliminate other potential causes of that harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 328D (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining when a defendant's negligence can be inferred based on the type of accident that injured the plaintiff).
questions.zh-question:
医院里的一名病人被安置在轮椅上，他骨折的腿在他面前伸直。当一名受雇于该医院的护士以正常速度推着轮椅通过一套自动门时，门夹住了病人的脚，导致其受伤。护士试图将轮椅从门中拉回。这一行为导致门更紧地夹住病人的脚，使其伤势加重。

病人起诉了医院，指控其对自动门维护不当。病人未能提供任何证据，证明医院有任何具体行为或疏忽导致自动门故障。医院已提出即决判决的动议。

法院是否应批准医院的动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为陪审团可能会认定门存在潜在缺陷。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为陪审团可以根据“事实本身说明问题”原则（res ipsa loquitur）认定医院存在过失责任。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为事故证明本身并不能确定伤者是过失行为的受害者。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为护士的行为是导致伤害的介入性替代原因。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：医院设备突然失灵、又拿不出直接过失证据时，能不能靠 事实自证（res ipsa loquitur） 让陪审团推定医院疏忽。

三秒认题路径：

自动门夹伤 → 无直接证据 → 排除他因 → 推定过失 → 不能驳回

核心法律规则

在 事实自证（res ipsa loquitur） 下，考场意思：虽然原告没拿到直接证据，陪审团还是可以从事故本身推断被告可能疏忽。前提有两个：这种伤害通常是像被告这样的人疏忽才会发生，而且证据要尽量排除其他原因。这里自动门本来不该在正常维护下夹住病人的脚，所以可以让医院先别在 summary judgment 阶段直接脱身。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 328D 锁定本题：当事故类型本身就指向疏忽、且其他原因被排除时，可以推定被告有过失。

思维导图

先看：题干有没有直接证明医院维护失职？
没有。 题干只说自动门把脚夹住，医院拿不出具体疏忽证据。
再看：这种伤害本身会不会“通常只在疏忽时发生”？
会。 正常维护的自动门不该突然夹伤病人脚，事故类型本身就很像设备维护不当。
第三关：其他原因有没有被排掉？
大体排掉了。 护士是正常推轮椅，初次夹伤不是他乱操作造成的，故障更像来自医院一侧。
卡死点：既然能走 res ipsa loquitur，就不能说“没有具体过失证据 = 直接胜诉”。
结论：法院该不该给医院 summary judgment？
不该。 陪审团可以据事故性质推定医院疏忽，所以答案是 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：没有“具体哪个员工做错了什么”，那就只能判医院赢。

但考试真正问的是：事故本身能不能让陪审团推断疏忽，而不是原告能不能先拿到一份“内部失误清单”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的伤有没有发生」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

自动门在正常维护下不该夹伤病人脚，且护士正常推轮椅已基本排掉其他原因，所以可用 res ipsa loquitur 推定医院过失，不能直接 summary judgment。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 latent defect 当成必考结论了，但题目问的是医院维护过失，不是卖门的人有无产品缺陷。

❌ 事实误判 | 事故本身偷换

✕ C: 只盯着“出了事故”就否认过失，忽略了事故性质已经足以触发 res ipsa。

❌ 法律适用 | 介入原因错套

✕ D: 把护士正常补救动作说成 superseding cause，但这正是医院门故障后可预见的反应。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看能否用事故本身推过失，再看是否真正排掉其他原因，最后才处理干扰项。

考场速记

记住一句：事实自证（res ipsa loquitur） 不是“没证据就算了”，而是“事故长得太像疏忽，陪审团可以先推定被告有责任”。

口诀：先问“这种伤是不是通常由疏忽造成”，再问“还有没有其他原因”。

reason.en: Malfunctioning doors on a patient suggest negligent maintenance by the hospital.
reason.zh: 自动门夹伤病人，暗示医院维护过失。

reason.en: Frames the claim as negligence in upkeep rather than product defect.
reason.zh: 将诉因定位为维护过失而非产品缺陷。

keywords.text: no evidence of specific conduct or neglect

reason.en: Triggers res ipsa when circumstantial inference may substitute for direct evidence.
reason.zh: 无直接证据时，可适用事实自证过失推定。

reason.en: Tests whether a jury could infer negligence from the record.
reason.zh: 判断陪审团能否从现有记录推定过失。

reason.en: Helps eliminate patient or nurse misconduct as the cause of the initial injury.
reason.zh: 有助于排除病人或护士不当行为致最初伤害。

reason.en: Raises superseding-cause distraction but does not negate the initial door malfunction.
reason.zh: 引出介入原因干扰，但不否定最初门故障所致伤害。

reason.en: Misstates the claim as product liability instead of improper maintenance.
reason.zh: 将诉因误作产品责任而非维护过失。

reason.en: Correct basis to infer hospital negligence without direct proof of fault.
reason.zh: 在无直接过错证据时推定医院过失的正确依据。

C.text: proof of an accident, by itself

reason.en: States a general rule while ignoring the res ipsa exception here.
reason.zh: 陈述一般规则却忽略本案适用的事实自证例外。

reason.en: Overlooks that accident circumstances can permit a negligence inference.
reason.zh: 忽视事故情境可允许推定过失。

reason.en: Mischaracterizes the nurse's foreseeable response as breaking causal chain.
reason.zh: 将护士可预见的救助行为误判为中断因果关系。

highlights.text: The patient has produced no evidence of specific conduct or neglect on the part of the hospital

reason.en: Absence of direct evidence is what makes res ipsa loquitur the controlling doctrine.
reason.zh: 缺乏直接证据使事实自证过失成为关键规则。

highlights.text: improper maintenance of the doors

reason.en: Defines the negligence theory and distinguishes it from latent-defect product claims.
reason.zh: 界定过失理论，并与隐蔽缺陷产品主张区分。

highlights.text: the doors closed on the patient's foot

reason.en: The unusual harm type typically indicates negligent maintenance of hospital equipment.
reason.zh: 此类伤害通常表明医院设备维护存在过失。

highlights.text: pushing the wheelchair through a set of automatic doors at a normal pace

reason.en: Normal use tends to eliminate other causes and supports a res ipsa inference.
reason.zh: 正常使用有助于排除其他原因并支持事实自证推定。

highlights.text: The hospital has moved for summary judgment

reason.en: The court must decide whether a jury could infer negligence from these facts.
reason.zh: 法院须判断陪审团能否从这些事实推定过失。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A man and his friend, who were both adults, went to a party. The man and the friend had many drinks at the party and became legally intoxicated. They decided to play a game of chance called "Russian roulette" using a gun loaded with one bullet. As part of the game, the man pointed the gun at the friend and, on her command, pulled the trigger. The man shot the friend in the shoulder.
The friend has brought a negligence action against the man. Traditional defenses based on the plaintiff's conduct apply. What is likely to be the dispositive issue in this case?

choices.A: Whether the friend could validly consent to the game.
choices.B: Whether the friend was also negligent.
choices.C: Whether the game constituted a joint venture.
choices.D: Whether the man was legally intoxicated when he began playing the game.

questions.explanation:
Contributory negligence
(defense to negligence)

Contributory negligence
(defense to negligence)
Traditional contributory
negligence jurisdiction		Plaintiff's negligence completely bars recovery
Pure comparative negligence
jurisdiction*		Plaintiff's negligence reduces recovery by plaintiff's proportionate fault
(eg, plaintiff 90% at fault can recover 10% of damages)
*Default rule on MBE.

In traditional common law jurisdictions (as seen here), contributory negligence is a complete defense to negligence when the plaintiff's failure to use reasonable care contributed to his/her injury. Here, the man negligently shot his friend during a game of Russian roulette. But the friend cannot recover from the man if she was contributorily negligent in becoming intoxicated at the party and agreeing to play the game. Therefore, whether the friend was also negligent is likely to be the dispositive issue in her negligence action against the man.

(Choice A) Consent may be a defense to negligence if the plaintiff assumed the risk of harm. Here, the friend did not assent to a liability waiver (no express assumption). And since the friend was intoxicated, she may not have understood and voluntarily accepted the risk of Russian roulette (no implied assumption). As a result, the friend's case is more likely to turn on whether she was contributorily negligent.

(Choice C) When multiple tortfeasors participate in a joint venture (eg, playing Russian roulette together), they are jointly and severally liable for any harm caused to nonparticipants. But the existence of a joint venture is irrelevant when the participants harm each other.

(Choice D) Voluntarily intoxicated persons are held to the same "reasonable person" standard as sober persons in negligence actions, so the man's intoxication would not shield him from liability in this case.

📌 Educational Objective

Under traditional common law rules, contributory negligence is a complete defense to negligence if the plaintiff's failure to use reasonable care contributed to his/her harm.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 467 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a plaintiff's contributory negligence is a complete bar to recovery for negligence).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 496D (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that implied assumption of the risk is only a defense if the plaintiff understood the unreasonable character of the risk).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子和他的朋友（均为成年人）去参加一个派对。该男子和他的朋友在派对上喝了很多酒，达到了法律上的醉酒状态。他们决定玩一种名为“Russian roulette”的博弈游戏，使用一把装有一颗子弹的枪。作为游戏的一部分，该男子用枪指着朋友，并在她的指令下扣动了扳机。男子射中了朋友的肩膀。

朋友对该男子提起了过失诉讼。基于原告行为的传统抗辩在此适用。本案中，决定性的争议点可能是什么？

zh-choices.A: 朋友是否能够对该游戏作出有效同意。
zh-choices.B: 朋友是否也存在过失。
zh-choices.C: 该游戏是否构成一项共同冒险。
zh-choices.D: 在开始玩游戏时，该男子是否处于法律上的醉酒状态。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Defenses to negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：在传统普通法的 过失相抵（contributory negligence） 规则下，原告自己有没有也犯了疏忽，能不能直接把赔偿整案挡掉。

三秒认题路径：

传统规则 → 原告也疏忽 → 完全抗辩 → 看 B

核心法律规则

在传统普通法州，过失相抵（contributory negligence） 是对 过失（negligence） 的完全抗辩，考场意思：只要原告自己的不合理不小心也促成了伤害，原告就可能一分钱都拿不到。

纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence） 才是按比例减赔；但这题给的是传统规则，所以重点不是“谁更坏”，而是“原告有没有也有错”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 467 锁定结论：原告的 contributory negligence 可以直接把恢复权挡掉。

思维导图

先问：这是传统州吗？题目已给“traditional defenses based on the plaintiff's conduct”。
是 → 进 过失相抵（contributory negligence）。
再问：原告自己有没有不合理疏忽，且这疏忽有没有促成伤害？
有 → 原告被完全挡回 → 不能恢复。
没有 → 继续看其他抗辩。
A 误区：只盯 assumed the risk，但题干更像在问原告有没有也疏忽。
C 误区：joint venture 管的是对外第三人，不是互相打伤时的核心问题。
D 误区：被告喝醉不帮他脱责，醉酒者仍按 reasonable person 标准看。
所以答案卡在：friend was also negligent。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然两个人都喝醉了，还一起玩危险游戏，那是不是该先看 consent、assumption of risk，或者看男人自己也醉了。

但考试真正问的是：在传统州，原告有没有也不小心到足以触发 过失相抵（contributory negligence）。

司法考试看的是「原告能不能在程序上拿到赔偿」，不是先纠结他有没有真的“同意玩命”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键是原告自己也在喝醉后参与高危行为，plaintiff's negligence 一旦成立，在传统州就能直接挡掉恢复。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 只盯 consent，漏掉题目真正要你先查原告自己有没有疏忽。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间关系误判

✕ C: 把 joint venture 用到互相伤害上，方向错了。

❌ 事实误判 | 醉酒免责偷换

✕ D: 看到他喝醉就想减责，但被告醉酒不等于免除过失标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定传统州规则，再问原告自己有没有也犯错，直接用完全抗辩收口。

考场速记

记住一句：传统州看原告是否也有错，有错就可能一票否决；比较过失州才是按比例分担。

这题的速记是：“先看原告，再看比例；传统州里，原告有错就可能全没。”

keywords.text: Traditional defenses based on the plaintiff's conduct apply

reason.en: Signals that contributory negligence, not consent or joint venture, controls the outcome.
reason.zh: 表明本案关键在共同过失，而非同意或共同事业。

reason.en: Frames the dispute as negligence with traditional contributory-negligence rules.
reason.zh: 将争议定性为适用传统共同过失规则的过失诉讼。

reason.en: The extreme risk makes the plaintiff's participation central to fault allocation.
reason.zh: 极高风险使原告参与行为成为过错分配核心。

reason.en: Intoxication may show the plaintiff failed to exercise reasonable care.
reason.zh: 醉酒可证明原告未尽合理注意义务。

reason.en: Asks which defense or fault question will decide the case.
reason.zh: 要求识别决定案件结果的核心法律问题。

reason.en: Voluntary participation in the game supports analyzing plaintiff fault.
reason.zh: 自愿参与游戏支持分析原告自身过错。

reason.en: Distracts toward assumption of risk instead of contributory negligence.
reason.zh: 将考生引向自承风险而非共同过失。

reason.en: Suggests consent to Russian roulette resolves the case.
reason.zh: 暗示同意玩俄轮盘赌即可决定案件。

reason.en: Directly states the complete-bar defense at issue under traditional rules.
reason.zh: 直接点出传统规则下完全阻却Recovery的共同过失抗辩。

reason.en: Irrelevant when co-participants injure each other.
reason.zh: 共同参与者互相伤害时该原则不适用。

reason.en: Misdirects focus to defendant's intoxication, which does not excuse liability.
reason.zh: 错误聚焦被告醉酒，而醉酒不免除其过失责任。

reason.en: Irrelevant because intoxicated defendants are judged by the reasonable-person standard.
reason.zh: 无关紧要，因醉酒者仍适用合理人标准。

highlights.text: Traditional defenses based on the plaintiff's conduct apply

reason.en: Directly points to contributory negligence as the controlling defense.
reason.zh: 直接指向共同过失为决定性抗辩。

highlights.text: The friend has brought a negligence action against the man.

reason.en: Establishes negligence liability with traditional contributory-negligence rules.
reason.zh: 确立适用传统共同过失规则的过失责任框架。

highlights.text: became legally intoxicated

reason.en: Supports finding the plaintiff failed to use reasonable care.
reason.zh: 支持认定原告未尽合理注意义务。

highlights.text: play a game of chance called "Russian roulette"

reason.en: The plaintiff's agreement to participate is evidence of contributory negligence.
reason.zh: 原告同意参与是共同过失的重要证据。

highlights.text: What is likely to be the dispositive issue in this case?

reason.en: Requires identifying which fault question decides recovery, not merely listing defenses.
reason.zh: 要求识别决定能否获赔的核心过错问题，而非罗列抗辩。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A hotel employed a carefully selected independent contractor to rebuild its swimming pool. The hotel continued to operate while the pool was being rebuilt. The contract between the hotel and the contractor required the contractor to indemnify the hotel for any liability arising from the contractor's negligent acts. A guest of the hotel fell into the excavation, which the contractor had negligently left unguarded.
In an action by the guest against the hotel to recover for his injuries, what would be the most likely outcome?

choices.A: Liability, because the contract between the hotel and the contractor required the contractor to indemnify the hotel for any liability arising from the contractor's negligent acts.
choices.B: Liability, because the hotel had a nondelegable duty to the guest to keep a safe premises.
choices.C: No liability, because the contractor was the actively negligent party.
choices.D: No liability, because the hotel exercised reasonable care in employing the contractor.

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for torts committed by its independent contractor. However, vicarious liability will be imposed if the independent contractor's work breaches a nondelegable duty owed by the principal-i.e, a duty retained by the principal even when the performance of the duty is assigned to an independent contractor. This includes the duty of a land possessor that holds its land open to the public to keep the premises safe for business visitors.

Here, the hotel hired an independent contractor to rebuild its swimming pool. While performing that work, the contractor negligently left the excavation unguarded. A guest then fell into the excavation and sustained injuries. And since the hotel had a nondelegable duty to keep the premises safe for its guests, the hotel is vicariously liable for the guest's injuries caused by the contractor's negligence.

(Choice A) The contractor's agreement to indemnify (ie, reimburse) the hotel for any liability arising from the contractor's negligent acts does not affect the hotel's liability to its guests. Instead, the indemnity agreement provides a basis for the hotel to seek reimbursement from the contractor if the guest's suit succeeds.

(Choice C) Active negligence is negligence resulting from an affirmative act (eg, rebuilding the swimming pool), while passive negligence is negligence resulting from inaction (eg, failing to maintain safe premises). However, these distinctions are outdated and, even if they applied, merely address the apportionment of damages between multiple defendants—not one defendant's liability to the plaintiff.

(Choice D) The fact that the hotel exercised reasonable care in employing the contractor shows that the hotel is not directly liable for its own negligence in hiring an incompetent worker. But the hotel is still vicariously liable for the contractor's negligence since the hotel owed its guests a nondelegable duty to maintain safe premises.

📌 Educational Objective

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for its independent contractor's torts. However, vicarious liability will be imposed when the independent contractor breaches a nondelegable duty of care owed by the principal-eg, a land possessor's duty to keep the premises safe for business visitors.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 57 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (no vicarious liability generally for independent contractor's torts).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 344 (nondelegable duty to keep business premises safe).
questions.zh-question:
一家酒店雇用了一位经过审慎挑选的独立承包人来重建其游泳池。在游泳池重建期间，该酒店继续营业。酒店与承包人之间的合同要求承包人就其疏忽行为所引起的任何责任对酒店进行赔偿。一位酒店的客人掉入了承包人因疏忽而未设防的挖掘坑中。

在该客人就其所受伤害向酒店提起的诉讼中，最可能的结果是什么？

zh-choices.A: 酒店有责任，因为酒店与承包人之间的合同要求承包人就其疏忽行为所引起的任何责任对酒店进行赔偿。
zh-choices.B: 酒店有责任，因为酒店对客人负有保持经营场所安全的不可转嫁的义务。
zh-choices.C: 酒店无责任，因为承包人是主动疏忽方。
zh-choices.D: 酒店无责任，因为酒店在雇用承包人时已尽到合理注意。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Vicarious liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：独立承包人一般不让雇主替他背锅，但如果承包人的工作碰到不可转让义务（nondelegable duty），比如经营中的酒店对住客负有保持安全场所的义务，酒店还是会被追究替代责任（vicarious liability）。

三秒认题路径：

独立承包人 → 安全场所义务 → 不可转让 → 酒店担责 → 选 B

核心法律规则

独立承包人（independent contractor）通常不让雇主直接替他的侵权负责；但如果承包人是在帮雇主履行一项不可转让义务（nondelegable duty），雇主还是会被替代责任（vicarious liability）锁住，考场意思：你把活外包了，不等于把这项责任也外包掉。

这里的关键义务是土地占有人对公开营业场所的顾客负有保持场所安全（keep the premises safe）的义务，考场意思：酒店不能靠“我请的是承包人”来躲开住客受伤这笔账。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题真正锁定的是独立承包人规则下的不可转让义务例外，而不是一般上诉规则。

思维导图

先问：酒店能不能用“独立承包人”直接脱身？
一般规则雇主通常不为独立承包人的侵权负责。
但本题卡点酒店是对住客开放的经营场所，负有保持安全场所的不可转让义务。
一旦承包人的疏忽让坑洞无人遮挡，这项义务就不能靠外包切断。
题干事实承包人把挖掘区留着不管，住客掉进去受伤。
法律结果承包人自己直接负责；酒店也因不可转让义务承担替代责任（vicarious liability）。
结论：酒店不能靠“我已经小心挑了承包人”来赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：酒店已经认真挑了承包人，又有indemnify条款，所以应该没责任。

但考试真正问的是：对住客这项安全义务能不能转出去；答案是不行。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个常见误判是把“承包人是主动挖坑的人”当成酒店免责理由；这只是在分谁更主动，不会把酒店对顾客的安全义务抹掉。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键触发点是酒店对营业场所住客负有保持安全场所的义务；承包人挖掘区无人遮挡，正是这项不可转让义务（nondelegable duty）被打穿，所以酒店要赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 赔偿关系误判

✕ A: 把indemnify当成对外免责，其实它只管事后向承包人追偿。

❌ 法律适用 | 主动被动误套

✕ C: 盯着“承包人更主动”就想让酒店脱身，这是拿旧标签替代责任分析。

❌ 事实误判 | 尽责即免责偷换

✕ D: 酒店care到的是雇人环节，不是对住客的安全义务本身。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“独立承包人”这层，再立刻问有没有不可转让义务；有的话，直接看酒店是否仍要对第三人负责。

考场速记

记住这句：独立承包人一般不替雇主背锅，但不可转让义务会把锅重新扣回雇主头上。看到酒店、商场、对外营业场所，就先想“安全义务能不能外包”，不能外包时，选能追到场所占有人那一项。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
During a comprehensive evaluation of an adult patient's psychiatric condition, a psychiatrist failed to diagnose her patient's suicidal state. One day after the misdiagnosis, the patient committed suicide. The patient's father, immediately after having been told of his son's suicide, suffered severe emotional distress, which resulted in a stroke. The patient's father was not present at the patient's appointment with the psychiatrist, nor did he witness the suicide. The father has brought an action against the psychiatrist to recover for his severe emotional distress and the resulting stroke.
Is the father likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the father did not sustain a physical impact.
choices.B: No, because the psychiatrist's professional duty did not extend to the harms suffered by the patient's father.
choices.C: Yes, because the father was a member of the patient's immediate family.
choices.D: Yes, because the psychiatrist reasonably could have foreseen that a misdiagnosis would result in the patient's suicide and the resulting emotional distress of the patient's father.

questions.explanation:
Mental-health professional's
duty to control patient's conduct
Must use reasonable care to:
  • determine whether patient poses risk of harm to others and
  • mitigate that risk-eg
  • • treat patient
  • • warn potential victims
  • • notify law enforcement
  • • seek patient's commitment

For negligent infliction of emotional distress (NIED), the plaintiff must prove that the defendant acted negligently by breaching a duty owed to the plaintiff. Mental-health professionals owe their patients a duty to use reasonable care. And because they have a special relationship with their patients, mental-health professionals also owe others a duty to use reasonable care to:

  • Identify patients who pose a foreseeable risk of physical harm to others and
  • take steps to mitigate that risk.

Here, the psychiatrist may be liable to the patient's estate for failing to diagnose his suicidal state. However, the psychiatrist is not liable to the father because the patient only posed a threat of physical harm to himself—not to his father. Therefore, the psychiatrist did not breach her duty to the father, and the father will not recover for his severe emotional distress or resulting stroke.

(Choice A) The zone-of-danger theory of NIED requires proof that the plaintiff was in danger of physical harm—not actually harmed by a physical impact. Therefore, had the psychiatrist breached her duty to the father by placing him in a zone of physical danger, then the father may have prevailed despite his lack of physical impact.

(Choice C) The father's relation to the patient is relevant under the bystander theory of NIED, which applies when a plaintiff suffers emotional distress upon witnessing bodily harm to a close relative. But since the father did not witness the patient's suicide, this theory does not apply.

(Choice D) The psychiatrist's ability to foresee that her misdiagnosis would result in the patient's suicide shows that she breached her duty to the patient—not the father. And though the father's resulting emotional distress may have been foreseeable, the psychiatrist's duty to the father only extended to foreseeable risks of physical harm.

📌 Educational Objective

Mental-health professionals have a duty to use reasonable care to identify and mitigate any foreseeable risk of physical harm that their patients pose to others.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 41 cmt. g (Am. L. Inst. 2012) (duty of mental-health professionals to control patients).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 47 cmt. i (Am. L. Inst. 2012) (duty arising from a special relationship is limited to foreseeable physical harm).
questions.zh-question:
在对一名成年患者的精神状况进行全面评估时，一名精神科医生未能诊断出其患者的自杀倾向。在误诊一天后，该患者自杀身亡。患者的父亲在被告知其儿子自杀的消息后，立即遭受了严重的情感困扰，并导致中风。患者的父亲既未在患者与精神科医生会诊时在场，也未目睹自杀过程。该父亲对精神科医生提起诉讼，要求为其严重的情感困扰及由此导致的中风获得赔偿。

该父亲的诉讼请求可能成功吗？

zh-choices.A: 不可能，因为父亲没有遭受物理性的撞击。
zh-choices.B: 不可能，因为精神科医生的职业责任不延及患者父亲所遭受的损害。
zh-choices.C: 可能，因为父亲是患者的直系亲属。
zh-choices.D: 可能，因为精神科医生理应预见到误诊会导致患者自杀，并由此给患者父亲带来情感困扰。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Vicarious liability

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：精神科医生对患者的照护义务，通常只延伸到可预见的第三人身体伤害，不会因为家属情绪受创就自动对家属承担 NIED（negligent infliction of emotional distress） 责任。

三秒认题路径：

医生误诊 → 患者自杀 → 父亲起诉 → 先看有无对父亲义务 → 再看能否直接赔

核心法律规则

做 NIED（negligent infliction of emotional distress），先问一句：被告有没有对这个原告负 duty（注意义务）。这里的关键不是“悲剧够不够惨”，而是精神科医生对 special relationship（特殊关系） 产生的义务，考试上主要是去识别并降低患者对他人造成的可预见 physical harm（身体伤害） 风险。foreseeable physical harm（可预见的身体伤害） 才是她对第三人的边界，不是对一切情绪后果兜底。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题对应的是 Restatement (Third) of Torts § 41 / § 47 的思路：精神健康专业人员对第三人的义务，限于可预见的身体伤害风险。

所以，医生可能对患者本人承担责任，因为她没识别出患者的自杀风险；但对父亲，题干没有给出“患者对父亲存在可预见身体伤害”的事实。父亲受的是听闻噩耗后的情绪和中风后果，不是医生对父亲本人的注意义务范围内的伤害。

思维导图

先问：父亲能不能赢，是不是因为医生对他本人负有可诉义务？
1.有没有 duty（注意义务） 直接指向父亲？
没有：精神科医生的第三人义务，卡在可预见的身体伤害，不是“家属情绪会受伤”。
2.患者有没有对父亲构成可预见的 physical harm（身体伤害） 风险？
没有。题干只有患者自杀，受害对象是患者自己，不是父亲。
3.父亲的中风能不能把“情绪伤害”变成可赔？
不能：后果很重，不等于义务扩张；关键是医生对父亲没有对应注意义务。
结论 选 B：not liable，因为义务没延伸到父亲。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：父亲这么近，又真的受了重伤，应该可以告吧。

但考试真正问的是：医生有没有对父亲负起能支持 NIED（negligent infliction of emotional distress） 的义务；这里没有，题干只是“患者自杀后父亲受刺激”，不等于医生对父亲可赔。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键是：医生的义务只覆盖患者及其可预见的第三人身体伤害，父亲并不在这个范围内，所以他不能凭自己的情绪损害直接赢。

❌ 概念混淆 | 物理接触误判

✕ A: 把 physical impact 当门槛，错把 zone-of-danger 和本题混在一起。

❌ 事实误判 | 近亲目睹偷换

✕ C: 只看“父子关系”就想套近亲旁观者规则，但他没目睹自杀。

❌ 法律适用 | 可预见性外推

✕ D: 把 foreseeable 情绪反应当成对父亲的义务范围，外推过头了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定注意义务的对象，再看第三人伤害是否仍属“可预见的身体伤害”范围。

考场速记

记住一句：精神健康专业人员对外的责任，重点是“防止患者伤到别人”，不是“安抚所有被波及的家属情绪”。

遇到类似题，先问：原告是不是那个医生负有义务的人；不是的话，NIED（negligent infliction of emotional distress） 往往直接卡死。

D.text: misdiagnosis would result in the patient's suicide

reason.zh: 确立对病人可能存在过失，并引出对第三人义务范围的分析。

reason.en: The patient posed a risk of physical harm to himself, not to his father.
reason.zh: 患者构成的是对自身的身体伤害风险，而非对父亲的风险。

highlights.text: not present at the patient's appointment with the psychiatrist, nor did he witness the suicide

reason.en: Eliminates bystander NIED and related presence-based theories.
reason.zh: 排除旁观者精神损害及其他需在场支持的规则。

highlights.text: recover for his severe emotional distress and the resulting stroke

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A four-year-old child sustained serious injuries when a playmate pushed him from between two parked cars into the street, where he was struck by a car. The child, by his representative, sued the driver of the car, the playmate's parents, and his own parents. At trial, the child's total damages were determined to be $100,000. The playmate's parents were determined to be 20% at fault because they had failed to adequately supervise her. The driver was found to be 50% at fault. The child's own parents were determined to be 30% at fault for failure to adequately supervise him.
The court has adopted the pure comparative negligence doctrine, with joint and several liability, in place of the common law rules relating to plaintiff's fault. In addition, the common law doctrines relating to intra-family liability have been abrogated.
What is the maximum amount, if anything, that the child's representative can recover from the driver?

choices.D: Nothing.

questions.explanation:
Liability of multiple tortfeasors for indivisible harm

Joint & several liability*
  • Any tortfeasor can be held liable for plaintiff's total amount of damages
  • Tortfeasors can sue each other for contribution
Several liability Each tortfeasor is liable for portion of damages corresponding to his/her proportionate fault (eg. 15% of damages for 15% fault)

*Default rule on MBE.

This jurisdiction has adopted the following:

  • Pure comparative negligence (default rule on MBE) – when the plaintiff's own negligence contributes to his/her harm, the plaintiff's recovery is reduced by his/her proportionate share of fault.
  • Joint and several liability – when multiple defendants cause the plaintiff indivisible harm, the plaintiff can recover the total amount of damages from any defendant (who can then sue the others for contribution)

Additionally, this jurisdiction has abandoned the common law rules of intra-family liability. As a result, the fault of a child's parents will not be imputed to the child or vice versa.

Here, the court determined that multiple defendants were at fault for causing the child's injuries: the playmate's parents (20%), the driver (50%), and the child's parents (30%). The child was not at fault. And since his parents' fault will not be imputed to him, his recovery will not be reduced for comparative negligence. Therefore, the child can recover his total damages ($100,000) from any of the defendants, including the driver.

(Choices A & B) If liability were only several (not seen here), each tortfeasor would only be liable for the portion of damages that corresponds to his/her proportionate fault. In that case, the child could only recover $30,000 from his parents (30% of total damages) and $50,000 from the driver (50% of total damages).

(Choice C) If traditional common law rules regarding intra-family liability and contributory negligence applied, the fault of the child's parents would be imputed to the child and bar all recovery. But these rules have been abandoned or replaced in this jurisdiction.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the pure comparative negligence doctrine, a negligent plaintiff's recovery is reduced by his/her proportionate share of fault. And under joint and several liability, any one of multiple tortious defendants who caused the plaintiff indivisible harm can be held liable for the plaintiff's total amount of damages.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 488 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a parent's negligence is no longer imputed to his/her child and a child's negligence will not be imputed to the parent).
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 875 (Am. Law Inst. 1979) (explaining that multiple tortfeasors who cause an indivisible harm can be held liable individually for the entire harm).

一名四岁儿童被玩伴从两辆停放的汽车之间推到街上，被一辆汽车撞倒，身受重伤。该儿童通过其法定代理人，起诉了汽车司机、玩伴的父母以及他自己的父母。经审判，该儿童的全部损害赔偿金被确定为100,000美元。玩伴的父母因未能充分监管其子女，被认定负有20%的过错。司机被认定负有50%的过错。该儿童自己的父母因未能充分监管他，被认定负有30%的过错。

法院已采用纯粹比较过失原则以及连带责任，以取代与原告过错相关的普通法规则。此外，与家庭内部责任相关的普通法原则已被废除。

该儿童的法定代理人最多可以从司机处获得多少赔偿（如果有的话）？

zh-choices.D: 无。

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：多个侵权人造成不可分损害时，共同及个别责任（joint and several liability）下能不能让原告向任一被告追偿全部损害。

三秒认题路径：

不可分损害 → 多个被告 → 纯比较过失 → 父母过失不归责 → 选全额

核心法律规则

纯比较过失（pure comparative negligence）的考场意思：原告自己有错时，赔偿只按自己的过失比例减。共同及个别责任（joint and several liability）的考场意思：多个被告一起造成同一份不可分损害时，原告可以向任何一个被告追全部金额，再由被告彼此去追分担（contribution）。

本题里孩子自己没有过失，而且本辖区已经废除了家庭内部责任（intra-family liability）的旧规则，所以父母的过失不会算到孩子头上。不可分损害（indivisible harm）已经成立时，原告就能向司机要全额，不需要按50%去砍半。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 875 的逻辑是：造成不可分损害的多个侵权人，可以各自被追到全额；配合 § 488，父母过失不再自动归责给孩子。

思维导图

这题先看：孩子自己有错吗？
NO：孩子无过失，先不减赔偿。
再看：父母的过失能不能算到孩子身上？
NO：已废除 intra-family liability，不归责。
最后看：多个被告造成的是不是同一份不可分损害？
YES：适用 joint and several liability。
卡死点：不按50%砍成 $50,000，而是可向司机追到 $100,000。
结论：司机不是只付自己的份额，而是可能被追全额。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：司机只占 50% 过错，所以最多只能赔一半。

但考试真正问的是：在joint and several liability下，原告能不能先向任何一个侵权人拿全额，而不是每人只付自己那一份。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干写明孩子无过失，且父母过失不再归责给孩子，所以赔偿不减；又因多个被告造成不可分损害，原告可向司机追回 $100,000 全额。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看司机比例

✕ A: 把 50% 当成唯一上限，漏掉共同及个别责任。

❌ 法律适用 | 把几分责任当总额

✕ B: 误以为被告只赔自己那半，忽略原告可先拿全额。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把父母过失当孩子过失

✕ D: 看到 intra-family 就以为会归责，但本题已被废除。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判原告是否被减赔，再看是否适用共同及个别责任，最后再拆分被告内部追偿。

考场速记

记住一句：纯比较过失先管原告自己的错，共同及个别责任再管多个被告怎么分账；原告先拿全额，被告再自己算 contribution。

reason.zh: 检验父母过失是否会减少子女的获赔金额。

highlights.text: with joint and several liability

reason.en: Allows recovery of the full $100,000 from the driver alone.
reason.zh: 允许仅向司机追偿全部10万美元。

reason.zh: 防止子女因父母30%过错而减少获赔。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
While walking on a public sidewalk, a pedestrian was struck by a piece of lumber that fell from the roof of a homeowner's house. The homeowner had hired a roofer to make repairs to his roof, and the lumber fell through negligence on the roofer's part.
If the pedestrian brings an action against the homeowner to recover damages for the injury caused to him by the roofer's negligence, will the pedestrian prevail?

choices.A: No, because the roofer was an independent contractor rather than the homeowner's servant.
choices.B: No, if the homeowner exercised reasonable care in hiring the roofer to do the repair work.
choices.C: Yes, because the roofer's act was a breach of a nondelegable duty owed by the homeowner to the pedestrian.
choices.D: Yes, under the res ipsa loquitur doctrine.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Nondelegable duties

(duties that cannot be assigned to another to avoid liability)
  • Maintain safe conditions on premises open to public (eg, store, restaurant)
  • Safely perform activities that:
    • are abnormally or highly dangerous
    • infringe on private property right (eg, nuisance, trespass)
    • are regulated by law or
    • are conducted in public place

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for torts (eg, negligence) committed by his/her independent contractor. But vicarious liability can be imposed when the independent contractor's work involves a nondelegable duty—i.e., a duty of care that cannot be assigned to a third party to avoid liability. This includes a land possessor's duty to safely conduct activities on the land that pose foreseeable risks of harm to others (eg, construction, repairs).

Here, the homeowner (land possessor) hired the roofer (independent contractor) to repair the homeowner's roof. Since repairing a roof poses a foreseeable risk of harm to others, the homeowner had a nondelegable duty to ensure that the repairs were conducted safely. And since the roofer's act (neglegently allowing lumber to fall from the roof) breached that duty, the homeowner is vicariously liable for the resulting harm (the pedestrian's injury).

(Choice A) Employers are vicariously liable for torts committed by their employees (ie, servants) while acting within the scope of employment. But the fact that the roofer was an independent contractor—not an employee—does not defeat the pedestrian's claim since the roofer's work involved a nondelegable duty.

(Choice B) The fact that the homeowner exercised reasonable care in hiring the roofer would show that the homeowner is not directly liable for negligently hiring an incompetent contractor. But the homeowner can still be vicariously liable for the roofer's negligence since the roofer's work involved a nondelegable duty.

(Choice C) Yes, because the roofer's act (actegligently allowing lumber to fall from the roof) was a breach of a nondelegable duty owed by the homeowner to the pedestrian.

(Choice D) When there is no direct evidence of negligence, the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur allows negligence to be inferred from circumstantial evidence if (1) the event that caused the plaintiff's harm would not ordinarily occur absent negligence by someone in the defendant's position and (2) the evidence tends to eliminate other possible causes of that harm. But this doctrine does not apply since the roofer's negligence is stated.

📌 Educational Objective

A principal is generally not vicariously liable for its independent contractor's torts. However, vicarious liability can be imposed when the principal owed a nondelegable duty of care—e.g., a land possessor's duty to safely conduct activities on the land that pose a foreseeable risk of harm to others.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm § 57 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (general rule: no vicarious liability for independent contractors' torts).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Liab. for Physical & Emotional Harm §§ 54, 62 (Am. Law Inst. 2012) (exception: land possessor's nondelegable duty to safely conduct activities on the land).
questions.zh-question:
一名行人在公共人行道上行走时，被一块从房主屋顶掉落的木材击中。该房主雇佣了一名屋顶工人来修理其屋顶，而木材是由于屋顶工人的过失而掉落的。

如果该行人对房主提起诉讼，就屋顶工人的过失所造成的伤害要求损害赔偿，该行人能否胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为屋顶工人是独立承包人，而非房主的雇员。
zh-choices.B: 不会，如果房主在雇佣屋顶工人进行维修工作时尽到了合理的注意义务。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为屋顶工人的行为违反了房主对该行人所负有的一项不可转委的义务。
zh-choices.D: 会，根据 res ipsa loquitur 原则。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Negligence

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：屋主把修屋顶这类有可预见危险的工作交给独立承包人后，能不能因为不可委托义务（nondelegable duty）而替对方的过失负责。

三秒认题路径：

独立承包人 → 屋顶维修 → 公共人行道受伤 → 不可委托义务 → 选 C

核心法律规则

独立承包人（independent contractor）一般不让雇主替他的侵权买单，考场意思：不是员工，不自动算雇主自己的锅。不可委托义务（nondelegable duty）例外是：有些义务不能外包，考场意思：你把活交出去，也不能把责任一起甩掉。

土地占有人对在土地上进行、且会给他人带来可预见风险的活动负有这种义务，比如修缮、施工。只要承包人的过失正好打穿这条义务，屋主就可能对结果承担替代责任。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用；本题锁定的是 不可委托义务（nondelegable duty） 例外，不是普通雇主-承包人免责规则。

思维导图

先看：这是 独立承包人（independent contractor） 的过失吗？
是：一般先不替承包人担责。
再问：有没有 不可委托义务（nondelegable duty）？
本题触发：屋顶维修属于土地上有可预见危险的活动，屋主不能把“安全完成”这件事一起外包。
卡死点：不是看“是不是员工”，而是看“这条义务能不能委托”。
结论：承包人把木料掉下去 → 打穿屋主的非可委托安全义务 → 选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然屋主已经合理挑选了屋顶工人，而且工人又不是员工，那就该免责。

但考试真正问的是：这类修屋顶工作本身有没有把屋主的安全注意义务留下来，不能靠“外包”消失。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（本题对应的不是证据泄露题，而是责任能不能转嫁。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干明确是屋顶维修中木料掉落，属于土地上有可预见风险的活动；nondelegable duty 使屋主不能把安全责任完全甩给承包人，所以要负责。

❌ 概念混淆 | 员工承包人混用

✕ A: 把independent contractor误当免责终点。

❌ 法律适用 | 受雇审查误套

✕ B: 盯着“合理雇用”就以为能挡住替代责任。

❌ 事实误判 | 证据缺口偷换

✕ D: 把res ipsa loquitur硬塞进来；题干已直接说出过失。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓责任归属，再看独立承包人例外；只要碰到土地上有可预见危险的修缮，就优先想不可委托义务。

考场速记

记住一句：独立承包人通常不替你背锅，不可委托义务却会把锅拉回屋主身上；遇到修缮、施工、公共风险，先想这条例外。

reason.en: Shows the injury occurred in a place where the land possessor's activity posed foreseeable harm.
reason.zh: 表明伤害发生在土地占有人活动可预见危及他人的场所。

keywords.text: piece of lumber that fell from the roof

reason.en: A foreseeable harm from roof repairs that triggers the land possessor's safety duty.
reason.zh: 屋顶修缮可预见造成的伤害，触发土地占有人安全义务。

reason.en: Establishes an independent contractor relationship that normally avoids vicarious liability.
reason.zh: 确立通常为独立承包商、一般不免雇主转承责任的关系。

reason.en: Roof repairs are a land-based activity posing foreseeable risks to others.
reason.zh: 屋顶修缮是在土地上进行、对他人有可预见风险的活动。

reason.en: Confirms the contractor breached the duty the homeowner could not delegate away.

reason.zh: 在题干已明确承包商过失时提供证据捷径的干扰项。

highlights.text: The homeowner had hired a roofer to make repairs to his roof

reason.en: Sets up the independent contractor relationship and the dangerous land activity at issue.
reason.zh: 确立独立承包商关系及有危险的土地修缮活动。

highlights.text: the lumber fell through negligence on the roofer's part

reason.en: Direct evidence of negligence makes res ipsa inapplicable and supplies the breach element.
reason.zh: 直接过失证据使事实自证不适用，并提供违反要素。

highlights.text: struck by a piece of lumber that fell from the roof

reason.en: Shows harm foreseeable from roof repairs, supporting a nondelegable safety duty.
reason.zh: 表明屋顶修缮可预见造成损害，支持不可转委安全义务。

highlights.text: brings an action against the homeowner

reason.en: Frames whether the pedestrian can recover from the homeowner rather than the roofer.
reason.zh: 界定行人能否向房主而非承包商求偿。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
While a businesswoman was leaving an elevator, it suddenly dropped several inches, causing her to fall. An investigation of the accident revealed that the elevator dropped because it had been negligently maintained by an elevator company. The elevator company had a contract with the owner of the building to inspect and maintain the elevator. The businesswoman's fall severely aggravated a preexisting physical disability.
If the businesswoman sues the elevator company for damages for her injuries, what should she recover?

choices.A: Damages for the full amount of her disability, because a tortfeasor must take its victim as it finds her.
choices.B: Damages for the injury caused by the falling elevator, including the aggravation of her preexisting disability.
choices.C: Nothing, if the accident would not have caused significant harm to an ordinarily prudent elevator passenger.
choices.D: Nothing, if the elevator company could not reasonably have been expected to foresee the extent of the harm that the businesswoman suffered as a result of the accident.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Relevance of foreseeability for negligence
DutyDefendant's duty only extends to foreseeable risks of his/her conduct
BreachDefendant fails to act like reasonable person under similar circumstances by not mitigating foreseeable risks
Causation
  • Actual (but for) cause - foreseeability irrelevant
  • Proximate cause - plaintiff's harm must have been foreseeable consequence of defendant's breach
DamagesForeseeability irrelevant (ie, eggshell-skull rule)

To recovery under a theory of negligence, the plaintiff must prove duty, breach, causation, and damages.

Under the eggshell-skull rule, damages are available for all of the harm stemming from the defendant's negligence. This is true even if the extent of that harm was unforeseeable and unusually severe-eg, due to the plaintiff's preexisting vulnerability or medical condition.

Here, the elevator company's negligent maintenance caused the elevator to suddenly drop several inches while the businesswoman was leaving it. Since this caused the businesswoman to fall, she can recover damages for her injury, including the aggravation of her preexisting disability. This is true even if the elevator company could not have reasonably foreseen the extent of the businesswoman's harm (Choice D).

(Choice A) Under the eggshell-skull rule, a tortfeasor "takes its victim as it finds her." This means that the elevator company must pay for the full extent of the businesswoman's injuries caused by its negligence (eg, the aggravation of her disability). But it need not pay for any injury that was not caused by its negligence (eg, her loss of ability).

(Choice C) The extent and severity of the plaintiff's harm never has to be foreseeable, so the fact that the accident would not have caused an ordinary elevator passenger significant harm is irrelevant.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the eggshell-skull rule, a tortfeasor is liable for all of the harm resulting from his/her tortious conduct —even if the extent of that harm was unforeseeable and unusually severe (eg, due to the victim's preexisting vulnerability).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 435 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (explaining that a tortfeasor can be liable for harm that he/she neither foresaw nor should have foreseen).
questions.zh-question:
一名女商人正要离开电梯时，电梯突然下降了数英寸，导致她摔倒。事故调查显示，电梯下降的原因是一家电梯公司过失维护所致。该电梯公司与大楼业主签订了检查和维护电梯的合同。女商人的摔倒严重加剧了她原有的身体残疾。

如果女商人就其所受伤害向电梯公司提起诉讼要求损害赔偿，她应获得什么赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 对其残疾的全额损害赔偿，因为侵权行为人必须按其受害者的实际情况承担责任。
zh-choices.B: 对因电梯坠落造成的伤害的损害赔偿，包括对其既有残疾的加重部分。
zh-choices.C: 不予赔偿，如果该事故不会对一个普通谨慎的电梯乘客造成重大伤害。
zh-choices.D: 不予赔偿，如果电梯公司无法合理预见到女商人因该事故所受伤害的程度。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Negligence - Damages

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失（negligence）里，蛋壳头骨规则（eggshell-skull rule）是否让被告为原告的预存伤情加重后果负责。

三秒认题路径：

看到跌落致伤 → 先找过失 → 再看损害 → 预存病情加重 → 仍可赔

核心法律规则

这题只抓这一条

损害（damages）看的是被告行为造成了什么后果，不要求这些后果都能预见。蛋壳头骨规则（eggshell-skull rule）的考试意思：被告要承担自己过失造成的全部伤害，哪怕原告本来就有脆弱体质，结果比常人更重。

所以这题里，电梯突然下坠把她摔倒，随后把既有残疾加重了，这部分也算她能拿到的赔偿。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Torts § 435 — 说明加重后的损害即使不可预见，仍可由过失方承担。

思维导图

过失导致电梯突然下坠？
是先确认：损害（damages）已经由被告过失引发。
下一步看原告是否有预存脆弱性（preexisting vulnerability）。
关键卡点不用卡死“加重程度是否可预见”，这一步对损害赔偿不重要。
结论被告赔下坠致伤 + 加重残疾，答案落在 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然她伤得比普通乘客更重，那被告是不是只赔“可预见的普通伤害”？

但考试真正问的是：损害（damages）阶段不看伤得重不重能不能预见，只看这次过失有没有把她摔伤、并把原有残疾加重。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 电梯下坠并摔倒 直接造成伤害，蛋壳头骨规则（eggshell-skull rule）让她连预存残疾被加重的部分也能赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 责任范围误判

✕ A: 把“全额”理解成无因果限制，take its victim as it finds her 不是让她拿与事故无关的损失。

❌ 法律适用 | 预见性套错

✕ C: 把“普通乘客会不会重伤”当成损害门槛，ordinarily prudent 不是这里的判断点。

❌ 事实误判 | 可预见性偷换

✕ D: 以为“结果太重”就不能赔，reasonably have been expected 只管可预见性，不管蛋壳头骨规则。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定损害阶段，再用蛋壳头骨规则把“不可预见的加重”直接排除出争点。

考场速记

记住一句：被告只要造成了伤害，就要为伤害结果负责；结果更重，不是免责理由。

考场速记：eggshell skull = “人脆弱也照赔”；别把“不可预见”错塞进 损害（damages）。
